title: Branch Art Exhibit: Works by Shipra Vyas
location: Albion, Auditorium
description:
Throughout the month of September, the works of artist Shipra Vyas are on display at Albion branch.
Shipra Vyas is a Toronto-based artist whose work explores memory, place, and the everyday moments that shape identity. Working primarily in pencil and pastel, she builds layered, textured drawings that carry a reflective atmospheric quality. Her practice is informed by family life, travel, her Indo Canadian roots, and literary influences, drawing on these to create intimate studies of connection, transition, and belonging. Her work can also be found on Instagram at @littlesketchdiary.
"This series of drawings is inspired by Caitlin Vernon’s debut poetry collection Hold On Until I Can Love You. Beginning with the book cover & illustrations, the project grew into a larger body of work exploring themes of early relationships, identity, and place. Created with pencil and pastel, the pieces draw on Glasgow and Toronto, using soft textures and layered greens to evoke a hazy, memory-like atmosphere that reflects and extends the poetry, while also inviting viewers into a shared space."
This exhibit is part of TPL's
Art Exhibit Space
program. Toronto Public Library provides space for local artists to exhibit their work at locations across the city. These exhibits aim to reflect the diverse cultural interests of the city and its neighbourhoods.
The exhibit can be viewed during Albion branch's open hours. Please check the
Albion branch
page before you visit.
Free. All are welcome.
Photo credit: Shipra Vyas,
Thoughts, Pencil and Soft Pastel, Medium.

title: Survivalist Series: Introduction to Camp Skills
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/intro-bushcraft)**

**Behold the profound utility of plants!**

Long before rope, tools, and construction materials came off a shelf, it came from the land: twisted from roots, stripped from bark, and spun from plant fiber.

This one-day workshop introduces you to the concepts of bushcraft, how to source raw materials straight from the wild and how to make them into things you need to survive. You'll learn to see the forest differently and walk away with the skills (and a few finished pieces) to prove it.

**You will learn:**

* How to identify and ethically harvest plants
* How to process these materials to create survival essentials
* Basic structures and tools that can be easily built, to improve wilderness convenience and quality of life.
* How to apply bushcraft concepts to meal preparation and cooking.
* The principles of sustainable bushcraft: what to take, what to leave, and how to harvest without depleting the source

**Who It's For**: Anyone looking to build on their outdoor skills with hands-on, practical craft. No prior experience required, though this pairs well with our Foraging workshop for those looking to round out their plant knowledge.

**About this Series**: The Survivalist Series is an expert-led set of courses designed to develop applicable and life-saving skills in the outdoors. Keep your eyes peeled for more courses on many other topics as they become available.

**Highlights**
**Plant Fiber Cordage:** Twist raw fiber into cordage strong enough to lash a shelter frame or hang a pack. And you will be able to bring some home!
**Ethical Harvesting:** Learn to read a plant before you touch it, and how much you can take without setting the population back.
**Expert Instruction:** Your amazing expert guide will teach you everything you need to know in a safe and approachable way.

**Event cost: $80+HST (for explorer members) - $30 optional transport available.**
**Register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/intro-bushcraft)**

**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.

Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.

Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!

***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

title: North Humber River Long Walk  - 16KM (You might see a deer!)
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
### 🌿 North Humber River Walk – 6th Annual! 🌿

We’re back for our **sixth year in a row** with this incredible walk — and it has become a true fan favourite!
The North Humber River trail is one of Toronto’s most peaceful and nature-filled walks. It’s a longer walk, but that’s part of what makes it so rewarding.

You’ll get out of the city, follow the river, explore beautiful natural areas, and see just how far you can go when you give yourself the chance.

This walk is about challenging yourself just a little — you'd be surprised how far you can go!
If you don't want to complete the entire walk, that's totally okay. You can leave along the way, and I can help you find the nearest way back toward public transit.
We'll finish with a quick stop at Tim Hortons before heading back toward Kipling Station.

### 📲 Stay Connected

Don't forget to join our **WhatsApp Group – [CLICK HERE!](https://chat.whatsapp.com/H59mSCbsAi018gYANrKAnc)**
It's a great way to get updates, connect with other members, and stay informed about the event.

📍 **Meetup Spot:** In front of the Information Booth at Kipling Subway Station Bus Terminal
🫎 Look for Mathew in the Moose Hat!

⏰ **Meeting Time:** Approximately **10:35 AM**

Please look up directions to Humberline Park before leaving and give yourself plenty of time to get there.
🚗 **Parking:** Parking availability in the area can vary, so please check the parking situation before coming.

⚠️ **Important:** If you drive to Humberline Park, **you will need to arrange your own transportation back at the end of the walk.**

We do not finish the walk back at Humberline Park. You may need to use Uber, a taxi, or public transit to get back to your vehicle.
If you're meeting us at the park, please make sure you are there and ready to walk by 10:35 AM. Once we arrive, we'll be continuing with the group.

***

### 💵 Meetup Fee

**$5 cash in person or e-transfer**
📧 **[mathewmaclean@hotmail.com](mailto:mathewmaclean@hotmail.com)**

This small fee helps support the group and keeps events like this running. Thank you for supporting the community!

***

### 🌲 What to Expect

🚍 A 40-minute bus ride to the starting point near Humber College
🌿 A peaceful walk along the North Humber River
🦌 Opportunities to spot deer, birds, and other wildlife
☕ Two rest stops along the route
🥾 A longer walk that will give you a chance to challenge yourself
🍩 A final stop at Tim Hortons before heading back toward Kipling Station

Some sections of this trail genuinely feel like you've left Toronto behind. It's one of those walks where the city slowly disappears and you're surrounded by trees, water, wildlife, and open space.

***

### 🧳 What to Bring

💧 Water
👟 Good walking shoes — some sections may be uneven
🥨 A snack
🧴 Sunscreen
🎒 A small backpack

***

### 👥 Who Is This For?

This group is for anyone who wants to get outside, explore Toronto, and meet people along the way — singles, couples, newcomers, longtime Torontonians, and everyone in between.

We host:
🎬 Movies
🚶 Walks & hikes
🎭 Arts & culture
🍽️ Restaurants
🎤 Karaoke
…and plenty more!

The activity is the **container**. The people you meet and the connections you make along the way are the real experience. 💛

***

### 💛 A Few Notes

You're welcome to join us even if you're deciding at the last minute.
If you need to leave the walk early, that's okay — just let me know and we'll help you figure out the best way to get back toward transit.
Sometimes things happen and events may need to be cancelled or changed. Please keep an eye on the event page for updates.

title: Landmarks 4: The British Coffee House to Victoria Square (NEW)
description:
Toronto History Walks
**The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!**

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

In this new volume, Landmarks 4 revisits the site of some of Toronto's urban legends, and historic buildings that gave rise to the city. This walk's focus is on the King Street West, Portland Street and lower Bathurst Street area

From there we wander around the area taking in landmarks not otherwise explored on other Toronto History Walks tours. So get your brains and feet ready for a workout my friends.

The British coffee house at the corner of King Street West and York Street in the old Chewett building dates from the 1830s. However, after the demise of the coffee house it became one of Toronto's best hotels the Rossin House.

There is also a connection to one of Toronto's best known characters, John Howard of High Park fame and the provincial Lunatic Asylum. It was in this building that John Howard lived until his country home out in High Park was completed.

Victoria Square is a little known gem in the heart of Toronto, and some of our earliest history begins there. So this tour returns walkers to the time period between 1812 and 1880 and everything in between.

Toronto is a city that hides its history in plain sight. Beneath the glass towers are layers of stories — grand hotels that vanished overnight, political scandals whispered through stone corridors, theatres that once glittered under gaslight, and laneways where the city first learned how to become a metropolis.

This new Toronto History Walks series of 60 different walking tours invites the walker to slow down, and see the city differently.

Over the course of 30 carefully chosen stops, this walking tour traces the landmarks that helped shape the history of Toronto. Beginning at the site of the legendary Holland House — once one of the city’s finest mansions, and a gathering place for politicians, and businessmen, the routes wind through the city uncovering stories both famous and forgotten.

Some locations are grand and imposing. Others are easy to walk past without a second glance. Every stop reveals a piece of Toronto’s personality. At Osgoode Hall, visitors will stand before one of the city’s most elegant historic buildings. Nearby, the old banks and newspaper buildings of the financial district recall an era when Toronto proudly called itself “Toronto the Good,” even as corruption and backroom dealings simmered beneath the surface.

The tour also explores the vanished city — the Toronto that survives only in photographs, and memory. Walkers will discover where magnificent Victorian structures once stood before demolition crews erased entire blocks in the name of progress. Former theatres, hotels, markets, and department stores emerge again through storytelling, helping modern explorers imagine the bustle, smoke, and noise of earlier generations.

Stories of fire, disaster, celebration, and reinvention. Participants will hear how the Great Fire of 1904 transformed downtown streets, how immigrant communities reshaped neighbourhoods block by block, and how Toronto repeatedly reinvented itself through booms, depressions, wars, and waves of newcomers.

But this tour is not simply about dates and buildings. It is about people. The politicians who argued over Confederation. The hotel clerks who witnessed scandals. The newspaper editors who shaped public opinion. The shopkeepers, labourers, entertainers, and ordinary Torontonians whose lives unfolded along these same streets.

Toronto has always had hidden corners and strange tales: tunnels beneath streets, forgotten cemeteries beneath office towers, unsolved crimes, and buildings said to carry echoes of the past. Even longtime residents may find themselves surprised by what has been quietly standing before them all along. Come along and experience a very different city. A deep dive into our history.

This walking tour begins at the southeast **corner** of King Street West and York Street, just ignore the entire 11th floor that's a flaw in the directions app within Meetup, I will be on the ground floor, trust me! We end our tour at Victoria Square near Portland and Wellington Street.

This walking tour is for all walking levels. Please dress for the season, and hope to see you there.

This tour has a ticket price of $15.00 per person.

location: Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Presented in conjunction with Game On! and programmed by film scholar, author, critic, and curator Narendra Pachkhédé, this screening of Satyajit Ray’s Shatranj Ke Khilari ( The Chess Players ) explores chess as a cultural form and a lens on power, strategy, and political inaction.

A brief introduction by Pachkédé will connect the film to three works in the exhibition. A 12th-century Iranian chess set, the Shahnameh folio “Buzurjmihr Masters the Indian Game of Chess,” and Yoko Ono’s Play It By Trust . Together, they trace chess from its material and courtly histories to its modern role as a space of cooperation.

The screening will be followed by a conversation between Bita Pourvash, curator of Game On! , and Narendra Pachkhédé, film scholar, author, critic, and curator, exploring what games reveal about conflict, responsibility, and historical change.

title: Canadian Premiere Anchorball After Dark, Royal Botanical Gardens (Burlington)
description:
Experience Toronto
On **Saturday September 5th,** **join us for the Canadian Premiere of Anchorball at The Royal Botanical Gardens (RBG) After Dark Event in Burlington.**
RBG After Dark transforms ANCHORBALL: A Curious Art Journey into a vibrant evening experience for adults. Explore the gardens after hours surrounded by 18 large-scale pop art sculptures, illuminated pathways, live entertainment, food, drinks, and interactive experiences throughout the night. We will have the pleasure of walking through these beautiful gardens (the number one spot for wedding photos) and seeing the Canadian Premiere of Anchorball. This way we see the Gardens in daylight, and also lit up at night. **Purchase your ticket for RBG After Dark Anchorball on Saturday September 5th.**

Explore the vibrant sculptural universe of artist and contemporary sculptor Ken Kelleher, internationally known as Anchorball. This massive outdoor exhibition transforms the garden into a vivid sculptural landscape where bold characters, imaginative narratives, and contemporary form merge with nature and blooms to create a world that feels full of wonder, yet deeply recognizable.

Featuring 18 monumental sculptures ranging up to 12 feet tall, the exhibition introduces visitors to an evolving fictional universe, known as Low Orbit City, populated by playful and mythical characters. In addition to the physical installations, visitors can discover a hidden digital world using augmented reality with characters known as Cloudwalkers and unlock an AR Masterpiece, extending the experience beyond the visible landscape and inviting moments of surprise, play, and exploration throughout the garden.

There will also be an acrylic paint workshop at 7 and 8pm for 30mins.

title: Forks of the Credit Summertime Trek
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/fforks-of-the-credit)**

**Ten kilometers, one river, and about 300 metres of elevation gain packed into a single Caledon loop.**

We start near Kettle Lake, a small glacial pond that gives this section of the park its name, and follow the Meadow Trail as it dips down toward the water before climbing back out through mixed forest. From there we pick up the Bruce Trail along an open ridge, where the ground flattens out and the Credit River valley opens up below.

The second half of the loop is where the park earns its name. We drop down toward the ruins of a former hydro power station, its concrete foundations still standing next to the river, before a short detour to the viewing platform for Cataract Falls. It is not a thundering waterfall, but the setting, tucked into the escarpment with the old ruins for company, is worth the stop.

The final stretch follows the river home, easy and flat, the escarpment behind you and the Credit River keeping you company the rest of the way.

**Highlights**
**Kettle Lake:** A glacial pond formed over 10,000 years ago, ringed by the lumpy, uneven ground left behind by melting ice.
**Cataract Falls and the Ruins:** A quiet waterfall next to the crumbling remains of a 19th century power station.
**Escarpment Ridge Views:** An open stretch of the Bruce Trail with sightlines down into the Credit River valley.

**Event cost: $50+HST (for explorer members) - $40 optional transport available.**
**Register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/fforks-of-the-credit)**

**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.

Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.

Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!

Mount Nemo tends to be a favourite park for nature enthusiasts, thanks to the unique escarpment-edge ecosystem and the incredible biodiversity that thrives at the park. Bring your magnifying glass, binoculars, and camera, and take any of the trails at Mount Nemo for incredible views, turkey vultures flying overhead, and more rare species of plants, animals and insects than you can count. If you’re vertically inclined, you can get face-to-face with the escarpment on one of the many climbing routes. And if you prefer to keep your feet on the ground, there is still an abundance of cliffs, crags and caves waiting to be explored.
Bring lots of water, lunch and appropriate clothing - long pants and sleeves as the days are a little cooler and it is still tick season.

title: English Spanish Language Conversation
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Friday
* Saturday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** here **»** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
**Héctor Fuentes**

title: Salsa Dura with Montreal Guests MARZOS & MATEO
location: Division 88,225 Geary Ave, Toronto, ON M6H 2C1, Canada
description:
Join us for our last edition of BEDA · Put Trouble On My Tab!

BEDA series is dedicated to the people who keep the city’s cultural and hospitality scene alive: musicians, restaurant workers, and tourism professionals who rarely get to experience the events they help make possible. This five-month series offers a late performance on Sundays, so those who work weekends can finally enjoy world-class live music. The project also builds a cultural bridge between Toronto and Montreal, inviting exceptional artists from across provinces to share the stage and strengthen connections within Canada’s music ecosystem

MARZOS & MATEO, winners of the 18th edition of the Syli d'Or World Music Competition and recipients of the Afropop Worldwide Award 2025, present a concert rooted in their Latin American origins and Afro-Caribbean heritage, combining original compositions with salsa classics.

MARZOS, a modern salsa dura ensemble from Montreal, brings together the power of a large-format orchestra with a contemporary approach to Afro-Caribbean traditions. Known for its precision, musical direction and energetic performances, the ensemble develops an original sound rooted in the diverse musical heritage of the Latin American diaspora.

MATEO, a Colombian singer-songwriter, performer and guitarist, brings his own contemporary perspective to Latin music, blending Afrobeat, alternative rock, electro and Afro-Colombian sounds.

A summer-long escape is unfolding at Toronto’s most iconic castle. From June 8th to September 7, Casa Loma https://casaloma.ca/ invites guests to experience its 10th annual Summer Series, featuring a rotating lineup of live music nights throughout its gardens and historic grounds.

Each weeknight brings a different musical experience beneath the stars:

  * Mondays: Symphony in the Gardens - an elegant evening of orchestral performances set against the castle’s illuminated terraces.
  * Tuesdays: Rock Symphony - blending classical instrumentation with iconic rock anthems for a powerful crossover experience.
  * Wednesdays: Tribute Shows - celebrating legendary artists through live performances that bring familiar hits to life in a uniquely atmospheric setting.

In addition to the music, guests are invited to explore the grounds and enjoy the food and beverage offerings throughout the evening as the castle transforms into an open-air concert destination.

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

description:
Woodworking Level 2 at TTLMakerspace

 
 
 Note: This course requires previous completion of Intro to Woodworking

 In this course at TTLMakerspace, you will use and expand upon the skills learned in Intro Woodworking. Working in a small group with dedicated instructor, you'll expand your skills in two practical box-building projects designed to develop deeper understanding of woodworking.

 In this followup to Woodworking Intro students advance their skills into more sophisticated use of both power tools and hand tools. During the course two projects are created that reveal techniques for creating mitred joints, splines, inlays, lap joints, and finishing techniques.

 Build up confidence in the shop and learn new, valuable woodworking techniques.

 
 Materials and equipment for all projects are provided with the course. 

 Schedule : 

 Six three-hour weekly classes, Tuesdays 10am to 1pm. 

 Outcomes : 

 At the end of this course you will have achieved the following goals: 

 
- Become more comfortable milling rough lumber 

- Complete mitered corners 

- Complete box joints 

- Use a spline jig 

- Complete inlays 

- Install hinges 

- Apply finishes 

- Learn how to plan projects efficiently with minimal waste 

 
 Following this course, you'll be certified to use the woodshop. And you'll be able to join the growing community of TTL Makers sharing knowledge on our Discord community.

Useful for: furniture, cabinets, organisers, cutting-boards

About Lil Taggart
Lil Taggart is an experienced and creative designer and instructor in Floral Arts. She is also an accredited Floral Design Judge and has competed on an international level as well as domestically. She serves on the board of Canada Blooms, co-chairs the staging for the Toronto Flower Show, is past president of the Georgetown Horticultural society and is a member of The Garden Club of Toronto.

title: Google Prompting Essentials: Online Learning Circle
description:
Ready to develop the skills to use generative AI (GenAI) tools effectively and responsibly for work and daily life? Join our staff-facilitated Learning Circle to complete the self-paced Google Prompting specialization. By completing this Learning Circle program, you will earn a Google Prompting Essentials certificate to share on your resume, LinkedIn and social media profiles!
What You'll Learn
This program is designed for those with some experience with using GenAI. Through short videos, articles, assignments and quizzes, you will discover:
Essential
Prompting Skills
: How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results.
Everyday Work Tasks:
Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more.
Data & Presentations:
How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data.
Advanced Techniques:
How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time.
Learning Circles are study groups guided by
library staff for people who want to complete the Google Prompting specialization together in a welcoming space:
Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials.
Participants are expected to commit to attending all four Learning Circle sessions.
Some Experience with GenAI Recommended: This course is ideal for participants who have completed the AI Essentials course Learning Circle.

title: 2026 CBC Massey Lecture:  Housing Inc.
description:
TORONTO ARTS & CULTURE
Since 1965, [CBC IDEAS](http://cbc.ca/ideas) has broadcast the Massey Lectures, exploring the ideas that make us who we are.

We attend the Massey Lecture every year.

**Housing is not a luxury. It is a requirement for human existence.**

In the 2026 CBC Massey Lectures, **Leilani Farha**, *global director of The Shift and former UN special rapporteur on the Right to Housing*, reckons with a crisis engineered by governments and perfected by financial firms.

In her first Massey Lecture, “Home,” she explores how our homes shape our sense of dignity, identity, and security. Because home is so fundamental to our lives, she argues, our housing system is inextricably linked to the question of who lives, who dies, and who counts.

title: Civic Meetup #559: Creeped Out: Privacy and Discrimination Risks of Health-related Machine Listening
location: Online: https://link.civictech.ca/zoom / Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario
description:
New technologies and organizations’ practices are regularly placing pressures and challenges on our privacy and transparency rights. This month, Civic Tech Toronto and the Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario are highlighting the work to defend, enforce, explain and update these rights. To see all September events, check our events listing on Guild. 

‎‎

Topic: Creeped Out: Privacy and Discrimination Risks of Health-related Machine Listening

Typical arguments about creepy technology focus on the visceral ‘ick’ factor of innovation. In contrast, this talk shares a methodology to track patterns of function creep and empirically assess changing privacy and discrimination risks. The research focuses on the product development and deployment of health-related machine listening: apps and devices that combine audio signal processing and machine learning techniques to produce sensitive inferences about people’s health from data points such as vocal biomarkers, coughs, infant cries, and other sounds. Drawing on a 10-year analysis period, the presentation will show the escalating privacy risks that are raised as health-related machine listening expands into new settings and targets ever-more data subjects.

Project Website: https://www.infoscapelab.ca/projects/losingyourvoice

‎‎

Speaker: Stephen J. Neville \[in-person]

Stephen J. Neville is a media and surveillance scholar based in Guelph, Ontario. Currently, he is a Fellow at the Infoscape Research Lab at Toronto Metropolitan University. He was the principal investigator for “Losing your voice to AI”, funded by the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada (2025-2026), which mapped the emerging industry of health-related machine listening to address problems of data privacy, consent, and transparency. With Greg Elmer, he is the coauthor of The Politics of Media Scarcity (Routledge 2024) which foregrounds marginalized histories and storytelling as a challenge to dominant narratives of abundance and digital divides in media studies. // Bluesky

‎

Agenda:

7:00-7:20 Welcome and Introductions

7:20-7:50 Presentation and Q\&A/discussion

7:50-9:00 Breakout groups

Our weekly civic meetups bring together Torontonians (designers, coders, urban planners, government staff, mappers, policy-makers, students, communications strategists, community organizers, and more) who share an interest in making Toronto more responsive, prosperous, sustainable, and equitable through design, tech, and data.

location: Tranzac,292 Brunswick Ave, Toronto, ON M5S 2M7, Canada
description:
Dear Toronto friends!

This will be the last performance in the Septet IV/IX Toronto series.

We are excited to present the final part of Ehsan Sadigh’s Septet IV/IX — Comprovisation (Composition + Improvisation) by Rondo Projects. Join us as a quartet!

Featuring:

Bea Labikova — baritone & alto saxophones

Chris Pruden — keys / synth bass

Dhaivat Jani — drums

Ehsan Sadigh — guitar


Tuesday, September 8th

9:00 PM

The Tranzac Club (Southern Cross)

PWYC (Pay What You Can)


For more details, check out the Tranzac Club website. Hope to see you there!


———


The idea behind Septet IV/IX was originally conceived by Ehsan Sadigh for a chamber ensemble and was planned to be performed in Tehran, with a flexible lineup of 7 to 12 musicians. Although geopolitical conflicts have temporarily put those plans on hold, the project has now taken shape in Toronto as a dynamic four-stage series, in which both the composition and the number of performers change and develop from one stage to the next, moving through duo, trio, and quartet configurations.


Featuring musicians from Toronto and Montreal, this initiative is a core part of Ehsan Sadigh’s Rondo Projects. The Toronto series began in a trio format, and this final performance features Bea Labikova, Dhaivat Jani, and Chris Pruden alongside Ehsan Sadigh.

Septet IV/IX is planned to be performed in Tehran in late 2026 or early 2027, in the Rondo Projects format, featuring leading local musicians.

title: Sept 9 - Physical AI Has a Data Problem. It Isn't Collection Workshop
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
This workshop goes from raw recording to curated corpus. We'll cover what MCAP is and why it's built that way, tour real Physical AI datasets across driving, aquatic, and forest robots, and open an episode with every sensor synced—including channels nothing knows how to decode.

**Time, Date and Location**

Sep 09, 2026
9:00 AM - 10:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/document-visual-ai-workshop-september-9-2026)**

Physical AI still relies on familiar computer vision tasks—detection, segmentation, depth, tracking. What's changed is the data unit: no longer a single image and label, but an episode—a dozen sensors ticking on independent clocks for minutes, with no frame boundaries.

Most computer vision tooling assumes the old unit and breaks on the new one.

That's why Physical AI teams end up with buckets of .mcap files nobody can characterize. Recording is cheap, so logs pile up faster than anyone curates them. Ask what's actually in there—which tasks, which conditions, how many failures and of what kind—and the honest answer is usually a shrug.
MCAP has been ROS 2's default log format since Iron, and as of [FiftyOne 1.19](https://docs.voxel51.com/index.html) it opens natively: cameras, LiDAR, GPS, IMU, and logs on one shared timeline, alongside your images and video.

We'll tackle quality, the harder half: what smoothness, sensor-health, and outlier metrics actually measure, where each falls short, and how to turn a score into a defensible decision.

You'll leave knowing how to load your own recordings, query a whole corpus instead of a single file, and which quality signals to trust for which job.

title: The Quote-to-Cash Blind Spot: Secret Scanning for Enterprise Revenue Systems
description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto
Every CPQ, CLM, and billing rollout I've run wires Salesforce or Vlocity to DocuSign, Stripe or Zuora-type billing, and ERP through API keys and OAuth tokens sitting in DataRaptors, Integration Procedures, and deployment scripts. AppSec teams usually classify that layer as "business configuration," so it never gets scanned the way application code does.

Where credentials actually live in a quote-to-cash stack: middleware scripts, integration procedures, CI/CD for CPQ deployments. Why "business systems" teams don't think of themselves as a scanning target, and what that costs. How GitHub Advanced Security's secret scanning, push protection, and custom patterns close the gap, even for teams that don't see themselves as developers.

A sample repo modeling a CPQ integration script with a hardcoded OAuth token and API key. Push protection blocking a commit in real time. A custom regex pattern built for an enterprise revenue-tool token format. The alert triage view a security lead would actually work from.

ABOUT THE EVENT
This is not a book reading.
It’s an intentionally designed experience.
Most book launches are a reading and a Q&A. This one isn’t, mostly because it would make no sense.
The Campfire Method is about designing genuine connection in a group, so I’m going to do that rather than describe it. You’ll walk in, and within a few minutes you find yourself in conversation with a like-minded person. Not through forced fun. Not through a round of two…

title: Hamilton Public Library Lecture: Stonehenge of the Americas
location: Hamilton Public Library – Central Library, 55 York Blvd, Hamilton, Ontario, L8R 3K1, Canada
description:
HPL Lecture Series: Stonehenge of the Americas? The Rise and Fall of Tiwanaku
 
High in the Bolivian Andes, on the shores of Lake Titicaca, lies Tiwanaku — often called the Stonehenge of the Americas. Around the end of the fourth century AD, this remarkable settlement underwent a dramatic transformation, becoming the first city in the highlands of Andean South America. What triggered this sudden explosion of political power, economic innovation and artistic creativity?
 
Drawing on 25 years of archaeological research, this talk explores discoveries that are reshaping our understanding of Tiwanaku’s origins, the environmental and social forces behind its rise and the factors that ultimately led to its decline.

title: Laverne Cox & Jason Stanley: Identity, Power and the Politics of Our Time
location: Toronto Reference Library, Appel Salon, Second Floor
description:
Join actor and activist Laverne Cox and philosopher Jason Stanley for a conversation about the political forces reshaping our world.
As civil rights, historical truth and democratic norms come under pressure in the United States, Canadians are watching closely. What does it look like when a society begins to rewrite its past, narrow who gets to belong and chip away at hard-won freedoms? And what can communities everywhere—including here at home—learn from this moment?
Drawing on Stanley's scholarship on propaganda and historical memory and Cox's powerful voice as an advocate for human dignity and equality, this discussion moves past headlines to explore the bigger questions: how democracies erode, how they're defended and why the stories a nation tells about itself matter so much.
Thoughtful, urgent and ultimately hopeful, this is a conversation for anyone trying to make sense of the times we're living in.
Q&A to follow. Books available for purchase.

title: Nate Hendley: Mounties, Marriage, and Murder

description:
John Wilson emigrated from Scotland to the Prairies in 1912, joined the Royal North-West Mounted Police (RNWMP) and fell in love with a Canadian woman named Jessie. Then, his wife, Mary, whom he had abandoned in Scotland along with his children, unexpectedly showed up in Saskatchewan. Mary soon disappeared and Wilson went from Mountie to murder suspect.
Author and freelance journalist, Nate Hendley, takes a look at a Canadian true-life murder mystery on the Prairies involving a double-crossing police officer, providing a glimpse behind the carefully polished image of the Mounties, to reveal a duplicitous liar who tried to get away with murder.

Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

title: In-Depth Intro to Woodworking Sept 10 [Thursdays - 6 week Intensive]
location: TTLMakerspace, 192 Spadina Ave., Toronto, ON
description:
Woodworking at TTLMakerspace

 
 Suitable for beginners, this woodworking course is designed to teach you all that you need to get started in woodworking by learning both traditional, and modern techniques.

 Students will learn valuable hands-on skills working on instructor-lead projects using both hand and power tools.

 Projects are chosen to provide skills development in a natural progression from familiarity with the unique characteristics of wood, to basic essential techniques, to some more advanced topics.

 Materials and equipment for all projects are provided with the course. 

 

 Schedule : 

 Six three-hour weekly classes, Thursdays 10am to 1pm. 

 Outcomes : 

 At the end of this course you will have achieved the following goals: 

 
- A complete understanding of the nature and properties of wood 

- Proficiency with traditional woodworking techniques

- Comfort working with chisels, planes, saws

- Proficiency with wood milling techniques

- Comfort with safe operation of power tools

- Familiarity with power planing, joiner, drill press, router and table saw 

- Dressing and laminating wood 

- Experience following project plans 

- Familiarity with joinery 

- Wood finishing, various treatments 

 
  Following this course, you'll be certified to use the woodshop. And you'll be able to join the growing community of TTL Makers sharing knowledge on our Discord community.

 Certifications for all courses are valid for one year from the time that they are issued, and can be renewed at no cost with your active monthly membership within 3 months of their expiry. Certification renewal requires booking with an instructor, is conducted at the makerspace, and helps you keep your skills current. 

Useful for: furniture, cabinets, organisers, cutting-boards 
 
 
 
 Want to get notified next time classes are posted? 

 Join our mailing list!

title: Working With Your Data, Safely: Files, Approvals and Memory
description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto
So far the agent can talk about markets but cannot touch anything of yours, and nothing stops it doing something it should not. This episode fixes both. We give it file access so it reads a real portfolio.csv and writes its reports back to disk, then put a place_trade tool behind an explicit human approval.

Approving every single read gets old fast, so we add auto-approval rules for the safe calls and one custom rule that clears small trades on its own. We finish with durable memory in two forms, the files the agent curates itself and the facts Foundry extracts automatically, and watch both survive a restart.

title: The Cartel and Other Cover Stories Book Launch
location: Ben McNally Books
description:
[at Ben McNally Books]
Join us at Ben McNally Books, in partnership with Freehand Books, to celebrate the launch of
The Cartel and Other Cover Stories
by Wayne Grady.
Order a copy of
The Cartel
here.
About the Book
From bestselling novelist Wayne Grady comes the delightful and inventive
The Cartel and Other Cover Stories
, his first collection of short fiction.
Just as cover songs are both tributes to other musicians and original works in themselves, here Grady masterfully reimagines classic short stories in a way that honours the originals while creating something entirely new.

Each story in this collection takes its inspiration from works by international masters of the form, including Anton Chekhov, Franz Kafka, and Lydia Davis, drawing together new contexts and connections.
For instance, in “La Gordita,” inspired by Guy de Maupassant’s “Boule de Suif” about the French bourgeoisie, Grady skewers wealthy expats in Mexico as they make arrangements to leave their winter homes when a drug cartel threatens to seize control of their town.
Bringing together delectably stylish prose, striking characters, a foreword from Margaret Atwood, and “literary liner notes” that bring context to the original stories and the short story form, Wayne Grady’s collection of cover stories is not to be missed!
About the Author
Wayne Grady is the author of more than a dozen works of nonfiction and three novels, including
Emancipation Day
, which won the Amazon First Novel Award and was longlisted for the Giller Prize. Wayne is also an award-winning literary translator, and won the Governor-General’s Award for his translation of Antonine Maillet’s On the Eighth Day. He divides his time between Kingston, Ontario, and San Miguel de Allende, Mexico, with his wife, the novelist and biographer Merilyn Simonds. For more about Wayne and his work, visit waynegrady.ca.

title: AI FinOps: The Next Frontier of DevOps Optimization
description:
Toronto Enterprise DevOps User Group
We spent years optimizing cloud infrastructure, right-sizing VMs, tuning pipelines, and fighting surprise cloud bills. Now a new cost center has entered the chat: AI. Every prompt, every agent interaction, every repository scan, and every generated line of code consumes tokens—and those tokens add up quickly.

AI coding assistants and agents like GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and OpenAI Codex are transforming how teams build software. But scaling AI adoption without understanding consumption patterns is a bit like giving everyone an unlimited cloud subscription and hoping for the best. (We all know how that story ends.)

In this session, we'll explore AI FinOps practices for enterprise engineering teams: how to measure AI consumption, optimize token usage, improve agent workflows, manage context efficiently, choose the right models, and get more value from every AI interaction.

Through practical examples with GitHub Copilot and modern AI coding agents, we'll apply familiar DevOps principles—visibility, optimization, governance, and continuous improvement—to the next generation of software delivery.

*Come at 5:30 pm have some pizza and chat for a bit. The presentation starts at 6:00 pm.*

title: CNC Milling for Builders - Sept 10  [Thursdays - 6 Week Comprehensive]
location: TTLMakerspace, 192 Spadina Ave., Toronto, ON
description:
CNC for Builders 

 
 

 
 In this course at TTLMakerspace, you will go from beginner to a practical working knowledge of CAD modelling and CNC machining with an automated milling machine, specifically for furniture, cabinetry, frames etc. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Starting with desktop versions of CNC machines, you’ll work your way through lessons up to the industrial Omni 1350 6’ x 8’ CNC milling machine. 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Schedule : 
 
 
 Six three-hour weekly classes, Thursdays 6pm to 9pm. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Outcomes : 
 
 
 At the end of this course you will have achieved the following goals: 
 
 
- 
 A complete understanding of the steps needed to go from concept to completed part 

- 
 Familiarity with the properties of a variety of hardwood materials 

- 
 Experience and comprehension of the most important principles of CAD modelling 

- 
 Selecting and programming the most commonly used tools 

- 
 Full understanding of the most common machining operations 

- 
 Experience creating tool paths with CAM software 

- 
 Setting up a CNC mill and performing operations 

- 
 Machine maintenance and Safety 

 
 
 Following this course, you’ll be certified to use desktop mills, and book time with the industrial mill at TTLMakerspace (with your membership). You will also be able to join the growing community of TTL Makers sharing CNC knowledge on our Discord community. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Useful for: furniture, cabinets, flat-pack, desktops, boats, frames

La Bibliothèque publique de Toronto et le
Théâtre français de Toronto
s'associent pour créer un club de lecture théâtre. Ce rendez-vous mensuel est l'occasion de discuter et d'explorer des scènes mythiques ayant marqué le monde du théâtre. Avec
Georges Som
, médiateur culturel, nous essayerons de comprendre les enjeux de ces scènes, de découvrir leurs sens et de partager nos sentiments sur leurs auteurs et autrices. Chacun est le bienvenu au club, qu'il soit néophyte ou amateur de théâtre confirmé. Les seuls prérequis pour participer sont la curiosité et le plaisir d'échanger autour du théâtre !
Au mois de septembre, nous allons discuter un extrait de la pièce
Trois versions de la vie
de Yasmina Reza.
Trois version de la vie
propose trois variantes successives d'une même situation : un couple arrive chez un autre sans y être attendu. L'improvisation donne le ton de la soirée, orchestrée par les deux hommes, astrophysiciens. Brusqués, malmenés, les masques se fissurent : évoluer parmi les matières noires des galaxies ne rend pas forcément habile à vivre le quotidien...

title: Documentary Screening: Nechako: It Will Be a Big River Again
location: Palmerston, Theatre
description:
Nechako
is a crucial documentary that follows two Indigenous Nations fighting for our collective future. When the Kenney Dam was built in the 1950s, the Nechako River was forever changed. The Stellat’en and Saik’uz Nations embarked on a groundbreaking legal proceeding against the Canadian government and Rio Tinto Alcan that lasted over a decade—a battle that continues today. Following community members living day to day on the river while they take on powerful institutions,
Nechako
is an urgent call to action to restore a river and a way of life.
2025. 90 minutes.
This screening is presented in collaboration with the National Film Board of Canada, which is Canada’s only public producer and distributor of Canadian films and series.
Drop-in.

title: Documentary Screening: Siksikakowan: The Blackfoot Man
location: Brentwood, Community Room, Ground Floor.
description:
Siksika filmmaker Sinakson Trevor Solway intimately portrays the lives of Blackfoot men as they navigate identity, kinship and the complex expectations of manhood. Through unfiltered moments and revealing conversations set against the breathtaking landscape of the Prairies, the film reimagines what it means to be a Native man.
Siksikakowan: The Blackfoot Man
is a profound ode to strength, vulnerability and love across generations.
Join us for this documentary screening. Thanks to
The NFB in Libraries
.
Note: this film will be screened with English closed captions.
Drop in, no registration required.

title: Laverne Cox: Transcendent
location: North York Central Library, Concourse Event Space
description:
Four-time Emmy-nominated actress Laverne Cox shares her journey from working as a struggling actress to leading a cultural movement.
Laverne Cox is a powerhouse in the fight for transgender rights and representation—but her path from a struggling trans actress to a cultural movement was anything but easy.
In Transcendent, Laverne invites us into her journey as a transgender woman in Hollywood; confronting childhood trauma, shame and feelings of unworthiness; and, ultimately, healing.
Laverne Cox speaks with author and activist Kai Cheng Thom about making history for her role in Orange is the New Black, her fearless advocacy for LGBTQ+ rights and finding her voice in a world that can too often feel lonely and unaccepting.
Q&A to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this event’s guests:

title: Canoe Camping in Killarney
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/killarney-camping-1)**

**Dive into the Killarney backcountry with this beautiful and beginner friendly canoe camping adventure.**

We're heading to Bell Lake, on the quieter east side of the park, for a weekend that mixes an easy paddle-in camping trip and an incredible hike to Silver Peak, the highest point in Killarney.

Friday, we'll paddle the short 2.5km crossing to our backcountry site, set up camp, and spend the afternoon settling in. The rest of the afternoon is yours to spend how you like. If you want to learn to pitch a tent, get a fire going properly, or handle a canoe, we'll show you. If you'd rather find a rock in the sun and do nothing, that works too.

Saturday, you can chill around camp or paddle over and hike Silver Peak, the highest point in the park. It's a roughly 11km round trip, starting on an easy rolling trail before a steep, hands on scramble up exposed quartzite for the final push. At the top, you're rewarded with a 360 degree view over Killarney's white ridges and out to Georgian Bay. Trust us, you won’t get many views in Ontario that are better than this!

Both nights, we'll eat around the fire and fall asleep under some of the clearest skies in Ontario. Killarney's stargazing is genuinely other-worldly. On a clear night you'll see the Milky Way and more stars than you knew existed. Sunday, we pack up and paddle back out.

By Sunday, you'll have spent two days swimming, paddling, and sleeping under the stars, surrounded by Killarney's unmistakable landscapes.

What's included

* Professional & certified guides
* ‍All camp meals, cooking equipment and mess kits
* ‍Tents
* Canoe rentals

Sleeping bags and sleep pads can be rented from WU for a small fee.

**Highlights**
**Silver Peak Summit:** The highest point in Killarney, with sweeping views over the range and out to Georgian Bay
**Stargazing:** With some of the darkest skies in Ontario, the Milky Way is in full view on a clear night
**Lake Swimming:** Cool off in clear water, or take the canoe out for a closer look at the shoreline

**Event cost: $455+HST (for explorer members) - $70 optional transport available.**
**Register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/killarney-camping-1)**

**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.

Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.

Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!

***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

title: Ireland Park, Queen's Wharf, and 1847 Irish Potato Famine
description:
Toronto History Walks
\*\***The Toronto History Walks Explorer Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!\*\***

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

This special historical walking tour discusses the Irish Potato Famine in great detail, and the implications for Toronto in 1847.

Starting the walking tour near Ireland Park just east of Bathurst Quay we take a deep dive into the events that saw thousands of people head west to Toronto in 1847! A truly global event! A life changing event for those caught up in the famine in Ireland and Toronto itself. Toronto was never the same after, and impacted the future of the city for nearly a century.

But the stories surrounding Ireland Park are not the only stories from this era. This tour looks at the Potato Famine with a different lens. We end at the corner of King and John streets at the site of the Fever Sheds.

This extensive tour begins in **Little Norway Park** adjacent to Queen's Quay West, at the foot of Bathurst Street, and ends at King Street and John Street!

This tour is for all walking levels. Please dress for the season.

This walk has a ticket price of $15.00 per person!

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

title: Google Prompting Essentials: Online Learning Circle
description:
Ready to develop the skills to use generative AI (GenAI) tools effectively and responsibly for work and daily life? Join our staff-facilitated Learning Circle to complete the self-paced Google Prompting specialization. By completing this Learning Circle program, you will earn a Google Prompting Essentials certificate to share on your resume, LinkedIn and social media profiles!
What You'll Learn
This program is designed for those with some experience with using GenAI. Through short videos, articles, assignments and quizzes, you will discover:
Essential
Prompting Skills
: How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results.
Everyday Work Tasks:
Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more.
Data & Presentations:
How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data.
Advanced Techniques:
How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time.
Learning Circles are study groups guided by
library staff for people who want to complete the Google Prompting specialization together in a welcoming space:
Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials.
Participants are expected to commit to attending all four Learning Circle sessions.
Some Experience with GenAI Recommended: This course is ideal for participants who have completed the AI Essentials course Learning Circle.

Some Like It Hot
ascends to inspired heights of silliness in-between, with Tony Curtis and Jack Lemmon both on career-best form as dragged-up musicians hiding out with Sugar Kane’s girl band.
Both the gangster story and the screwball antics hark back to Hollywood films of the 1930s, but Wilder’s outrageous and subversive play with gender was truly boundary pushing and helped lead to a loosening of censorship after United Artists released the film without certification.” – British Film Institute

description:

title: Fabric IQ y Ontología MCP: la capa semántica que entiende tu negocio
description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto
La sesión final lleva la serie al nivel más avanzado: la semántica empresarial como fundamento de todos los agentes.

Fabric IQ (GA desde Build 2026) es la capa de contexto compartido que unifica Data Agents, modelos semánticos y Ontologías sobre OneLake.

Aprenderás qué es una Ontología en Fabric, cómo define entidades, relaciones, propiedades y reglas de negocio vinculadas a datos en vivo, y cómo exponerla como servidor MCP para que cualquier agente externo — Claude, Copilot, agentes de Foundry — pueda fundamentar su razonamiento en ella sin reescribir integraciones.

Construiremos un flujo multi-agente completo donde el orquestador consulta la Ontología vía MCP para entender el negocio, delega al Data Agent para los datos, y entrega respuestas consistentes y gobernadas.

Cerraremos con una hoja de ruta práctica: qué está GA, qué está en Preview, y cómo planificar la adopción en tu organización hoy mismo. Los últimos 15 minutos serán Q&A abierto.

Trae tu caso de uso real — los últimos 15 minutos son para arquitectura personalizada y preguntas abiertas.

🎬 Let’s Go to the Movies (and Actually Talk… or Not)

Whether you're a film nerd, popcorn enthusiast, or just looking for a chill night out with interesting people — this one's for you.

We’re heading out to see a movie together, then grabbing food or drinks after. If the film's great (or terrible), we’ll probably talk about it forever. If it’s just okay, we’ll talk about it for 10 minutes and move on to everything else — books, dating apps, weird dreams, how Toronto keeps getting more expensive, etc.

The vibe is relaxed, friendly, and not too serious. No film degree needed. No icebreakers. No pressure to “perform.” Just come enjoy the film, connect with some thoughtful people, and see where the night goes Click here to watch trailer!

description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
# 🎤🏝️ KARAOKE AT THE TORONTO ISLANDS! — OUR FIRST EVER! 🌅🎶

**Friday\, September 11 \| Karaoke starts at 8:00 PM**
We're doing something we've **never done before** — taking our Meetup karaoke night to the **Toronto Islands!** 🏝️🎤

Join us for an unforgettable evening of music, laughs, drinks, and summer vibes at the **Toronto Island Marina & Yacht Club**, with [karaoke hosted by the fantastic ](https://torontoislandmarina.com/event/karaoke-with-ivan-rivers/?instance_id=558)**[Ivan Rivers](https://torontoislandmarina.com/event/karaoke-with-ivan-rivers/?instance_id=558)**[!](https://torontoislandmarina.com/event/karaoke-with-ivan-rivers/?instance_id=558)
What better way to say **BYE BYE TO SUMMER** than singing your favourite songs on the Islands? ☀️🎶

### 🏝️ GETTING TO THE ISLANDS

We will be taking the 7PM ferry to Centre Islands.

If you're arriving later you'll need to get to Marina on your own.

👉 **Check the ferry schedule here:**
[Toronto Island Ferry Routes & Schedules](https://www.toronto.ca/explore-enjoy/toronto-island-ferries/ferry-routes-schedules/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**Important:** Give yourself plenty of time to get to the ferry terminal and board the boat. Ferry lineups can vary, especially on a summer evening.
Once you arrive at **Centre Island**, make your way toward the **[Toronto Island Marina & Yacht Club](https://torontoislandmarina.com/event/karaoke-with-ivan-rivers/?instance_id=558)**[.](https://torontoislandmarina.com/event/karaoke-with-ivan-rivers/?instance_id=558)

🚶‍♂️ Follow the signs toward the marina and **look for our Meetup signs on the tables**. That's where you'll find our group!

### 🎤 KARAOKE STARTS AT 8:00 PM!

We'll be settling in at the Marina & Yacht Club before karaoke gets underway at **8 PM**.

🎶 Hosted by **Ivan Rivers**
🎤 Your favourite songs
😂 Plenty of laughs
🏝️ An amazing Island setting
🌃 Toronto skyline views
☀️ One last big summer night!

Whether you're the person who immediately grabs the microphone or the person who says *"I'm just here to watch"* before eventually getting talked into singing — **come join us!** 😆

### 📱 FINDING THE GROUP

All **registered Meetup attendees will have Nick's phone number** so you can contact him if you have trouble finding the group or need assistance getting to our tables.
Please make sure your phone is charged!

### ⚠️ A FEW THINGS TO KNOW

• **RSVP is important** — please register if you're planning to attend.
• **Check the ferry schedule before leaving home.**
• Allow extra time for ferry lineups and the walk from Centre Island to the marina.
• Wear comfortable shoes — you'll be walking on the Island.
• Keep an eye on the weather and dress appropriately for an evening outdoors.
• Don't forget your phone! 📱
• And most importantly… **come ready to have FUN!** 🎉
This is our **FIRST-EVER Toronto Islands karaoke night**, so let's make it a good one!

Unsure of your schedule? You can just show up for this one .

🏝️ **Toronto Islands + 🎤 Karaoke + 🎶 Great music + 😂 Great people = one heck of a summer send-off!**

**Let's say BYE BYE TO SUMMER in style!** ☀️🍂🎤
**See you on the Islands!**

title: Randy Boyagoda: Lords of Serendipity
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
TPL presents novelist Randy Boyagoda in conversation with Parul Sehgal at the Toronto Reference Library's Appel Salon.
In his wildly funny and richly observed new novel
Lords of Serendipity
, acclaimed author Randy Boyagoda delivers the twenty-first-century global campus novel, a story that spans contemporary Sri Lanka and the United States, following two teenage girls with similar collegiate ambitions. What does the global scramble for elite education reveal about class, ambition, and inequality today? How do institutions meant to open doors so often become sites of exploitation, for domestic and international students, for parents, for those gatekeepers and intermediaries trying to extract as much as they offer?
Drawing on his own decades inside the academy as an English professor and U of T's first-ever Advisor on Civil Discourse, Boyagoda brings a novelist's eye and a scholar's insight to this wicked, humane satire of careerism, hope, and the lengths we'll go to for the people we love.
Join one of Canada's most celebrated literary novelists, in conversation with acclaimed critic Parul Sehgal, for an evening exploring ambition, inequality, and the absurd theatre of higher education in the twenty-first century.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

title: Caves, Cliffs, and Crevices: The Duncan Caves Loop
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/duncan-caves)**

**Join us as we head to the Duncan escarpment to explore some incredible ‘crevice’ or ‘fracture’ caves, created over thousands of years through a mixture of glacial movement, extreme temperatures and the raw force of gravity.**

We start the hike through open farmland and meadow before the ground tilts up and we climb onto the escarpment itself. From there, most of the day is spent walking along the escarpment and through the forest that grows right up to the cliff edge and spill over its exposed rock.

We will then descend into the caves, with some being over 30 metres deep. You will be scrambling in some places, working your way down and through one of the more unique pieces of trail anywhere in Ontario.

From the caves, the trail climbs back along the escarpment edge through mature forest, with a stretch of cliff top that opens up into views out over the valley below. We drop back down and loop through the same mix of field and forest that opened the day.

**Parking is extremely limited at the trailhead, so we recommend taking transport for this adventure.**
‍
**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to [info@wildernessunion.com](mailto:info@wildernessunion.com)

**Highlights**
**The Crevice Caves:** A gorge over 30 metres deep, formed by rock shifting off the escarpment face.
**Cliff Top Views:** A stretch of trail along the escarpment edge showing off open views over the valley.
**Farmland to Forest:** Open farm fields give way straight into escarpment forest.

**Event cost: $60+HST (for explorer members) - $40 optional transport available.**
**Register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/duncan-caves)**

**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.

Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.

Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!

***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

title: (SOLD OUT SESSION) Art and Form intermediate lighting workshop w Ciara
description:
The Toronto Photography Group
## LINK to purchase tickets for event- [https://www.wtpg.ngo/event-details/wtpg-signature-series-art-and-form-intermediate-level-lighting-with-ciara](https://www.wtpg.ngo/event-details/wtpg-signature-series-art-and-form-intermediate-level-lighting-with-ciara)

## About the event

# Light, Art & Form — Intermediate Art Nude Photography Workshop

![](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/1eaf19_36e8e2cfab3e43db8b02a308cfd28143~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_1686,h_844,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_auto/1eaf19_36e8e2cfab3e43db8b02a308cfd28143~mv2.jpg)

## About the Event

**10:00 AM – 12:00 PM**
We are excited to present **Light, Art & Form**, an intermediate-level studio photography workshop exploring the creative possibilities of **art nude photography, light and form**, featuring the talented model **Ciara Antoski**.
This hands-on workshop is designed for photographers who want to develop their understanding of studio lighting while creating dramatic, artistic and carefully composed images for their portfolios.
Working in a small, intimate group, we'll explore several professional lighting setups and discuss how the **position, direction, quality and shape of light** can transform the appearance of the human form.
![](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/1eaf19_1102af7eb2474a63bc94b3ad85ccabcb~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_1686,h_844,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_auto/1eaf19_1102af7eb2474a63bc94b3ad85ccabcb~mv2.jpg)

## Workshop Details

Are you passionate about art nude photography? Do you want to better understand how professional photographers create dramatic and beautiful lighting?
This workshop is focused on **learning through doing**. Phil Sutherland will guide participants through each setup, explaining the lighting choices, modifiers, angles and techniques used to create the desired look.
Participants will have opportunities to photograph each setup while receiving guidance and feedback throughout the session.
![](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/1eaf19_13ca992b3f9e4f2faccb98a3ecc45847~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_918,h_613,al_c,q_85,enc_auto/1eaf19_13ca992b3f9e4f2faccb98a3ecc45847~mv2.jpg)

### Framing & Composition

During the workshop, we'll explore several approaches to photographing the figure, including:

* **2/3-body compositions**
* **Floor-level compositions featuring lingerie**
* **Full-body compositions**
* Exploring how framing, negative space and perspective affect the final image
* Using light and shadow to emphasize form and create mood

## Workshop Team

**Instructor:** Phil Sutherland

**Model:** Ciara Antoski

**Assistant:** Volunteer to be announced
Ciara brings considerable experience and professionalism to the workshop, and we're thrilled to have her working with us for this session.

### Small Group — Maximum 6 Photographers

To provide a better learning and shooting experience, we are limiting this workshop to **a maximum of six participants**.
Keeping the group small allows for more individual attention, more opportunities to ask questions and meaningful shooting time with each lighting setup.

## About West Toronto Photography Group

As an **Indigenous-run, not-for-profit arts organization**, West Toronto Photography Group is committed to supporting photographers, sharing knowledge and making arts programming accessible to the community.
Our workshops are designed to create a welcoming and professional environment where photographers can learn, experiment, meet other artists and—most importantly—have fun making photographs.

## Workshop Information

**Maximum Participants:** 6

**Workshop Fee:** CAD $125 + HST and applicable vendor fee

## What Should I Bring?

Please bring:

* DSLR, mirrorless or medium-format camera
* Your preferred lenses
* Fully charged batteries
* Freshly formatted memory card(s)
* A general-purpose lens
* Pen and paper if you'd like to take notes

**Tripods and camera supports are not required** for this workshop.

### Wireless Triggers

We provide wireless triggers for most mainstream camera systems. If you're unsure whether your camera is compatible, please contact us before the workshop and we'll be happy to confirm.

## Model Release

A **West Toronto Photography Group model release** will be provided to each participant.
The release covers **non-commercial use and photography created for educational and training purposes**. The model will sign the releases, and printed copies will be provided to participating photographers.

## Cancellation & Transfer Policy

If we, as organizers, need to postpone or cancel the workshop, refunds will be issued within **72 hours**.
We understand that sometimes circumstances prevent participants from attending. If you can no longer attend, please contact us as soon as possible. We will do our best to help you **resell your workshop spot to another member of the group**.
If we are able to resell your spot, you will be reimbursed for the ticket price. If the spot cannot be resold, you may transfer your registration to another person to attend in your place; unfortunately, **no refund will be available if the spot remains unsold**.

## Join Us

Come explore the relationship between **light, shadow and the human form** in this focused intermediate photography workshop.
Whether you're looking to strengthen your studio lighting skills, expand your portfolio or explore new approaches to art nude photography, **Light, Art & Form** offers an opportunity to learn, experiment and create in a supportive professional environment.
We look forward to welcoming you to the studio!

title: Cyanotype Printmaking
location:
HackLab.TO
1677 St Clair Ave W, Toronto ON M6N 1H9, Canada
description: Cyanotype, aka Blueprinting, is one of the earliest known photographic printing processes. Discovered in the 1840s by John Herschell, this photo-sensitive dye was once ubiquitous as a method of reproducing building plans and schematics. Anna Atkins, a family friend of Herschell's received recognition for her contributions to science - unusual for women at the time - when she travelled around the British coast producing botanical contact-prints. Join us in celebrating her legacy and exploring the creative applications of this non-toxic & easy to use photographic chemistry.
