title: Indigenous Beading Workshop: Orange Shirt Pin
description:
Date: Saturday, September 12, 2026
Time: 10:30 am – 1:00 pm
Location: Bata Shoe Museum, 327 Bloor St. W.
Tickets: $65 
Join Toronto-based Cree-Métis artist Marissa Magneson for a beginner-friendly beading workshop. Through this hands-on workshop, participants will walk away with a greater understanding of Indigenous beadwork, tools, and techniques as they work to complete a small beaded Orange Shirt pin. No experience is necessary.  
A note from the artist: “I include ceremonial tobacco in these pins, recognizing that learning and discussing topics including, but not limited to, residential schools is heavy. The medicine is there to help us in navigating those feelings, while marking our commitment to and responsibility of reconciliAction. Likewise, this becomes a part of the ceremony found within this workshop, as the medicine is added in the community, making everyone a part of that work.” 
Participants are invited to fill their pins with ceremonial tobacco, one of the four sacred medicines, but this step is not mandatory.  
Agenda
10:00 am – Doors Open
10:30 am to 1:00 pm – Workshop (with a 30-minute break) 
Recommended for participants 16+. Includes instruction, materials, and access to all current exhibitions.  
BUY YOUR TICKETS  

ABOUT Marissa Magneson: 
 
Marissa Magneson is a Cree-Métis artist, photographer, educator, and workshop facilitator currently pursuing her Ph.D. at York University in the Faculty of Education, where she is researching Beadwork as Pedagogy: A Bridge Towards Cultural Reclamation and (re)Conciliation. She has a BFA honours degree from York University (Toronto, Canada) and a Master’s degree in Canadian and Indigenous Studies from Trent University (Peterborough, Canada). Her research explores Indigenous methodologies using beadwork as visual storytelling. Marissa’s work is rooted in decolonizing education, strengthening community, and cultural reclamation. In her collaborative work with various organizations, Marissa works towards photographing, consulting, educating, and creating programming in meaningful ways. Marissa would like to acknowledge her maternal grandmother, Elaine Jessop, whose life-long work on Indigenous women’s rights inspires her own journey.

title: Introduction to Silverpoint Drawing
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for a fun-filled afternoon of silverpoint drawing!
Discover the fascinating qualities of silverpoint, a drawing medium favoured during the Middle Ages and Renaissance by old masters, such as Leonardo Da Vinci and Albrecht Dürer. Participants will create an original silverpoint drawing of a leaf onto a prepared board that will develop warm brown tones as it ages. Beginners welcome.
 
Each attendee will receive a silver drawing pencil and learn how to continue using this medium beyond the classroom.
 
Saturday, September 12, 1 to 4 p.m.
Public $70, TBG Members $65 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Alan Li
Artist and conservationist Alan Li uses pencils, ink and paint to document the wonders of the natural world. Alan’s mission is to build connections to nature through arts-based education. Since 2015, he has been partnering with non-profit environmental organizations to teach nature focused art programs and workshops.
 
Alan was responsible for the successful launch of the Toronto Nature Sketch program in 2018, teaching all of the art lessons during that inaugural year. Nature Sketch is an initiative of Canadian artist Robert Bateman and the Bateman Foundation.
In 2019, Alan was a speaker at the annual Ravine Symposium at Toronto Botanical Garden. In his presentation, he shared stories behind ravine-inspired artwork created by himself and a small brigade of volunteer artists. Funds raised through the sale of the artwork were donated to ravine conservation initiatives at the garden.
 
Alan currently teaches Field Sketching, Nature Drawing and Linocut Printmaking at Toronto Botanical Garden and the High Park Nature Centre.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
 
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!

**It's that time again everyone, and TIFF and the stars are back in Toronto as if they ever left. So let's do another film locations extravaganza and have some fun in the mean time. I love this tour.**

Mary Pickford stares into the camera.

Born on University Avenue, she became the girl with the golden curls, the first Hollywood star, and now Toronto is the star!

Good Will Hunting, Pacific Rim, X-Men, Robocop, Total Recall, Prom Night, Suicide Squad, My Big Fat Greek Wedding, Police Academy, and the list goes on and on and on.

It was back in the 1920s that Toronto emerged as a shy newcomer. But it stepped up to the camera, smiled, and went to work. The first real feature movie was "The Man From Toronto," even though it was not filmed here, and in the late 60s Toronto was "Goin' Down the Road," that the city was Hollywood bound.

And it wasn't just movies! Television movies, series, documentaries, music videos and video games were all shot here in Toronto. Award shows such as The Genie's, Juno's, the Canadian Screen Awards, Giller Prize and The Much Music Video Awards are all celebrated here! Let's find out where the movies came alive with this unique walking tour!

This walking tour is for all walking levels and fitness skills. Please dress for the season and bring water. And remember to bring your love of movie magic as well. Hope to see you there.

This tour begins at the famous TORONTO sign at Nathan Phillips Square. We end at Front and Jarvis!

title: Pin Up Perfection w Ciara
description:
The Toronto Photography Group
## Details

\#\# Details
Link for tickets - [https://www.wtpg.ngo/event-details/pin-up-perfection-photography-lighting-workshop-2](https://www.wtpg.ngo/event-details/pin-up-perfection-photography-lighting-workshop-2)
\#\# About the event
**Quick Details**
1:00 pm - 3:00 pm Pin Up Perfection! Photography lighting workshop
Model Ciara Antoski
Instructor: Phil Sutherland
Assistant/ Volunteer to be announced soon,
\# Pin Up Perfection\! — Photography Lighting Workshop
\#\# Quick Details
**1:00 PM – 3:00 PM**
**Pin Up Perfection! — Photography Lighting Workshop**
**Model:** Ciara Antoski
**Instructor:** Phil Sutherland
**Assistant/Volunteer:** To be announced
Step back into the golden age of **retro Pin Up photography** for a fun, hands-on studio lighting workshop designed to help you build your confidence, understand studio lighting and create great images.
Expect **oldies tunes, vintage-inspired outfits, classic Pin Up poses and some seriously fun lighting!** We are thrilled to have **Ciara Antoski** joining us as our model. Ciara is an amazing model, and we are very lucky to have her helping us bring this workshop to life.

* \!\[img\]\(\)
* \!\[img\]\(\)
* \!\[img\]\(\)

\#\#\# What You'll Learn
Whether Pin Up photography is a new interest or an established passion, this workshop will help you take your studio lighting skills to the next level.
This **two-hour, information-packed workshop** is limited to **only 6 photographers**, giving everyone plenty of opportunity to ask questions, experiment with the lighting and get hands-on shooting time.
During the workshop, we will:
**1\. Explore the equipment**
Get a detailed introduction to the studio equipment, modifiers and lighting tools we will be using. We will build and adjust **three different lighting setups** throughout the workshop.
**2\. Discover the Old\-School Pin Up Look**
We'll explore the history and techniques behind classic Pin Up photography, including how older studio spaces, lights and modifiers were used to create that distinctive vintage look. We'll also compare traditional techniques with modern studio lighting tools.
**3\. Shoot Three Lighting Setups**
We will create and photograph **three different lighting setups**, giving each participant opportunities to shoot, experiment and see firsthand how changing the position, size and direction of the light affects the final image.
\#\# Who Is This Workshop For?
This workshop is suitable for **photographers of all skill levels** who want to learn more about studio photography and become more comfortable working with professional lighting equipment.
You don't need to be an experienced studio photographer. We'll demonstrate the lighting techniques, explain the equipment and give everyone opportunities to photograph each setup.
We'll also discuss how different modifiers—including **reflectors, umbrellas, softboxes, grids, snoots and beauty dishes**—can be used to shape and control light.
\#\#\# Maximum 6 Participants
Keeping the group small means **more shooting time, more opportunities to ask questions and more hands-on learning** for everyone.
Time is valuable, so we keep our workshops efficient, practical and focused on getting you behind the camera. You'll spend less time standing around and more time **learning, shooting and experimenting with light.**
\#\# What We Provide
📸 A professional and comfortable studio environment
💡 A variety of professional lighting equipment and modifiers
🎯 Hands-on instruction and lighting demonstrations
👩 A professional model with multiple shooting opportunities
🤝 Time to network and learn with other photographers
📚 Practical instruction you can take back to your own studio or shoots
**No turkey shoots!** Everyone gets opportunities to photograph the model and work with the lighting setups.
\#\# What Should I Bring?
**Your camera!** Any DSLR or mirrorless camera with manual controls will work perfectly.
Please bring:

* A camera capable of manual exposure
* Freshly charged batteries
* Formatted memory cards
* Your favourite lens — anything from approximately **10mm–160mm** can work, depending on your camera and shooting style
* Your curiosity and passion for photography!

Don't worry if you're not sure what settings to use. **We'll help you get started with the appropriate exposure settings and explain why we're using them.**
Most importantly, bring your enthusiasm and a willingness to learn. **We'll bring the fun!**
\#\# Who Should Take Our Workshops?
Our workshops are perfect for photographers who have a **basic understanding of their camera and manual settings**, but they are also welcoming to photographers at more advanced levels who want to explore new lighting techniques.
Whether you're:

* Just starting to shoot in a studio
* Looking to understand studio lighting better
* Interested in Pin Up and vintage photography
* Wanting to experiment with professional modifiers
* Looking for new lighting ideas for your own photography
* Or simply want to spend two hours making great photographs with other photographers

**Pin Up Perfection! is designed to be fun, practical and packed with information.**
Come learn the lighting, photograph an amazing model, experiment with classic Pin Up techniques and leave with new skills you can put to work in your own photography.
If Pin up photography lighting is one of your interest or your passion and you want to upgrade your studio lighting skills
You will be substantially informed from this well paced 1.5 hour group workshop and we are limiting the workshop size to only 6 people to allow more time for questions and learning.
1 - This workshop will spend the two hours going through a detailed run down of equipment names and how we will use them as we set up the lighting for each of the 3x setups we will build during the workshop.
2 - We will discuss old school Pin Up shooting and how the older modifiers and studio spaces worked and take time to introduce different tools used to create images in studio that are old and new school
3 - We will shoot 3 different lighting set ups in the 2 hour lighting workshop and have a great time in studio.

title: From Hello to Hangout
description:
Try New Things in Toronto!
How to Turn a Good Conversation Into an Actual Connection

Let’s say you start a conversation.. GREAT! Then the problem is what happens after, the "let's hang out sometime" that never turns into an actual plan, the friendly chat that fades into nothing, the acquaintance you never quite become friends with… the first date that never comes.

This workshop is all about the specific, tangible moves that turn a good conversation into a real friendship, a great romance and maybe even a solid social circle.

**In 60 minutes, you'll learn how to:**

* Lock in real plans on the spot, instead of vague "let's exchange numbers" energy
* Build a group chat that takes on a life of its own
* Start a recurring hangout that makes you the person people gather around
* Deepen a friendship without oversharing (or staying stuck in small talk forever)
* Become the person who connects others

Whether you're rebuilding your social circle after a breakup, new to a city, or just tired of conversations that go nowhere, you'll leave with a concrete plan and a cheat sheet to take with you.

title: Improv Class for New Friends
description:
Improv For New Friends
Don't be disappointed if you don't see a bunch of people attending. I advertise this on multiple platforms and the class usually sells out.

\*\*If you don't use Paypal, email me at ralph@socap.ca and we'll figure it out. You can pay be etransfer or with a credit card/cash at the venue.\*\*

Improv comedy uses several techniques to create laughter. These include, creating an atmosphere free of judgement, saying 'yes', active listening, being positive, putting your focus on others, and the importance of play and laughter.

Not coincidentally, these are the same things that happen to us naturally when we are bonding with another person.

In this class, we'll explore these techniques not with the goal of being funny, but with the goal of being people that other people want to be around.

The teacher, Ralph MacLeod, is a co-founder of two independent improv clubs in Toronto - Bad Dog Theatre and Social Capital Theatre. He's been teaching improv for over 30 years. He also teaches these same techniques to several organizations including UofT, Google, Kraft, Shopify and many, many more.

Please feel free to ask any questions you may have!

FAQs and Good To Know....

After every event, a group from this class sit down and have a drink together so be prepared to stay if you want! Of course, you don't HAVE to.

You also don't have to be single or bring a friend. The vibe of this class is much more 'making new friends' than a 'singles' mixer'.

We usually run to 8:15 so pay for extra parking!

title: The 28th Annual Family & Friends Golf Tournament
location: Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre
description:
Golf Registration is Closed! ⛳ Thank you for the incredible support! The 28th Annual Family & Friends Golf Tournament will be held on Sunday September 13, 2026, on the Classic Course at Rolling Hills Golf Club in Stouffville. This day is also National Grandparents’ Day, so we will have special prizes for the Grandparent/Grandchild Champions! This is a chance for families and friends to share a fun day of golf – all skill levels are welcome and there are lots of prizes to be won! After a great day of golfing, there will be games, a raffle, prize presentations and dinner back at the JCCC. We encourage everyone to join with grandparents, grandchildren, parents, siblings, aunts, uncles, cousins, or just as a group of friends. There will be awards for 3 categories: iA Private Wealth Cup (Lowest Scramble Score for foursome) Consul General Cup (Lowest Family* Scramble) * Must all be related Roy & Kay Shin Memorial Cup (Lowest Grandparent/Grandchild Score) Note: a foursome cannot win more than 1 category. As in the past, it will be an early Shotgun format (8:30am start for everyone) and the format is a Texas Scramble (where everyone hits a tee shot, then the foursome picks the best lie, and everyone else plays their ball from that spot, and so on). We are so appreciative of iA Private Wealth's Marty Kobayashi, confirmed again this year as our Platinum Sponsor. So please come on out for a fun day!! The Tournament is limited to the first 144 golfers registered. We had an overwhelming response last year so make sure to get your registration submitted before it fills up. REGISTRATION NEW THIS YEAR: Registration will ONLY be on-line through the "Register" link below. You must register the whole team (4 players) at sign up. See below for the details. The registration link will open on Monday July 13, 2026 at 10 AM . Please note that Green Fees, Cart Rental fees and food prices have all gone up substantially over the past year, so we have no choice but to increase entry fees. However, we have eliminated the 2-price system so now all golfers pay the same price: Entry Fee: Regular 4 player team ($145 pp - includes tax) OR Gold Sponsor 4 player team $680. Fees include – Green fees/Shared Power Cart/Musubi Lunch/Awards/Dinner/Prizes. Dinners only: Adults $35 (includes tax) / Children (under 10 years $12 (includes tax)). More Registration details: Register as 4 person Teams – Regular Fee or as Gold Sponsor Register up to 2 teams in one application. Award categories and extra dinners are included in the registration form. Main contact/payee required to sign up by name, additional players can be left anonymous. Substitute players allowed, no refunds. Contact the organizers to confirm all player names no later than Monday August 31st . Other sponsorship types: In Memoriam ($200) / Bronze level ($200) which include signage and 2 adults dinners – please contact the organizers to provide more details. Register *Player registration is full. Dinner, and In Memoriam and/or Bronze sponsorship are still available until August 14. For ALL inquiries/questions : Organizers Sharon Marubashi by e-mail , or cell (647-291-4751) and Dawna Kobayashi by e-mail , or cell (416-407-8102).

title: 31st Annual Tim Hortons GWN Dragon Boat Challenge
location: Marilyn Bell Park,1095 Lake Shore Blvd W, Toronto, ON M6K, Canada
description:
GWN Dragon Boat is proud to present the 31st Annual Tim Hortons GWN Dragon Boat Challenge, taking place on September 12 & 13, 2026 at Toronto’s scenic Marilyn Bell Park. This event proudly supports Tim Hortons Foundation Camps.

Twenty paddlers move in unison, combining strength and teamwork in a boat whose elaborate design originates from ancient China. Social groups and businesses alike embrace the sport because it builds camaraderie, forms connections, and promotes healthy lifestyles.

Admission to this family-friendly event is free; races will begin at approximately 8:30am and will continue throughout each day. Festival grounds will offer a variety of activities for all participants and spectators. Families can bring their children to enjoy live performances, inflatable bounce houses/obstacle courses in the interactive Family Fun Zone. Grab a bite from one of our Food Trucks while wandering through the Health & Wellness Zone featuring exciting local products and services to assist in leading a healthy lifestyle. For all your shopping needs, stop by the Artisan Village and Vendor Marketplace. Last but definitely not least, the Left Field Brewery Beer Garden will keep the party going located right by the finish line with a live band performing on the main stage each afternoon.

New teams and individuals are welcome! Invite friends, family, colleagues - form a group of 16 to 25 people and sign-up a team today. If you or a couple of friends are interested, there is a pay per seat option available, contact us at info@gwndragonboat.com mailto:info@gwndragonboat.com?subject=GWN%20Challenge%20-%20inquiry  to join.

title: GO Train Hike - Unionville/Markham
description:
Toronto Bruce Trail Club
he villages of Unionville & Markham are connected by the Rouge Valley Trail System following the Rouge River and running behind the historic buildings on Main Street Unionville, by Walden Pond in Austin Drive Park, through Milne Dam Conservation Area, and ending with a 143 metre long suspension bridge over the dam. We will walk into the village of Markham and finish with a short boardwalk trail through Tannery Pond which is close to the Markham GO Station. We begin the hike at Unionville GO Station hiking north to the historic Main Street and picking up the Rouge Valley Trail at Carlton Road. Return to Toronto or the starting point by GO Train or York Region Transit bus. Optional stop at the Rouge River Craft Brewery after the hike.
Terrain is easy, mostly paved path/boardwalk with some dirt trails.
On The Go Maps Link:
[https://onthegomap.com/s/g5rhpj1s](https://onthegomap.com/s/g5rhpj1s)

Bring lunch, water, snacks, hat. and insect repellant.

Please register on the Bruce Trail Conservancy website at:
[https://hikes.brucetrail.org/event/go-train-hike-unionville-markham-rouge-river-trail-2/2026-09-13/](https://hikes.brucetrail.org/event/go-train-hike-unionville-markham-rouge-river-trail-2/2026-09-13/)

title: English Spanish Language Conversation
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Friday
* Saturday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** here **»** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
**Héctor Fuentes**

title: On the Trail of the Family Compact (NEW for 2026)
description:
Toronto History Walks
\*\***The Toronto History Walks Explorer Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!\*\***

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket price when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

The **Family Compact** was a small group of powerful men who controlled much of the political, and social life in what was then called Upper Canada (Ontario) during the early 1800s. They were not an official organization with membership cards or meetings, but rather a close-knit network of politicians, judges, church leaders, and wealthy businessmen who often shared similar backgrounds, and family connections.

Because so many important positions were held by members of this circle, they had enormous influence over government decisions, land distribution, banking, education, and policy. To many ordinary settlers arriving in the colony, it often seemed as though a handful of well-connected families were running the province.

The influence of the Family Compact was strong in the growing town of York, later Toronto. York was the colonial capital, and many of the colony's most powerful figures lived and worked there. Men such as John Strachan played major roles in shaping the colony's institutions. The group believed that society worked best when guided by educated and wealthy leaders, and they often looked to Britain as their model.

While they saw themselves as protecting stability and order, critics argued that they were protecting their own privileges and limiting opportunities for others.

As Upper Canada grew, dissatisfaction with the Family Compact also grew. Farmers, merchants, and reform-minded citizens became frustrated by what they saw as favoritism, and limited political representation. Many believed that government positions and economic opportunities were being distributed based on connections rather than merit. Reformers such as William Lyon Mackenzie used newspapers and public meetings to challenge the Compact's power and demand a more democratic system of government.

The conflict reached a dramatic point during the Upper Canada Rebellion of 1837. Although the rebellion itself was quickly defeated, it highlighted widespread concerns about how the colony was being governed. In the years that followed, political reforms gradually reduced the influence of the Family Compact and introduced more responsible government.

Today, the Family Compact is remembered as an important part of Toronto and Ontario's early history, and how growing demands for democracy helped shape the province we know today.

This tour explores some of the sites associated with the Family Compact, and the history of early Toronto and Ontario. There are about 25 stops on this new tour for 2026!

This walk begins and ends outside St. James Cathedral at 106 King Street East at Church Street.

This tour has a ticketed price of $15.00 per person!

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket price when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

You will take home 4 creations of your own design and if you cant get enough in class, you can use the TTL Makerspace leatherworking kits or borrow one of the Toronto Tool Library’s similar kits.

 Materials and equipment for all projects are provided with the course.

 
 
 
 Projects: 
 
 Project 1: Leather Wallet 
 Project 2: Coin Purse 
 Project 3: Waterskin 
 Project 4: Collar/bracelet 
 
 
 Materials and equipment for all projects are provided with the course. 
 
 

 
 
 
 

 
 Schedule 
4 weeks, Sundays 2pm to 5pm 
 
 

 
 
 Outcomes 
 At the end of the course you will have achieved the following goals: 
 
  

 
- A good understanding of the nature and properties of leather 

- A solid foundation in various methods of cutting, burnishing, dying and finishing. 

- Experience with stamping and engraving leather projects. 

- Familiarity with sewing machines and their use on thinner leather. 

- Knowledge of wet molding and the waterproofing of leather. 

- An understanding of studs, buckles, rivets, snaps and other hardware. 

 
 
 
 

 
 Useful for: bags, garments, belts, custom cases/sheaths

title: La Société d'histoire de Toronto: HISTORITOUR - ALLAN GARDENS, SES SERRES ET SON PARC
location: Allan Gardens, 160 Gerrard Street East, Toronto, Ontario, M5A 2E5, Canada
description:
Départ : Rencontre au coin sud-est des rues Jarvis et Carlton – le tram 506 vous y dépose
Fin : Dans le parc 
Guides : Béatrice Luneau et Rolande Smith 
Terrain plat 
Depuis sa création en 1858, le parc Allan Gardens n’a cessé de voir la ville grandir autour de lui. L’ensemble de ses six serres ont été installées au fur et à mesure des années (The Palm House en 1910, The Temperate House en 1924 et les autres dans les années 50). Certaines serres ont été transférées de l’Exhibition Place et de l’Université de Toronto. 
Venez découvrir ce que cet ensemble vous offre aujourd’hui. Cette visite se fera en plusieurs étapes commençant par une présentation en salle sur l’histoire du parc et des serres, puis une visite des serres et si le temps le permet un tour du parc et de ses arbres. 
Pas nécessaire de réserver. La Société d’histoire de Toronto passe le chapeau à la fin de la visite. Pas de chien. 
Contacts : info@sht.ca ou smth7631@rogers.com

Toronto has a rich history, and it's all around us, but certain buildings do stand out and tell our story. On this walking tour the following buildings are explored and their history revealed. This new tour is for residents and tourists who want to reconnect with their city, or get to know it from a different vantage point!

* Daniel Brooke Building
* St. Lawrence Hall
* St. James Anglican Cathedral
* St. Michael's Cathedral
* Mackenzie House
* Massey Hall
* Old City Hall
* Osgoode Hall
* Campbell House Museum
* Gooderham Building

and a few other hidden surprises along the way from the Toronto Stock Exchange to the New City Hall and a few others in between!

This walking tour is for all walking levels. Please dress for the season, and hope to see you there.

Please meet in front of the iconic St. Lawrence Hall at the corner of Jarvis and King Street East, we end the tour at Historic Campbell House!

This tour has a ticket price of $15.00 per person.

title: Computers for Beginners
location: York Woods, Enhanced Learning Center
description:
Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse
A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this first session you will:
Observe and practice how to operate a mouse effectively
Understand various mouse pointers and cursors
Review basic keyboard functions
Use the mouse for basic Windows functions
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a computer mouse at a basic level and will be able to go online for additional practice.
Prerequisites: No computer experience required.
Format: Hands-on with demonstrations
Computers for Beginners 2: Use the Keyboard
A class on basic keyboard functions for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this second session you will:
Familiarize yourself through practice with the most essential keyboard functions (alphabet, number and symbol keys)
Practice proper keyboarding posture
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a keyboard at a beginner level and know how to go online for additional practice.
Prerequisites: Computer for Beginners 1 or basic mouse skills
Format: Hands-on with demonstrations
Computers for Beginners 3: Use Windows
A class on essential basic Windows skills for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this third session you will:
Become familiar with the Windows (10) operating system
Practice using common Windows features: File Explorer, Desktop, Taskbar, Windows, Applications
Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to create and organize files in the Windows environment.
Prerequisites: Computer for Beginners 1 & 2 or basic mouse and keyboarding skills
Format: Hands-on with demonstrations
Computers for Beginners 4: Use the Internet
An introductory class on the Internet for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fourth session you will:
Understand how to read a web site address
Practice using web addresses
Search for information using a search engine
Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches.
Prerequisites: Computer for Beginners 1 & 2 or basic mouse and keyboarding skills
Format: Hands-on with demonstrations
Computers for Beginners 5: Use Google Search and Maps
A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fifth session you will:
Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites
Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel.
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use more advanced search engine features and use Google Maps at a basic level.
Prerequisites: Computers for Beginners 1 & 2 or basic mouse, keyboarding and internet skills
Format: Hands-on with demonstrations
Computers for Beginners 6: Use Gmail
Learn to use Gmail, Google’s free web-based email service.
In this sixth session you will:
Practice basic email functions: send, read, reply, forward, delete email, and attach files
Review how spam and junk mail work
Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to use email.
Instructions on how to set up and manage your own free Gmail account are included in the handout.
Prerequisites: Basic keyboarding and mouse skills required.
Format: Hands-on with demonstrations

title: Dystopia Nonfiction Book Club: The Crisis of Canadian Democracy
location: Toronto Reference Library, Lower Level, Room B1
description:
Join us each month to discuss issues in politics and society, and explore how powerful forces are exploiting our world and dystopian imaginings are becoming present-day realities.
September’s book is
The Crisis of Canadian Democracy
by journalist Andrew Coyne. Copies of the book are available in print and eBook format. Book club attendees are encouraged to read the book in advance of the meeting.
The Crisis of Canadian Democracy "dismantles the comforting myths Canadians tell themselves about their political system, revealing a parliamentary structure eroded by unaccountable leaders, disempowered MPs, manipulated elections, and systemic dysfunction. [The book] is both a wake-up call and a call to action, offering compelling solutions to restore genuine self-government to Canadian politics." Andrew Coyne warns Canadians that "as Parliament's legitimacy declines, people look to alternate sources of representation... In time, as we have seen south of the border, the discrediting of democratic institutions can begin to nourish a desire for autocracy."
Drop in. No registration required.

title: Patrick Radden Keefe: London Falling
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
TPL presents acclaimed investigative journalist Patrick Radden Keefe in conversation with Rachel Giese at the Toronto Reference Library's Appel Salon.
From the bestselling author of Empire of Pain and Say Nothing, Patrick Radden Keefe, comes
London Falling: A Mysterious Death in a Gilded City and a Family's Search for Truth
, a gripping investigation into extreme wealth, dark truths, power, identity and inequality.
Through the investigation of teenager Zac Brettler’s fall to death from a luxury riverside apartment, Keefe deftly fills-in the gaps of this tragic story with the skill of an investigative journalist. By exploring the societal and familial roots behind Brettler’s death, Keefe transforms a true-crime mystery into a meditation on modern parenting, unresolvable grief, and the corrosive effects of isolation in a city where wealth means everything.
What does London's underworld of dirty money and untouchable power reveal about the wider forces reshaping cities everywhere? And how do families rebuild their understanding of someone they loved after learning they never fully knew them at all?
Join one of the most acclaimed nonfiction writers working today, in conversation with journalist and critic Rachel Giese, for a riveting exploration of truth, deception, and the hidden costs of a gilded world.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

title: ROM:  Weston International Award--Evening with Hanif Abdurraqib ($20)
description:
TORONTO ARTS & CULTURE
{ This Author EVENT is Sold-Out }

Always a HOT ticket--an important (international) AUTHOR Talk. At the ROM.

($15-$20 only!!)

American author **Hanif Abdurraqib has won the 2026 Weston International Award. $75,000**

**Overview--**

The evening will feature **Hanif Abdurraquib** delivering a talk and having an in-depth conversation with **CBC ARTS.**

\*\*\*Join us on Monday, September 14 at the Royal Ontario Museum, for an evening with the 2026 Weston International Award winner, hosted by Ali Hassan of CBC’s Canada Reads.

**Hanif Abdurraqib is an American memoirist and poet known for his distinctive style of cultural and artistic criticism through the lens of music,** **sport, and contemporary American issues**. In a creative and wide-ranging talk, he will bring his unique and rare intellect to the role of nonfiction in our society, and his relationship to it as someone from an unconventional background.

He’ll then sit down for wide-ranging and free-wheeling conversation with a member of the award jury and author Tessa McWatt. Jurors said his “work sings and stings and brings truths, both personal and communal, as he voices culture and its complexities with bold, compassionate lyricism and a real sense of love,” and that is what he will bring to the stage.

***The $75,000 prize is a companion to the existing Hilary Weston Writers' Trust Prize for Nonfiction, which is awarded annually to a Canadian author for a single work of nonfiction.***

The Weston International Award recognizes the career achievement of an international author for a body of nonfiction work. Eligible international authors must have published at least three books of outstanding literary merit, in the genre of nonfiction, that are written in English or else widely available in translation.

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

title: "Public Trust" by Paul Ramírez Jonas: Interactive public artwork
location: Fort York, Branch Atrium
description:
How serious are the promises we make to one another, the vows we take, or the pledges made by our civic leaders?
Paul Ramírez Jonas’s interactive artwork,
Public Trust
, asks participants of all ages to examine the value of their word by declaring a promise that is recorded in a drawing they can keep.  That promise is then published on a large-scale marquee board and placed alongside commitments made by politicians, scientists, economists, companies, and weather forecasters, all drawn daily from headline news.
In recognition of International Day of Democracy on September 15, this interactive art event officially kicks off Toronto Public Library's Fall 2026 Celebrate Democracy series. As a vital part of our civic and democratic life, TPL is proud to host
Public Trust
in collaboration with
The Bentway
, an invitation to reflect on community engagement, civic participation, and the promise of democracy as we approach the municipal election on October 26.
Please join us at 6pm for a live talk with the artist, Paul Ramírez Jonas, also hosted at the Fort York branch. Visit the
program registration page
for more information and to register.
Check out the
KnowYourVote.TO
website and the
Celebrate Democracy
page to learn more about Toronto’s upcoming municipal election, access important voter resources, and discover activities and interactive library programs for all ages happening at a branch near you.
Public Trust
is presented by The Bentway in partnership with the Waterfront BIA and in collaboration with Toronto Public Library and Harbourfront Centre.
This event is generously supported by the McConnell Foundation.

title: Garden Sketchbook: 4-Part Workshop
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for a four-week introduction course and learn how to sketch plants outdoors at Toronto Botanical Garden!
Enjoy the beauty of TBG while learning how to sketch plants outdoors in the garden during this five-week class. You will develop observational skills and be taught techniques in line, shape, proportion and the fundamentals of colour mixing. Constructive feedback will help increase your creative confidence. Beginners welcome.
 
Art materials will be provided. Please bring a portable folding stool, wide brimmed hat and suitable footwear.
 
In the event of rain, we will move into the library and draw terrarium plants.
 
Tuesdays, September 15, 22, 29 & October 6 from 1 to 3 p.m. (four sessions).
Public $120, TBG Members $110 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Alan Li
Artist and conservationist Alan Li uses pencils, ink and paint to document the wonders of the natural world. Alan’s mission is to build connections to nature through arts-based education. Since 2015, he has been partnering with non-profit environmental organizations to teach nature focused art programs and workshops.
 
Alan was responsible for the successful launch of the Toronto Nature Sketch program in 2018, teaching all of the art lessons during that inaugural year. Nature Sketch is an initiative of Canadian artist Robert Bateman and the Bateman Foundation.
 
In 2019, Alan was a speaker at the annual Ravine Symposium at Toronto Botanical Garden. In his presentation, he shared stories behind ravine inspired artwork created by himself and a small brigade of volunteer artists. Funds raised through the sale of the artwork were donated to ravine conservation initiatives at the garden.
 
Alan currently teaches Field Sketching, Nature Drawing and Linocut Printmaking at Toronto Botanical Garden and the High Park Nature Centre.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
 
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member !
 
Additional Program Information



Please review our Refund Policy and Terms of Agreement.
For more information on accessibility at the garden please review our Accessibility Features webpage. If you have any accessibility requirements during your program please email programsupport@torontobotanicalgarden.ca.

title: Closing the Loop: Modular, Testable Postgres for AI Agents
description:
Toronto Postgres
Coding agents don’t need better instructions. They need a tighter feedback loop.

This session shows how to build that loop directly into Postgres. We’ll use `pgpm`, a Postgres package manager, to turn schemas into composable, versioned modules with deterministic dependencies, then test them against the real database with `pgsql-test` — including roles, permissions, functions, constraints, and RLS.

From there, we close the loop: **write → test → fix → push → CI/CD**.

That changes the role of testing. Tests are no longer just something humans run before shipping; they become the control system for coding agents. An agent can generate code quickly, but the database provides the deterministic signal for whether that code is actually correct.

| We’ll build a modular schema live, let an agent extend it, and let the tests decide what ships |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
|

description:
Address:

Every frontier model runs on minerals. Behind the GPUs, the servers, the cooling systems and the power infrastructure that make up a data centre sit gallium, germanium, rare earths, copper, tungsten and a dozen other inputs whose mining and refining are concentrated in a small number of countries. Countries like China, that have weaponized that dominance, restricting exports of gallium, germanium, graphite and rare earth magnets, and each time targeting a material critical to AI. Demonstrating how a supply chain chokepoint becomes a tool of statecraft.

What exactly is AI infrastructure,…

title: Good Morning, Midnight by Lily Brooks-Dalton
description:
Post-Apocalyptic Book Club - Toronto Chapter
This time we'll be reading *Good Morning, Midnight* by Lily Brooks-Dalton. Here's the blurb:

Augustine, a brilliant, aging astronomer, is consumed by the stars. For years he has lived in remote outposts, studying the sky for evidence of how the universe began. At his latest posting, in a research center in the Arctic, rumors of war arrive. The scientists are forced to evacuate, but Augustine stubbornly refuses to abandon his work. Shortly after the others have gone, Augustine discovers a mysterious child, Iris, and realizes the airwaves have gone silent. They are alone.

At the same time, Mission Specialist Sullivan is aboard the Aether on its return flight from Jupiter. The astronauts are the first human beings to delve this deep into space, and Sully has made peace with the sacrifices required of her: a daughter left behind, a marriage ended. So far the journey has been a success, but when Mission Control falls inexplicably silent, Sully and her crew mates are forced to wonder if they will ever get home.

As Augustine and Sully each face an uncertain future against forbidding yet beautiful landscapes, their stories gradually intertwine in a profound and unexpected conclusion. In crystalline prose, *Good Morning, Midnight* poses the most important questions: What endures at the end of the world? How do we make sense of our lives?

title: Summer of Fear '77: The Murder of Shoeshine Boy Emanuel Jaques
location: Toronto Reference Library, Beeton Hall, Ground floor
description:
Investigative journalist Robert J. Hoshowsky (
Outraged: the Murder of Shoeshine Boy, Emanuel Jaques
) examines the shocking abduction and murder of a 12-year-old boy that enraged a nation and forced the shutdown of Yonge Street’s sex trade.
The discovery of Emanuel Jaques’ remains on the rooftop of a Yonge Street massage parlour on August 1
st
, 1977, ignited a firestorm. Within a few days, thousands descended on Toronto City Hall demanding the reinstatement of capital punishment, which had just been abolished a year earlier.
Fed-up with countless sex shops, strip clubs and X-rated movie theatres, the public, politicians and businesses demanded change. This resulted in the most sweeping clean-up in Canadian history, which remains controversial to this day.
The author will have copies of the newly-released, second edition of his book for sale:
Outrage: the Murder of Shoeshine Boy Emanuel Jaques
(ISBN 1069337404).

ABCD Reads "[Transcription](https://tpl.bibliocommons.com/v2/record/S234C4726966)" by Ben Lerner.

([RESULTS](https://opavote.com/results/5098056250032128) of the poll for this event.)

**:: ABOUT THE BOOK ::**
"From the “most talented writer of his generation” (The New York Times), a lightning flash of a novel that is at once a gripping emotional drama and a brilliant examination of the devices, digital and literary, we use to store―or to erase―our memories.
The narrator of Ben Lerner’s new novel has traveled to Providence, Rhode Island, where he is to conduct what will be the final published interview with Thomas, his ninety-year-old mentor and the father of his college friend, Max. Thomas is a giant in the arts who seems to hail “from the future and the past simultaneously” and who “reenchants the air” when he speaks. But the narrator drops his smartphone in the hotel sink. He arrives at Thomas’s house with no recording device, a fact he is mysteriously unable to confess." (from [Goodreads](https://www.goodreads.com/en/book/show/231387262-transcription))

"An emotional drama and an examination of the devices, digital and literary, we use to store—or to erase—our memories." (from [BookMarks](https://bookmarks.reviews/reviews/transcription-2/))

location: Online: https://link.civictech.ca/zoom / Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario
description:
New technologies and organizations’ practices are regularly placing pressures and challenges on our privacy and transparency rights. This month, Civic Tech Toronto and the Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario are highlighting the work to defend, enforce, explain and update these rights. To see all September events, check our events listing on Guild. 

‎‎

Topic: Unnecessary and Disproportionate: Bill C-22 and Lawful Access

This talk will present on a recent joint brief published by the Citizen Lab and the Canadian Civil Liberties Association, which analyzed the privacy and human rights implications of Bill C-22: An Act respecting lawful access.

Brief: "(Un)forced Errors: An Analysis of Proposed Surveillance Expansion under Bill C-22, An Act respecting lawful access" by Cynthia Khoo, Tamir Israel, and Kate Robertson.

‎‎

Speaker: Cynthia Khoo \[in-person]

Cynthia Khoo is a technology and human rights lawyer based in Toronto, and a Senior Fellow at the Citizen Lab. She has developed and provides, through her legal practice and research, expertise specialized in how digital technologies impact the equality, privacy, and free expression rights of historically marginalized groups. / Website: tekhnoslaw.ca / Bluesky: cyn-k.bsky.social

‎

7:00-7:20 Welcome and Introductions

title: Reconnect, Recalibrate & Immerse in Nature: Sound Bath at the Garden
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Relax, recharge, and reconnect through a peaceful garden walk and immersive outdoor sound bath.
Step into a serene oasis where nature and sound harmonize to restore your mind, body, and spirit. Begin your journey with a guided tour of our lush botanical garden, where vibrant flora, hidden nooks, and the gentle rustle of leaves awaken your senses.
 
After the stroll, settle under the open-air pavilion for a 1-hour immersive sound bath, designed to recalibrate your nervous system and cultivate deep relaxation. Allow the resonant tones of wooden chimes, gong, flute, and tuning fork to wash over you, gently releasing tension and fostering a profound sense of balance.
 
This experience is perfect for anyone seeking:
 


stress relief and nervous system reset—a mindful connection with nature
a sensory journey through sound and space
moments of introspection, calm, and rejuvenation


Whether you are a sound healing enthusiast or simply craving a tranquil escape, this event invites you to breathe, listen, and reconnect. Come harmonize with nature and yourself in this enchanting outdoor setting.
 
What to bring:
 


Floor mat (blanket or pillow also welcome)
Water
Journal
Pen


Wednesday, September 16, 8:30 to 10 a.m.
Public $70, TBG Members $60 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Natasha
Join certified sound therapist Natasha for a transformative meditation experience that integrates the soothing vibrations of tuning fork chimes, immersive soundscapes through speakers, and mesmerizing astral light projections. This unique approach to meditation enhances relaxation, reduces stress, and promotes emotional well-being, allowing you to connect deeply with your inner self and the surrounding environment.
 
Benefits of this meditation experience:
 


Stress reduction: Immerse yourself in calming sounds that promote relaxation and reduce anxiety.
Enhanced focus: Tuning fork frequencies help improve concentration and clarity of thought.
Emotional balance: Experience a greater sense of peace and emotional stability.

Natasha’s love for the outdoors stems from her childhood experiences of fishing and horseback riding, which instilled in her a deep appreciation for nature. She has also formulated a safe lemongrass hair conditioner suitable for all hair types, inspired by her desire for better ingredients in personal care products. 
Natasha works alongside the CNIB, a cause close to her heart. Her late maternal grandmother lost her vision, and this experience fuels Natasha’s passion for building community and helping others connect with their true sense of purpose. She is also a program instructor at the Toronto Botanical Gardens. In addition, her company works closely with CAMH to provide personal care products (including our lemongrass hair conditioner) to the at-risk and vulnerable population. 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden 
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member! 
Additional Program Information 




Please review our Refund Policy and Terms of Agreement.
For more information on accessibility at the garden please review our Accessibility Features webpage. If you have any accessibility requirements during your program please email programsupport@torontobotanicalgarden.ca.
To learn more about the Toronto Botanical Garden and our programs, please review our list of Frequently Asked Questions.

title: Google AI Essentials: Online Learning Circle
description:
Curious about artificial intelligence or want to learn practical AI skills for work and personal use? Join our staff-facilitated learning circle to complete the self-paced Google AI Essentials specialization.
This 10-hour introductory-level specialization, offered through Coursera, is available for free to learning circle participants. It is made up of five courses, each containing four units that consist of short videos, articles, assignments and a short multiple-choice quiz.
By completing the specialization,
you will learn:
How AI works
How to write effective prompts
How to use generative AI tools responsibly
How to identify AI's potential biases and avoid harm
How to stay up to date with AI news
After you complete the course, you earn a Google certificate and a badge to share with others
Learning Circles are study groups guided by
library staff for people who want to complete the Google AI Essentials specialization together in a welcoming space:
Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials.
Participants are expected to commit to attending all four learning circle sessions.
No AI experience is required.
How to Joi
n a Learning Circle:
Register once on the first session of this event series, in order to attend all sessions.
Please sign up with a
valid email address
.
A valid TPL library card is required for online circles.
Attend all four sessions online via Zoom, September 9, 16 and 23.
Registration is a two-step procedure. First, participants must complete their registration through this page. After this step, library staff will follow up to request additional information in order to complete the registration.

title: Indigenous Medicine Workshop: Cedar Salve

The program will be capped at the first 15 participants.
Tanya Gluvakov is a mixed Mohawk woman from Toronto with family and "roots" from Six Nations of the Grand River in Oshweken, Ontario. She also leads several projects that bring the resurgence of medicines and accessibility to urban communities

title: London Curious Wanderers Author Talk
location: Ben McNally Books
description:
[at Ben McNally Books]
Join us at Ben McNally Books as we host Jack Chesher, the author of the
London Curious Wanderers
series.
London: A Guide for Curious Wanderers
London: Hidden Corners for Curious Wanderers
About the Books
London is famous for its museums, each one full of treasures and relics – but the biggest museum in the capital is the city itself.
From the stories behind unusual street names, to the trees in our parks; railings made from recycled WWII stretchers, to shrapnel damage on walls; the hidden symbols on post boxes, to prehistoric tree trunks – there is a rich history hidden in the oft-overlooked details of the city's streets, gardens, parks and buildings.
This richly detailed and beautifully illustrated book provides a miscellany of historic features and curiosities to spot as you wander around the capital. Whether you’ve always wondered why there are cattle troughs on your route to work, why bollards often look like upside down cannons or wanted to know what a Victorian stink pipe is – this book will provide the tools to decipher London’s secret code, and introduce you to a treasure trove of hidden spots to explore.
The book comes complete with maps so you can spot these details yourself on walks through the capital.

So, pop on a sturdy pair of shoes and get ready to turn the city into the museum you never knew you had.
About the Author
Jack Chesher grew up in Essex, and exciting day trips to London have always been part of his life. After graduating from Bristol University, where he studied history, he finally took the plunge and moved to the capital in July 2020. title: Bridging Minds: Menopause and Brain Health – Memory, Thinking and Dementia Risk
description:
Menopause can affect many aspects of health, including how we think and feel. But what do we actually know about its effects on memory and thinking, and is there a connection between menopause and dementia later in life?
In the first of two Bridging Minds webinars to focus on menopause, join Alexis Reeves, Scientist at Women’s College Hospital, to explore what current research tells us about menopause and brain health. Learn about changes in memory and thinking that can happen during menopause, whether they continue afterward, and what researchers are learning about factors that may influence brain health and dementia risk later in life.
What to Expect
Menopause and your health:
Setting the stage for what we know about this immensely important life transition, and it’s impacts of longer-term health
Memory and thinking during and after menopause:
Do symptoms related to memory, concentration or thinking “bounce back” after menopause?
Menopause and brain health later in life:
Explore what researchers know about how factors such as the age at perimenopause, the type and severity of symptoms, and menopausal hormone therapy may be related to brain health and dementia risk later in life
Bio:
Alexis Reeves is an epidemiologist, scientist at Women’s College Hospital Research and Innovation Institute and assistant professor at University of Toronto. Her research focuses on the causes and consequences of disparities in accelerated aging.  Much of her work has focused on the health of women, especially Black women, as they enter into life-stages, such as the midlife menopausal transition where cardio-metabolic risk is high and disparities can exacerbate.  Overall, her work aims to advance health equity and support minority populations to thrive as they age.
About the Series
Bridging Minds: Health & Science Conversations is a partnership between the Toronto Public Library and Women’s College Hospital. Through monthly discussions led by experts from across different clinical areas and scientific disciplines, this series provides attendees with the opportunity to engage directly with our topics and speakers and empowers communities to navigate health and science topics confidently, inspiring a future of informed decision-making.
Learn more:
https://www.womenscollegehospital.ca/bridging-minds/

title: Storytelling Through Beadwork
location: Lillian H. Smith, Room B/C
description:
Uncover the hidden symbols and intricate meanings found in beadwork in this interactive talk with Cree-Métis artist, Marissa Magneson.
Marissa will explore beadwork as a form of storytelling and expression, revealing layers of history, identity, culture, and spirituality.
Attendees will gain a deeper appreciation for this art form that transforms beads into vibrant narratives!
Marissa Magneson is a Cree-Métis artist, photographer, and educator with Red River roots, holding a BFA (Hons.) and a Master’s in Indigenous Studies with a focus on beadwork as visual storytelling. Her work centers on decolonizing education, community strengthening, and reclaiming cultural practices, and she has been nationally recognized as a 2023 Vanier Scholar and one of York University’s Top 30 Alumni Under 30. Currently a PhD candidate at York University, Marissa also teaches, creates, and facilitates workshops. She is inspired by the legacy of her Métis grandmother, Elaine Jessop (Desjarlais).

location: OCAD University Auditorium,100 McCaul St, Toronto, ON M5T 2W7, Canada
description:
Things Fall Apart: In Conversation with Allison Glenn, Curator, Toronto Biennial of Art 2026

Join us!

September 16, 2026
7:00pm
100 McCaul Street, Auditorium (Room 190)
OCAD University

FREE: Get your ticket here https://www.eventbrite.ca/e/in-conversation-with-allison-glenn-curator-2026-toronto-biennial-of-art-tickets-1999034475930?aff=oddtdtcreator

The fourth edition of the Toronto Biennial of Art https://torontobiennial.org/ , Things Fall Apart, curated by Allison Glenn https://www.allisonglenn.com/ , unfolds through a set of propositions anchored by the question: What can we learn from artists who explore rupture as an ontological tool or a way of understanding?

Relying on the shared geographies of the Great Lakes as a place of departure, this Biennial traces relationships between the expansive but interconnected waters of the Great Lakes region and over sixteen global waterways that span five continents.Things Fall Apart considers ideas of syncopation and disruption through the lens of shared thematics that emerged from artists’ voices: diaspora through movement and migration, syncretic traditions, notions of borders, water networks, maritime histories of empire, corporeality, calls to action, global climate justice, genocides, speculative and science fictions, material memory, the transformation of knowledge, and both water and land as conceptual links.

Things Fall Apart is organized in three parts: a central exhibition that grounds itself in methodologies of collectivity, sovereignty, reflection, and refusal; a series of performances and artist-led programming that invites embodied engagement with these practices; and a collaboratively curated gathering. Join this year's curator to learn about the process of leading to Things Fall Apart.


Allison Glenn:

Allison Glenn is a New York-based curator and writer focusing on the intersection of art and public space, through biennials, special projects, public art, & major new commissions. For seventeen years, Glenn has been devoted to realizing ambitious and experimental exhibitions with a wide range of contemporary artists working across the globe. She is Curator of the 2026 Toronto Biennial of Art, titled Things Fall Apart, opening September 26, 2026, and Curator of Espacio Central, as part of the CARA Platform.

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

title: Nature of Chi: Tai Chi & Qigong at the Garden (8 sessions)
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us Thursday mornings for Tai Chi and Qigong at the Garden!
“CHI” is the universal life force that runs through our bodies. Routine practice of Tai Chi and Qigong can help cultivate our internal energy flow. “NATURE OF CHI ”combines seasonal Tai Chi and Qigong to help restore, regulate, and awaken our natural body functions. Classes will include warm-ups, breath work, a variety of Tai Chi and Qigong movements that connect to the 5 elements, and a short guided meditation to help relax, calm, and balance mind, body, and spirit. “NATURE OF CHI” Tai Chi is suitable for all age groups, fitness levels, and does not require any previous Tai Chi or Qigong experience.
 
This is an outdoor program. In the case of poor weather, classes will be moved indoors.
 
Thursdays, September 17 through November 5 from 8:30 to 9:30 a.m. (8 sessions)
Public $120, TBG Member $96 (plus applicable taxes and fees)
 
About David Leopold
Sifu David Leopold has been practicing, studying, researching, and teaching martial and healing arts since 1994.
 
In 1999, Sifu David achieved his black belt in Shaolin Kung Fu. Since 1999, Sifu David has received numerous certifications in Tachi had and weapon forms and seven Qigong routines. In 2009, Sifu David received his Usui Reiki master certification from the Naturopathic School of Medicine in Toronto.
 
In 2012, Sifu David travelled to China to compete in the International Wushi Competition in Shanghai. He brought home 2 gold and a bronze medal.
 
By combining all these modalities and experiences, Sifu David brings a unique style of teaching that includes technique, philosophy, and practicality. Sifu David’s approach to teaching is relaxed and he believes Taichi and Qigong practice should be useful in everyday life and enjoyable to do.
 
Sifu David has a passion for martial and healing arts. His holistic approach to wellness includes physical, emotional, spiritual and nutritional well-being. Sifu David continues to improve his skills as a practitioner, teacher/mentor, and hopes to teach for the rest of his life.
 
Sifu David’s words of wisdom:“To be a master of what you do, you must first be a master unto yourself.”

title: Blue Willow in the Clouds: The Architectural Reuse of Willow Ware in 19th-Century India
location: Gardiner Museum, 111 Queen's Park, Toronto, ON, M5S 2C7, Canada
description:
Blue Willow in the Clouds: The Architectural Reuse of Willow Ware in 19th-Century India            
                                    
                                
                        
                                                
                                                        Get Tickets                        
                                            
                
                    
    



	

    
         
    




	


			

    
        
             
                
                    Thursday September 17, 2026
12:00 pm – 1:00 pm ET
Online via Zoom 
Part of the Gardiner Signature Lecture Series
The Robert and Marian Cumming Lecture 
Speaker: Heeryoon Shin, Assistant Professor of Art History and Visual Culture, Bard College 

                
                    
    



    
         
    




    
        
             
                
                    The popular Willow pattern seen on Staffordshire transferware found a new life as ornamentation in palace interiors in 19th-century India. Set into walls in their original form or broken into flat, rectilinear pieces, Blue Willow plates and their luminous blue-and-white surface effectively framed gods and kings, creating a multisensory space. 
Taking the late 19th-century sites of Juna Mahal in Dungarpur and Junagadh Fort in Bikaner as points of departure, this online talk will explore how the design and materiality of Willow ware and its display acquired new meaning and purpose in Indian palaces. 
Evoking the tradition of tiled ornamentation and the display of ceramics in the chini khana (“China room”) in India, while also referencing European porcelain rooms, the transferware-covered walls reveal the complex cultural negotiations and material and political aspirations of 19th-century India. By examining the Indian reuse of Willow ware, which has been largely studied in terms of Western responses to Chinese export porcelain, this talk complicates the conventional narrative of West looking East and instead highlights the nonlinear and multidirectional flows of ceramic culture.

                    Heeryoon Shin is Assistant Professor of Art History and Visual Culture at Bard College. Her current book project explores architectural revival, mobility, and cross-cultural exchange in eighteenth-century India through the lens of temple architecture in the pilgrimage city of Banaras. She is also developing a second project on the global circulation of blue-and-white ceramics and their interaction with local production and use in South Asia.

title: Sept 17 - ADAS, AV, and AI Meetup
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join our virtual meetup to hear talks from experts on cutting-edge topics across AI, ML, and computer vision.

**Time, Date and Location**

Sep 17, 2026
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/adas-av-and-ai-meetup-september-17-2026)**

**AI for Autonomous Driving: From Data to Decisions**

Building reliable automated driving systems is as much a data and engineering challenge as a modeling one. In this talk, Tin will share perspectives from his work at Porsche AG on applying modern AI methods across the autonomous driving development process, from making sense of large-scale driving data to understanding and evaluating how AI-based systems behave on the road. He'll discuss lessons learned from real-world development, where today's approaches shine, and where hard problems remain for the ADAS and AV community.

*About the Speaker*

[Tin Stribor Sohn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/tin-stribor-sohn/) is a PhD Student at Porsche AG and Karlsruhe Institute of Technology in the area of Foundation Models for Scenario Understanding and Decision Making in Autonomous Robotics, Tech Lead at Data Driven Engineering for Autonomous Driving, Prior: Master in CS at University of Tuebingen with focus on Computer Vision and Deep Learning and co-founder of a software company for smart EV charging

**Advancing ADAS and Autonomous Vehicle Development with Multimodal Data**

ADAS and autonomous vehicle systems rely on increasingly complex data from cameras, video, LiDAR, radar, and other sensor streams. In this session, Murilo will introduce Voxel51 and explore how the latest multimodal capabilities in FiftyOne help teams bring these data sources together to better understand their datasets and model behavior. He’ll discuss how unified workflows for visualization, search, curation, and evaluation can help ADAS and AV teams uncover challenging scenarios, investigate model failures, and build safer, more reliable autonomous systems.

*About the Speaker*

[Murilo Gustineli](https://www.linkedin.com/in/murilo-gustineli/) is a Machine Learning Engineer at Voxel51 working at the intersection of representation learning and computer vision. He holds an M.S. in Computer Science from Georgia Tech, where he co-leads the DS@GT Applied Research & Competitions group, advancing machine learning research through competitive challenges and peer-reviewed publications.

**From Survey-Grade Maps to Physical AI: Scaling Real-World Data for Training and Simulation**

Physical AI systems are increasingly constrained not by model architectures, but by the availability of scalable, high-fidelity real-world data. This talk explores how Dynamic Map Platform transforms survey-grade road assets collected across 1.8 million km of roads worldwide into training- and simulation-ready datasets, including point clouds, imagery, HD maps, road surface models, and 3D Gaussian Splatting representations.

We will discuss why geometric accuracy, semantic understanding, and real-world diversity are critical to building robust autonomous driving systems. Attendees will learn how real-world geospatial data can be structured and scaled for AI training and simulation workflows.

*About the Speaker*

[Ryoto Miyake](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ryoto-miyake/) is a Software Engineer at Dynamic Map Platform, where he works on transforming large-scale geospatial data into AI-ready datasets for training, simulation, and validation, such as HD maps and 3D Gaussian Splatting. With a background in transportation engineering, he works closely with automotive manufacturers and industry partners to bridge large-scale real-world mapping data with next-generation AI and mobility systems.
