title: Paper Quilling: Sunflower Workshop
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for a fun-filled workshop on paper quilling and learn how to make amazing art with paper strips!
Join us for a relaxing and creative paper quilling workshop where you’ll transform simple paper strips into beautiful art. Guided by experienced instructor Deepa Krishnan, you’ll learn essential quilling techniques as you create a vibrant sunflower on a 5″ × 7″ canvas.
 
Personalize your artwork by choosing your favorite colours and adding your own creative touches, making each piece truly one of a kind. Whether you’re completely new to paper quilling or have some experience, this beginner-friendly workshop is designed for everyone. You’ll leave with a stunning handmade sunflower that’s perfect for brightening your home and celebrating the beauty of the fall season.
 
All materials provided. Suitable for adults and children ages 10 and above.
 
Thursday, September 17, 2 to 4 p.m.
Public $50, TBG Members $45 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Deepa Krishnan
Deepa Krishnan is a self-taught artist specializing in the art of paper quilling, which involves manipulating narrow strips of paper to create exquisite designs. She discovered this art form when she was looking for a creative outlet from her engineering job. She was so amazed by the possibilities and beauty of paper quilling that she decided to pursue it as a full-time career. Since then, she has been passionately mastering this technique and has created many artworks drawing inspiration from nature, music and travel. She cuts the paper strips in different widths to add depth and dimension to her creations. She loves to play with the colours and experiment with the quilling techniques to create her own distinctive style. Deepa believes that anyone can learn this art form, regardless of their age or skill level and she hosts many workshops to spread the joy of quilling. She enjoys seeing her students discover their own creativity and style in paper quilling.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!

title: Curator's Talk: Unearthing Vindolanda
description:
Date: Thursday, September 17, 2026
Time: 7:00 pm – 8:00 pm
Location: Bata Shoe Museum, 327 Bloor St. W.
Tickets: $25 
Join us for a fascinating evening with archaeologist Elizabeth Greene, whose extensive research at Vindolanda has helped reshape our understanding of life on the edge of the Roman Empire. 
Drawing on her firsthand excavation experience, Greene will take us behind the scenes of the dig: what it feels like to carefully unearth history layer by layer, the challenges of working in the soil of northern England, and the thrill of discovering objects that have not been touched in nearly two millennia. 
Located just south of Hadrian’s Wall, Vindolanda is one of Britain’s most extraordinary Roman sites, famed for its remarkably preserved artifacts—including leather shoes, writing tablets, and everyday objects that offer intimate glimpses into ancient lives. Whether you’re passionate about archaeology, Roman history, or the stories hidden beneath our feet, this is an evening not to be missed 
BUY YOUR TICKETS  
Agenda
6:30 pm – Doors Open
7:00 pm – Lecture Begins
8:00 pm – Lecture Ends/Galleries Open
9:00 pm – Museum Closes 

ABOUT ELIZABETH GREENE: 
 
Dr. Elizabeth Greene is Associate Professor and Canada Research Chair in Roman Archaeology at the University of Western Ontario in Canada. She has excavated at the site of Vindolanda and researched aspects of the museum collection since 2002, and is currently working on an extended research project on the Roman shoes and leather objects from the site.  

Please review our Terms and Conditions in advance and check in with Visitor Services upon arrival. Questions? Email us info@batashoemuseum.ca anytime.

title: Paul Theroux: True North, On the Road in Canada
location: Toronto Reference Library, Appel Salon, Second Floor
description:
For more than half a century, Paul Theroux has traveled the globe and chronicled its far corners with curiosity, wit, and an unflinching eye. He joins us on stage to discuss his newest book,
True North
, in which he turns that eye to Canada.
In True North, Theroux travels widely through remote villages, multicultural cities, and sweeping landscapes that have defined modern Canada. Along the way, he speaks with farmers, refugees, writers like John Irving and Michael Ondaatje, and Indigenous leaders such as Tanya Talaga, listening as Canadians reckon with identity, belonging, and patriotism, often in response to the jabs and provocations of their southern neighbor.
With the empathy of a companion and the sharpness of a cultural critic, Theroux delivers a timely, vivid travel narrative that reveals Canada as never before — diverse, unsettled, and alive with stories.
In conversation with acclaimed writer and critic Charles Foran.

description:
Magnus Hara: The Light of Day            
                                
    



	

	


			
Events
	







    
        
             
                
                    September 18 – November 8, 2026
The Hilary and Galen Weston Foundation Hall. Ground Floor
Included with admission. Free for Gardiner Members. 

                
                    
    



    
         
    




	


  Get Tickets



  Become a Member






    
         
    




    
        
             
                
                    This exhibition features the work of Magnus Hara, recipient of the 2024 Gardiner Museum Prize, awarded to a graduate of the Sheridan College Ceramics Program. Through alteration and combination of intimately known forms, this collection of vases is a reclamation of joy and autonomy after grief, loss, and injury. Intuitive assemblies of form, pattern, and configuration are used to question and confront the familiar in a dynamic visual language. 

                
                    
    



    
         
    




    
        
                            
                    
                        
                    
                
                       
            
                
                    About the Artist
                    
                
                
                    Magnus Hara
                    
                
                
                    Magnus Hara is a non-binary multimedia craftsperson with a specialty in ceramics currently living and working in Hamilton, Ontario. With a background in production pottery, they use their skills on the wheel to create functional and sculptural pieces for the home with a focus on the idea of mundane intimacy. Hara studied Ceramics at Mohawk College before obtaining a Bachelor of Craft and Design from Sheridan College. Most recently, they completed an artist residency at the Society for Contemporary Craft in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.

title: Birding with Beni: Fall Birding
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for a fall birding nature walk!
Fall migration is well underway! Join TBG Horticulturist and avid birder Sasan Beni for an engaging walk through the gardens and Wilket Creek Ravine, as you seek out the wildlife that call this place home. Learn how to identify the many different species passing through and how you can help them in their journey.
 
Bring your binoculars for a better view (we will have extras on hand) and a mug/thermos for a warm beverage and post-birding chat.
 
As with any wildlife tour, the spotting of birds and other wildlife is not guaranteed and is not within the control of the tour guide. Please be patient and considerate. The tour will not be rescheduled due to a lack of bird sightings. The tour will only be rescheduled due to inclement weather.
 
Meet at the TBG main entrance, just outside the George and Kathy Dembroski Centre for Horticulture.
 
Friday, September 18, 8 to 10 a.m.
Public $22, Members $20 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Sasan Beni
Sasan Beni is a writer turned Horticulturist. He graduated with a diploma in Environmental Landscape Management from Seneca College in King City, worked for the Toronto Zoo as a seasonal gardener, and joined TBG in 2020 as a seasonal Horticulturalist. His home is a revolving door of tropical plants. Beni is also passionate about birdwatching and wildlife photography. In the last three years, he has led many guided birdwatching walks around Toronto and has written several articles for Trellis magazine illustrated with his nature photographs.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!
 
Accessibility
The walk will be at a leisurely pace throughout, following designated pathways and trails, but sometimes covering uneven terrain and steep inclines. Dress appropriately for the weather and walk slowly. Wearing layers is recommended. Closed-toed shoes are required. We will begin promptly. NOTE: This program occurs rain or shine (save for cases of extreme weather); please dress appropriately for the weather.

description:
Start your day with a nature hike through the gardens on your way to an outdoor yoga class at Toronto Botanical Garden.
Following the wonderful response to our last class, we’re doing it again! This all-levels yoga class combines mindful movement, breath awareness, and relaxation techniques to support strength, mobility, balance, and overall well-being.
 
Participants will be guided through accessible yoga postures and movement practices designed to help release tension, improve flexibility, and cultivate a sense of calm and connection. The natural beauty of the Garden provides the perfect setting to slow down, recharge, and enjoy a mindful start to the day.
 
Enjoy some herbal tea from the Garden before heading back to The George and Kathy Dembroski Centre for Horticulture to complete your visit. Feel free to bring a mug for tea!
 
No prior yoga experience is required. Modifications and options will be offered to accommodate a range of abilities and experience levels.
 
Please bring your own yoga mat and any props that help you feel comfortable and supported in your practice.
 
Please meet at the TBG main entrance, just outside the George and Kathy Dembroski Centre for Horticulture promptly at 10:45 a.m. Participants will be led on a short walk to the yoga location.
 
This is an outdoor yoga class. In the case of dangerous or severe weather, the program will be moved indoors. Please note, the walk up to the grounds includes a short walk uphill with some steps and uneven slopes. If you have any accessibility concerns, please reach out to programsupport@torontobotanicalgarden.ca.
 
Friday, September 18, 10:45 a.m. to 12 p.m.
Public $20, TBG Members $15 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Laura Bianchi
Laura is a certified yoga therapist and yoga teacher based in Toronto. She offers group yoga classes and individualized yoga therapy sessions that support physical, emotional, and nervous system well-being through safe, adaptive, and thoughtfully guided practices.
 
Laura has experience working with diverse populations and specializes in creating accessible, inclusive classes that help participants improve mobility, reduce stress, build resilience, and cultivate a deeper connection with their bodies. Her teaching style is warm, supportive, and focused on meeting each person where they are, making yoga approachable and beneficial for people of all ages and experience levels.

title: Ghost Stories of Toronto: Colonial Spectres
description:
"It’s only by our lack of ghosts we’re haunted," the poet Earle Birney once said of Canada. But the truth is that people have been telling supernatural tales in Toronto since the city was founded, and long before that, too. We'll begin this series of talks with author Adam Bunch by heading back to the city's founding days as a settlement to explore ghost stories from the early 1800s and see what they have to reveal about colonialism, the War of 1812, and the fears of the settlers who lived in this place two hundred years ago.
About this event's guest:
Adam Bunch
Read More:
The Toronto Book of Love
The Toronto Book of the Dead
About this series:
You can learn a lot about Toronto through its ghost stories. Whether you believe in the supernatural or not, the tales we tell about spirits and spectres illuminate the true history of the city. They're often tied to dramatic stories of death and disaster, to fascinating historic sites, and to pivotal moments that helped shape our communities. In this series of talks by author Adam Bunch, we'll explore Toronto's past through tales of ghosts, séances and hauntings. Whether it's phantom horses from the War of 1812, the strange prime minister who believed in the occult, or the ghost who was arrested by the Toronto Police Morality Squad, these supernatural stories have a lot to teach us about the history of the place we call home.

title: The History of the Eaton Centre (NEW for 2026)
description:
Toronto History Walks
**The Toronto History Walks Explorer Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!**

Most people visit Toronto's Eaton Centre to shop, and it's a great place to do just that. But few realize they are walking through one of the city's greatest stories of ambition, controversy, architecture, and change.

Join me as we step beyond the storefronts to uncover the remarkable history hidden beneath the soaring glass roof of the galleria. Discover how this world famous complex rose from a maze of Victorian streets, warehouses, theatres, and historic buildings, and learn why one of Toronto's largest redevelopment projects almost resulted in the demolition of Old City Hall and the beloved Church of the Holy Trinity.

This fascinating walking tour explores nearly 160 years of Toronto history, beginning with the extraordinary rise of Timothy Eaton and the department store that transformed shopping into the "art of shopping," almost overnight.

We'll examine the neighbourhood that existed before the Eaton Centre, meet some of the colourful characters who worked and lived here, and trace the dramatic battles between developers, preservationists, politicians, and citizens that forever changed the face of downtown Toronto. Along the way, you'll see surviving landmarks, forgotten streets, hidden architectural secrets, and public art that millions pass every year without noticing.

You'll also discover why the Eaton Centre became an international model for shopping centre design, admire its spectacular vaulted glass ceiling, and hear the stories behind the famous flock of suspended Canada geese.

We'll explore how the complex evolved through the decline of the Eaton's department store, and the arrival of new retailers, that helped redefine the downtown core. From engineering marvels to architectural triumphs, this is the story of how a shopping mall became one of Canada's most recognizable landmarks.

Whether you're a lifelong Torontonian, a first-time visitor, a lover of architecture, or someone fascinated by urban history, this tour offers a new perspective on a place you thought you knew. By the end of our walk, you'll never look at the Eaton Centre the same way again, I promise. Come and discover the hidden history beneath the glass canopy, and experience one of Toronto's most compelling stories.

This event is for all levels and walkers, there are a few steps here and there to navigate, but mostly on one level.

This walking tour begins on the steps of Old City Hall at the northeast corner of Bay Street and Queen Street West, and
has a ticket price of $15.00 per person.

**Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

title: Google Prompting Essentials: Online Learning Circle
description:
Ready to develop the skills to use generative AI (GenAI) tools effectively and responsibly for work and daily life? Join our staff-facilitated Learning Circle to complete the self-paced Google Prompting specialization. Essential
Prompting Skills
: How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results.
Everyday Work Tasks:
Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more.
Data & Presentations:
How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data.
Advanced Techniques:
How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time.

title: 2026 Toronto Colloquium in Medieval Philosophy: A Celebration of Deborah Black
location: Jackman Humanities Building 100
description:
Please join us for the 2026 edition of the University of Toronto Colloquium in Medieval Philosophy. 
Program
FRIDAY, SEPTEMBER 18
Session I (3:30 – 6:00 pm) 
Martin Pickavé (University of Toronto): Welcome
Stephen Dumont (University of Notre Dame): Deborah as a Scholar, Friend, and Colleague
Peter Adamson (LMU Munich): What’s Truth Got to Do with It? Logic as (Mere) Instrument in Philosophy of the Islamic World 
SATURDAY, SEPTEMBER 19
Session II (9:30 am – 12:00 pm) 
Ginger Hegedus (Western University): Kalamic Mutations in the Thought of al-Qirqisāni and Ashʿarī
Kara Richardson (Syracuse University): Avicenna on Nature as a Stable Efficient Cause 
Session III (1:45 – 4:15 pm) 
Luis Xavier López-Farjeat (Universidad Panamericana): Ibn Bājja on Imagination and Intellection: An Alternative Interpretation against Averroes’s Reconstruction
Taneli Kukkonen (NYU Abu Dhabi): Averroes on Past and Future Infinity 
Session IV (4:30 – 6:15 pm) 
Stephen Ogden (University of Notre Dame): Avicenna’s Emanationism and Aquinas’s Critique
Deborah Black: Closing Remarks 
All sessions are free and open to the public and will be held in Room 100 of the Jackman Humanities Building (170 St. George Street). 
The colloquium is sponsored by the Department of Philosophy, the Collaborative Specialization in Ancient and Medieval Philosophy, the Centre for Medieval Studies, and St. Michael’s College. 
Organizers: Reza Hadisi, Peter King, Jon McGinnis, and Martin Pickavé.

title: Wildlife-friendly Fall Gardens
location: Fairview, Room 201, 2nf Floor
description:
At this time of year, many people admire the fall colours but also feel the need to rake and dispose of leaves, cut dead stems, and remove fallen branches. But what if this tidying up negatively affects our gardens and pollinators? While we may not see the bees and butterflies during the fall and winter, they are still around!
In this presentation, learn about how to maintain and protect wildlife habitat even throughout the colder months, and how “leave the leaves” can help nature come back stronger the next season.
Presented by
Dorte Windmuller
, a Butterflyway Ranger of the
David Suzuki Foundation (DSF)
as part of TPL’s environmental program series, Our Fragile Plant.

location: Sanderson - Closed, Main Floor Program Room
description:
Due to renovations the Bookclub will take place in Scadding Court Community Center in Room 4 (same building), participants will be responsible in sourcing copies of the monthly titles themselves as the branch will not be open to the public during this time. We apologize for the inconvenience!
Become a page-turner by joining the Between the Lines Book Club! Here, we embark on a new chapter with every read, diving into a world of endless possibilities. From gripping thrillers to heartwarming coming-of-age tales, or a sprinkle of fantasy adventures, there's something for everyone. Whether you're a die-hard fan of one genre or love mixing things up, you'll find a place here to discuss, share, and connect with fellow readers. Ready to explore different worlds and discover your next favorite book? Join us and let's turn the page together!
Friday September 18
: The Covenant of Water by Abraham Verghese
The Covenant of Water
by Abraham Verghese is a sweeping, richly detailed novel set in Kerala, India, that follows a family across generations as they live with a mysterious condition in which some family members have a fear of water. Beginning in the early 1900s, the story unfolds through the lives of several generations, connecting their personal struggles, relationships, and secrets in unexpected ways. Blending family history, love, loss, medicine, faith, and cultural traditions, the novel explores how the past shapes generations to come. Verghese brings the landscape and people of Kerala vividly to life, while weaving together themes of resilience, sacrifice, healing, and the complicated bonds of family. It is an immersive and emotional story that invites readers to become deeply invested in the lives of its characters and the mysteries that connect them.

title: Wilder Series: The Provoking Lake Loop
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/provoking-lake)**

**Most people take two days to walk around Provoking Lake. We are doing it in one.**

This one's part of our Wilder series, our lineup of challenging adventures for those chasing bigger, more grueling and more rewarding days out.

We’ll be taking on Loop 1 of the Algonquin's Highland Backpacking Trail, The trail circles Provoking Lake through classic Algonquin forest, roots, rock, and enough elevation change to keep your attention the whole way around, covering 21.5km by the time we're back at the car.

You will pass a couple of lookouts over the lake and the surrounding hills, and long stretches where the loudest thing around is a woodpecker or your own footsteps. Backcountry campsites dot the shoreline the whole way around, a quiet preview of what a multi-day trip on this trail could look like down the road.

Twenty one kilometres of Algonquin backcountry, done in a day. Are you up for it?

**Due to increased demand for daily vehicle permits in fall, all members will be required to take our transport for this adventure. The cost of transport is included in the cost of this adventure.**
‍
**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to [info@wildernessunion.com](mailto:info@wildernessunion.com)

**Highlights**
**Provoking Lake Lookouts:** A couple of clearings along the loop open up over the lake and the surrounding hills.
**A Real Physical Test:** 21km and over 800 metres of climbing in a single day. Come ready to work for it.
**Wildlife Country:** Moose and loons are regulars around Provoking Lake, keep your eyes open.

**Event cost: $130+HST (for explorer members)**
**Register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/provoking-lake)**

**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.

Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.

Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!

***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

title: Algonquin Voyageur Canoe Paddle
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/voyageur-paddle)**

**Prepare for a truly unique paddling adventure, as you take on a beautiful route in two epic voyageur canoes.**

Adapted from traditional canoes designed by Indigenous communities, these 10-person voyageur canoes were used for many years to carry people and supplies. Now, you’ll get the opportunity with a full crew to try your luck at navigating these vessels through the beautiful waters of Algonquin.

We'll meet at Algonquin Outfitters on Oxtongue Lake to begin our journey...

You’ll be split into two canoes and follow a winding, 15km route down the lake and onto the river. Be sure to watch the shoreline for dense pines and the odd cottage tucked into the trees. Getting a big canoe to move well takes real teamwork, and with two crews on the water, don't be surprised if the paddle turns into a friendly race. It's a full day on the water with the people beside you, calling out strokes, laughing at whoever falls out of rhythm, and figuring out together how to steer 8 metres of canoe.

**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to info@wildernessunion.com

**Highlights**
**The Voyageur Canoe: **An 8 metre canoe paddled by a full crew instead of a pair.
**Sandy Beaches:** Discover lakeside sandy beaches contrasting the granite cliffs.
**Oxtongue Lake: **Sandy shoreline and clear water at the doorstep of Algonquin Park

**Event cost: $110+HST (for explorer members) + $60 optional transport available.**
**Register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/voyageur-paddle)**

**About Wilderness Union**

title: History of Aviation: Air Wars (LECTURE ON THE GO)
description:
Toronto History Walks
**The Toronto History Walks Explorer Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!**

We have an amazing "Lecture on the Go" series for 2026. New topics and fascinating stories abound! Join us and learn about the world and keep active and warm and cool during the winter and summer months!

I started this walking classroom when we were under that horrible cloud called Covid. This series was popular and helped people get back into society and life. **This is part two of the Aviation series that will debut in August 2026 with the Lecture on the disaster at Tenerife**!

The "Lecture on the Go" Series is open to members who have purchased the YEARLY MEMBERSHIP PASS, it's free for those members. If you wish to attend a lecture and you are not a yearly pass member then the price **per** lecture is $20.00.

In this second part of *History of Aviation: Lecture on the Go* series, we move from the daring pioneers of early flight into the era when aviation truly changed North America forever. By the 1920s and 1930s, airplanes were no longer just fragile machines flown by adventurers. Air mail routes connected distant cities, passenger airlines began appearing across the continent, and aircraft designers pushed technology forward at a breathtaking pace.

The skies over North America became a laboratory of innovation, where speed, distance, and reliability improved year after year. It was an exciting time filled with record-breaking flights, famous pilots, and the growing belief that aviation would shape the future.

The Second World War transformed aviation more dramatically than anyone could have imagined. Aircraft became central to modern warfare, leading to what many historians call the first true “air wars.” Massive bomber fleets crossed oceans, fighter aircraft battled for control of the skies, and radar and engine technology advanced at incredible speed. Companies like Boeing and Lockheed Martin grew alongside the military demand for aircraft production. Air power became a decisive force, changing military strategy forever. Yet even during wartime, aviation inspired people with stories of courage, skill, and technological achievement that captured the imagination of the public across North America.

Canada also played a remarkably important role in the growth of aviation during this era. The Canadian aviation industry expanded rapidly during the war years, building training schools, manufacturing aircraft, and supporting Allied operations across the Atlantic. Programs such as the British Commonwealth Air Training Plan turned Canada into one of the world’s great pilot-training countries. Canadian companies like de Havilland Canada became known for designing rugged aircraft capable of operating in harsh northern conditions. Bush planes and bush pilots like Max Ward (Wardair) opened remote regions of the country, connecting isolated communities and supporting exploration, mining, and medical transport. Aviation helped shape modern Canada in ways that many people today rarely stop to consider.

After the war, aviation entered the jet age and North America became the focus of global aerospace innovation. Commercial air travel exploded in popularity as families could suddenly cross the continent in hours rather than days. Airports expanded into enormous transportation hubs, while military aviation evolved into the era of supersonic fighters, strategic bombers, and space exploration. The story of aviation in North America is ultimately a story of ambition, and invention, a reminder that humanity has always looked toward the sky and imagined what might come next. But this story has plenty of mystery and thrills, so come aboard and take to the skies. So if you love to fly then this is your boarding pass!

In this lecture on the Go,
Upcoming topics in the 2026 series:

\*Philosophy 1: Great Minds of the Western World: Goethe to Kant! - (August 2026)

World: Chuang Tzu to Dalai Lama - (July 2026)

So book your plans now!

description:
Design and create a beautiful fall-themed glass plate!
Cool crisp air? Colourful leaves? Think fall. Capture the fall colours in this fused glass class. Using Glassline Paint, coloured frit, and stringers, Millean Kung will guide you through creating your own fall scene on a 6” x 6” plate. You will learn about the various types of glass, tools involved, and techniques used.
 
All materials will be provided. This course welcomes beginners.

Saturday, September 19, 1 to 3 p.m.
Public $115, TBG Members $110 (plus applicable taxes and fees)
 
About Millean Kung
Born and raised in Toronto, Millean discovered pottery and glass art more than 10 years ago. Currently, she is a member of the of the Potter’s Studios in Scarborough and is involved in the Small Business Arts Mentorship Program at Glasstronomy Studios in Markham. Since retiring from education, Millean has devoted her time to her pottery and glass art. She is the sole proprietor of her business, “1 in a Millean”, and participates in a number of arts and crafts shows.
 
Millean also loves to garden and is a member and a volunteer at the Toronto Botanical Garden. To keep her schedule busy, she enjoys cooking and baking.

A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!

description:
Experience Toronto
**On Saturday September 19th,** join me to **see Being Heumann at the 51st edition of the Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF)**. *Heumann* is the opening and closing show for TIFF 2026. Featuring a breakout performance by Ruth Madeley and Oscar nominee Mark Ruffalo, this inspiring historical drama from Oscar-winning filmmaker Siân Heder (*CODA*) celebrates the paradigm-shifting activist Judy Heumann, “Mother of the Disability Rights Movement.” Every bit as moving as her Best Picture Oscar winner, *CODA*, *Heumann* tells the remarkable true story of the woman who led a world-changing campaign for accessibility. Judy Heumann rallied a handful, then dozens, then hundreds of ordinary Americans with disabilities to push the US government to live up to its commitments. Though set in the past, *Being Heumann* couldn’t be more pertinent to our present. title: Noronic Disaster! Was it Arson? Interactive Game and Tour (77th ANNIVERSARY)
description:
Toronto History Walks
\*\***The Toronto History Walks Explorer Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!\*\***

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

**This special anniversary tour commemorates the burning of the Noronic in Toronto harbour on the evening of September 16-17, 1949! Seventy Seven years ago**

First it was **Ambrose Small** and my team of brilliant detectives who tried to figure it out. The walkers on this tour just about cracked the case. Well done my detectives.

And then the case that shocked Canada and the world, the murder of **Burt Massey!** That was a tough assignment with 15 characters all wanting their time in the sun! But now a new assignment for my brilliant detectives. The Harley Karulis Detective Agency needs your help once again! Here is the folder with all the information, down below! Your assignment awaits! Keep reading.......

Saturday September 17, 1949 in the early hours. A small harmless fire in a closet on C Deck erupted into an inferno that destroyed the Canada Steamship Lines, Noronic. It was Toronto's greatest disaster.

On this tour we will meet and hear the stories of passengers, crew and firefighters who responded on that fateful night. Our goal is to try and figure out the true story of what happened on C Deck in that same closet. Was it an accident or was it done on purpose? If it was indeed arson, then why?

The Noronic was built by the Northern Navigation Company, a subsidiary of the Richelieu and Ontario Navigation Company. It plied the waters of the Great Lakes since its first trip in 1913. It carried millions of happy holiday makers, but things were coming to an end. Could this be the motivation to end the service. Points to ponder!

The car was King or Queen, and the second world war was over and attitudes were "a changing," quickly! The days of the passenger cruise ships on the Great Lakes were seen as part of the old world.

Are you up for this interactive game once again?

This walking tour/game takes participants back in time to 1949 Toronto, and explores the many sites associated with this disaster and the personalities involved. You will be introduced to 15 historic characters and each has their own dark secrets, it will be up to you to uncover the truth.

**This tour DOES not require a PRESTO card! All the sites are centred around the southern section of the downtown core and harbour front!**

Our walk begins outside the **Westin Harbour Castle Hotel** on Queen's Quay and Bay Street just east of the Jack Layton Ferry Terminal on Queen's Quay East at the front doors of the hotel. A video on the disaster will follow in the comments to introduce you to this fascinating piece of Toronto history!

This tour has a ticket price of $15.00 per person. Please get your tickets early if you would like to attend as this tour has a limit of 25 participants!

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket price when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

description:
Enjoy an evening of soulful vocals, intricate rhythms, and musical exchange at the Aga Khan Museum.

Bringing together three accomplished artists of classical music, this vocal recital celebrates the expressive depth of raga through voice, harmonium, and tabla. Acclaimed khayal vocalist Warren brings decades of experience with Indian, Western, African, and African-American music. He is joined by harmonium accompanist Hardeep and distinguished tabla artist Kiran.

Together, the musicians create an intimate and dynamic musical exchange, balancing the meditative qualities of raga with the energy of rhythmic interplay and improvisation.

title: Hello Fall Colours: Dorset Hike & Lookout Tower
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/dorset-hike-and-lookout)**

**Not every good trail makes it into a guidebook, and this hidden gem sure hasn't.**

Tucked just southwest of Algonquin, it's a route we keep close for our members: rolling rock outcrops, quiet beaver ponds, and wide ridges that open into sweeping views when you least expect them. In September, the whole forest turns to a radiant display of red, orange, and gold; the kind of colours that makes you stop mid-stride. Welcome to fall in Ontario.

We'll cover 7.5 km at a comfortable pace, with plenty of time to take it in before stopping for lunch at one of the best views on the route. It's a moderate hike, and a solid choice if this is your first time out on trail.

From the trailhead, it's a short drive to Dorset. The tower was first built in 1922 as a fire lookout and rebuilt in 1967 into the structure that stands today. Climbing to the top puts you level with the treetops and gives you a panorama of the hills and lakes around Lake of Bays, all dressed in their fall colours. It's one of Ontario's most recognizable lookouts, offering a totally different perspective after a morning spent within the tree canopy.

**Please note that anyone not taking the WU transportation will need to purchase their own tower access pass.**
‍
**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to [info@wildernessunion.com](mailto:info@wildernessunion.com)

**Highlights**
**The Lookout Tower Climb:** The observation deck sits 142 metres above Lake of Bays, with a 360 degree view over the surrounding hills and lakes.
**A Trail Off the Map:** A quiet, little-known route kept for Wilderness Union members, far from the lineups that build up around Dorset in the fall.
**Fall Colours:** Red, orange, and gold scattered across the Canadian Shield.

**Event cost: $75+HST (for explorer members) + $60 optional transport available.**
**Register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/dorset-hike-and-lookout)**

**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.

Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.

Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!

***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

title: English Spanish Language Conversation
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Friday
* Saturday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** here **»** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
**Héctor Fuentes**

title: Toronto's Art Deco 1929-1939: VOLUME 1 and 2 (SPECIAL EXTENDED TOUR)
description:
Toronto History Walks
\*\***The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!\*\***

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

Art Deco is all around us.

Streamlined Modern or Art Modern are two other fascinating ways to say the same thing. Whichever way you plan on saying it, Art Deco buildings tell a rich story of optimism and positivity during one of the most darkest decades in history, the great depression of the 1930s!

This walking tour explores our built environment of our downtown core. Toronto Stock Exchange built in 1937, along with the Royal York Hotel and the Canada Permanent Trust Company are prime examples. But others line Spadina Avenue during the challenging years of the depression, but also during the tensions which were bubbling in the Garment Industry. Art Deco buildings were centre stage!

These buildings tell a story that goes beyond style into the heart of the Toronto story itself!

Built at the height of the roaring 1920s and 1930s, the bubble was about to burst however, and the depression was just settling in. But a new style would set the tone, and it was called Art Deco!

Toronto built some of its most enduring buildings, and left a built legacy of Art Deco during the 1930s which should be treasured and protected. Losing any of these treasures would surly be a loss to the community. They tell a rich and inviting story about the growth of Canada, and Toronto!

This walking tour is for all walking levels. Please dress for the season, and hope to see you there.

Please meet under the **clock tower** of the Queens Quay Terminal at 207 Queens Quay West on the south side just west of York Street! We end on Spadina and Richmond Street!

This tour has a ticket price of $15.00 per person.

title: SOLD OUT: Botanical Cyanotype Printmaking
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for a fun-filled afternoon of cyanotype printmaking!
Please join us for a delightful afternoon of cyanotype printmaking! In this hands-on workshop you’ll create a small collection of original cyanotype prints inspired from plants at Toronto Botanical Garden. Our instructor will demonstrate every stage of the process and explain how you can continue creating cyanotype prints year-round at home.
 
Beginners welcome. All materials are included. Please wear old clothes or bring an apron.
 
Sunday, September 20, 1 to 4 p.m.
Public $65, TBG Members $55 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Alan Li
Artist and conservationist Alan Li uses pencils, ink and paint to document the wonders of the natural world. Alan’s mission is to build connections to nature through arts-based education. Since 2015, he has been partnering with non-profit environmental organizations to teach nature focused art programs and workshops.
 
Alan was responsible for the successful launch of the Toronto Nature Sketch program in 2018, teaching all of the art lessons during that inaugural year. Nature Sketch is an initiative of Canadian artist Robert Bateman and the Bateman Foundation.
 
In 2019, Alan was a speaker at the annual Ravine Symposium at Toronto Botanical Garden. In his presentation, he shared stories behind ravine-inspired artwork created by himself and a small brigade of volunteer artists. Funds raised through the sale of the artwork were donated to ravine conservation initiatives at the garden.
 
Alan currently teaches Field Sketching, Nature Drawing and Linocut Printmaking at Toronto Botanical Garden and the High Park Nature Centre.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
 
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member !
 
Additional Program Information



Please review our Refund Policy and Terms of Agreement.
For more information on accessibility at the garden please review our Accessibility Features webpage. If you have any accessibility requirements during your program please email programsupport@torontobotanicalgarden.ca.
To learn more about the Toronto Botanical Garden and our programs, please review our list of Frequently Asked Questions.

description:
Toronto History Walks
\*\***The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**

So many walkers have expressed interest in a full explanation of the dreaded PATH, so here it is. A full course on the PATH, its history and explanation. You will become a PATH specialist after this, guaranteed!

I've heard it so many times, with so many people, the common refrain, "I got lost in the PATH." If you are one of the many who have simply vanished in Toronto's underground never to be seen again, check out this popular historical walking tour.

This tour demystifies the PATH system and explains how it works in grand detail. It takes walkers through the system and points out the crucial connectors and branches within the system to effortlessly guide the lost through the maze. Once experienced the PATH will be an invaluable aid to navigating the downtown, in both summer and winter, rain or shine, hurricane or drought. You might even enjoy getting lost in the underground, lost but not forgotten.

This is the full PATH course curriculum:

Part 1: The History of THE PATH
Part2: Connectors and signboards
Part 3: Understanding the above ground connection
Part 4: Hidden paths to get one around quickly
Part 5: The Blind Spots and how to work with them
Part 6: The Maps
Part 7: Getting from here to there!

This walk is for all fitness levels and skills. This tour is indoors, so please dress for the conditions, and is considered an all-weather​ tour.

The walk begins **inside** the Atrium on Bay at the northeast corner of Dundas Street West and Bay Street adjacent to the Red Lobster restaurant!

This tour has a ticket price of $15.00 per person!

title: Beginner Crochet - September
location: Bistitchual, 266 Jane St, Toronto, ON M6S 3Z2
description: This listing is for a two session Beginner Crochet Course. The classes will be held in person at Bistitchual on Sunday September 20th and 27th from 4:00pm-5:30pm Learn the fundamentals of crochet in this two part class. We will be covering chaining and single crochet, as well as double and half-double crochets. Don’t know what any of that means? Great, you’re in the right place! We’ll provide all the materials, including a simple pattern that teaches you common terms and instructions you’ll encounter in most crochet projects. We will also discuss how to choose the appropriate yarn and hook for a project as well as where you can take your crafting after you master these basic techniques. There’s a lot to learn, and we’re excited to accompany your beginning in the wonderful craft of crochet! Materials are included! - 50g ball of worsted weight cotton in your choice of colour - 6mm crochet hook Our class size is capped at 4 people, so everyone can receive the attention they need. Mike will share lots of tips and techniques to get you well on your way. About the instructor: Tired of disposing of clothes that were still perfectly wearable, Mike (he/him) started crafting mainly as a means of mending and repair. This led him to knitting (and later crochet), which pretty much immediately became one of his favourite tools of self-expression. Please note that classes will only proceed if we have a minimum of two attendees . If the minimum is not met, there will be the option for a refund or to reschedule. There will be a four person maximum for each class. Please pre-book your spot to let us know you are coming! Cancellation Policy Classes must be paid for at the time of registration to reserve your spot. - If cancelled 48 hrs or more prior to the start of the first class will be given a store credit. Classes cancelled less than 48 hrs prior to the start of the class will not be reimbursed.

title: The OPTIONS Program - Master's Career Exploration Cohort Fall 2026
description:
The OPTIONS Program is an initiative to support all engineering graduate students and postdoctoral fellows to explore diverse career options.  
Purpose & Content  
This program is designed for Master’s students considering different career opportunities. It equips you with personal and professional skills to navigate your career exploration while complementing your technical expertise.  
You will:  

Create a Career Exploration Plan to achieve your goals 
Reflect and communicate the skills you develop in your graduate studies to move into different career options  
Join a dynamic cohort of Master’s students from different departments with diverse career aspirations. 

The program provides:  

Four, two-hour sessions 
Two career management tools to develop an individualized, career exploration plan 
A one-on-one, 30-min meeting with a career coach  
Activities designed to help you reflect and communicate on your experiences, skills, and strengths  
A Peer Success Team to support your career exploration 

Schedule  
Review the OPTIONS Master’s Schedule Fall 2026 before submitting an application to ensure you can attend all four sessions. All sessions are in-person with the exception of the one-on-one career coaching appointment.  
If you will experience a visa delay and might not be able to attend the first session on Thursday, October 1 in-person, please contact Joanne at joanne.lieu@utoronto.ca.  
Benefits  
In addition to the programming, resources, and one-on-one meeting listed above, participants who complete the program (attend three of four sessions) receive a digital certificate of completion.  
Selection Criteria  

U of T Engineering Master’s student 
Strong interest in developing personal and professional skills beyond technical knowledge 
Curious about career exploration 
Eager to participate in group discussions 
Willingness to be part of a team and support your peers’ career preparation 

Program Delivery                    
This is an interactive program (not a traditional lecture). You will participate in interactive activities and small group conversations. For online sessions, you will need to use your audio to communicate with peers and (if possible) video.  
All four sessions occur live from Thursday, October 1 to Thursday, October 22 from 1 – 3 pm ET in-person.  
Applicant Commitment 
By applying to The OPTIONS Program, I commit to attend all four sessions. Why?  

This program is designed as an integrated sequence of sessions, and you will benefit most by attending all four sessions. We recognize some session titles or descriptions might not resonate with you. We ask that you bring curiosity, patience, and an open-mind. Since 2017, we have delivered thirteen OPTIONS cohorts to over 400 graduate students and postdoctoral fellows. The MOST common feedback we receive from participants is that the individual sessions build on each other to form a comprehensive, structured career management experience. 
You are joining a cohort of 40 participants, and within this cohort you are placed in a Peer Success Team of four to five participants. Over four sessions, you will work with the cohort and your team to complete program activities and discussions. By applying to this program, you are committing to the cohort and your Peer Success Team that you will attend all sessions. 
You commit to participate and engage in conversations with your peers. In particular, for online sessions you will need a quiet space and access to your audio to participate in small discussions (and, if possible, your video). During an online session, you should not be completing work outside the program, commuting, etc. 
The Institute for Studies in Transdisciplinary Engineering Education and Practice invest a significant amount of resources and time in developing and delivering this one of a kind program to you FREE OF CHARGE. We ask that you commit to attend all four sessions AND, although not required, take advantage of the one-on-one meeting, and session materials. 
We receive more applications than the program can accommodate. By committing to this program, you are taking a spot from another student. 

Most importantly, this program is here for YOU to develop your personal effectiveness, clarify your career aspirations, and have a meaningful learning experience with a supportive community of peers and instructors. There is no homework, only optional activities to accelerate your career exploration, and no grades. We recognize life happens and there might be unexpected situations that might mean you have to miss a session. That is okay! Remember, you must attend at least three of the four sessions to receive your certificate.  
Applications Due   
Submit your application by Monday, September 21 at 12:00PM EDT.

title: Robert Wald (University of Chicago)
location: MP1318A
description:
Title: Black Holes Decohere Quantum Superpositions

Abstract: We show that if a massive body is put in a quantum superposition of spatially separated states, the mere presence of a black hole in the vicinity of the body will eventually destroy the coherence of the superposition. This occurs because, in effect, the gravitational field of the body radiates soft gravitons into the black hole, allowing the black hole to harvest "which path'' information about the superposition. A similar effect occurs for quantum superpositions of electrically charged bodies. The effect is very closely related to the memory effect and infrared divergences at null infinity.
Host: Anupam Mazumdar

title: Appreciation vs Appropriation: Reconciliation in Practice
location: Spadina Road
description:
Join Dr. Ruth Green for a discussion that explores the line between Indigenous cultural appreciation and cultural appropriation. Using real world examples like artwork, jewelry, clothing, and pow wows, Ruth will examine how non-Indigenous people can engage respectfully with Indigenous cultures and make informed, respectful choices. Attendees will learn how to reflect on representation, ownership, intent, and ceremony, while preparing to thoughtfully respond to questions about their choices.
No registration required. All are welcome.
Dr. Ruth Green (she/her) is a Haudenosaunee urban Indigequeer woman (Kanienkehaka Turtle Clan from Six Nations) who identifies as an activist-turned-accidental academic. She is an Associate Professor in the Indigenous Field of Study Program at Wilfrid Laurier University. Previously Ruth was chair of the Indigenous Research Ethics Board, special advisor to the President and the Dean on Indigenous Initiatives and Director of the School of Social Work at York University. She is a board member of Pride Toronto and a Community Council member with Aboriginal Legal Services

title: Practical 3D Print Sept 21 [Mondays - 6 Week Comprehensive]
location: TTLMakerspace, 192 Spadina Ave., Toronto, ON
description:
In this course at TTLMakerspace, you will go beyond basic 3D printing knowledge and be able to create custom designs. Learn to use CAD modelling to upgrade or build your own models, optimized for 3D print.

 
 
 
 
 
 
 Starting with manual printer control, you will progress to custom modelling and even advanced techniques such as 3D scanning and reverse engineering.

 Schedule: 

 
 Six three-hour weekly classes, Mondays 6:00pm to 9:00pm.

 
 
 
 
 
 Outcomes: 
 
 
 At the end of this course you will have achieved the following goals: 
 
 
 
- A complete understanding of the steps needed to go from concept to completed part

- Experience and comprehension of parametric 3D modelling

- Knowledge of 3D printing best practices 

- Familiarity with scanning for 3D print 

- Principles of reverse engineering and part repair

- Understanding of the properties of different 3D printing filaments

- Use cases for SLA (resin) printing vs. FDM printing 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Following this hands-on course, you’ll be certified to use 3D printers and book time with the machines at the TTLMakerspace (with your membership). You will also be able to join the growing community of TTL Makers sharing 3D printing & 3D modelling knowledge on our Discord community.

title: Virtual REGISTER: Free Women's Masterclass - Your Permission Slip to...
description:
Experience Toronto
**Note: This is for Women only (sorry guys). After you RSVP, you will also need to Register to receive your link to the event.**

On **Wednesday, September 21st,** **join me for A free women’s wellness masterclass - Your permission slip to stop existing, and start living.**
You've been waiting for permission.

* Permission to rest without earning it.
* Permission to say no without the guilt spiral.
* Permission to want more, even when your life looks good on paper.

Here's the thing, though - nobody else is coming to give it to you. The only signature that was ever required on that slip is YOURS.

In one guided session, you'll walk away with:

* The exact permission you've been withholding from yourself, named and specific to you.
* Clarity on whose voice has been running your inherited rulebook all these years.
* The truth about why waiting feels safe when it's really just well-disguised avoidance.
* A real glimpse of the woman already forming underneath your everyday life.
* And the signature moment, where you write your permission on an actual piece of paper, sign it, date it, and make it official.

Plus the piece nobody teaches. Why will power alone never holds, and what actually does.

One session. One signed piece of paper. A completely different way of moving through your life.

That's exactly what our free Your Permission Slip masterclass is about.

title: Let's Talk Depression: What It Is, What It Isn't, and What Helps
description:
Depression is one of the most common mental health conditions in the world; yet it remains widely misunderstood.
Far more than ordinary sadness or "feeling down," clinical depression (also called major depression) is a complex mood disorder shaped by a combination of factors, including genetic predisposition, changes in brain chemistry, life stress, and personal history. For many people, it can be debilitating, persistent, and difficult to recognize — both in ourselves and in those we care about.
This talk will focus on demystifying depression and offer practical, evidence-informed insights into understanding and addressing it.
What to Expect:
Understanding Depression:
This talk will explore what depression actually is (and what it is not), and how to recognize when low mood may be something more serious.
Dispelling Misinformation:
Addressing common myths and misconceptions that can prevent or delay people from seeking help.
Getting Help:
A discussion of practical ways to support ourselves and others, what to do when someone close to us is struggling, and when it may be time to seek professional care.
About Dr. Gerasimos Konstantinou
Dr. Gerasimos Konstantinou is a psychiatrist and researcher based in Toronto, where he works at the Centre for Addiction and Mental Health (CAMH) and Toronto Western Hospital. He specializes in mood disorders, particularly depression, and in advanced treatment approaches for people who have not found relief through standard medications or therapy.
He is currently an Assistant Professor in the Department of Psychiatry at the University of Toronto, an Associate Scientist at CAMH's Campbell Family Mental Health Research Institute, and leads the Mood Disorders Clinic at CAMH, which supports people facing acute episodes of depression and anxiety.
This program is presented by Toronto Public Library in collaboration with
The Centre for Addiction and Mental Health (CAMH)
.
Your Health Matters
This program is part of Toronto Public Library’s
Your Health Matters
initiative, which offers trusted health programs and resources to help people make informed decisions about their health. Learn more by exploring the
Your Health Matters web page
.

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

title: 2026 Jerome S. Simon Memorial Lectures (Barbara Vetter, Freie Universität Berlin)
location: Jackman Humanities Building 100
description:
We are pleased to announce Barbara Vetter as our esteemed speaker for the 2026 Jerome S. Simon Memorial Lectures. Dr. Vetter is a professor of theoretical philosophy at Freie Universität Berlin, and co-director of the “Human Abilities” project (www.human-abilities.de). Her work focuses on the metaphysics and epistemology of modal properties — dispositions, abilities, and so on — and their role in the metaphysics and epistemology of modality. She published Potentiality: From Dispositions to Modality with the Oxford University Press in 2015. In 2026, she received a Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz prize.  Dr. Vetter is currently working on a book that develops an agency-based approach to the epistemology of modality. 
The title of the series is “Modal Knowledge in Action.” 
More information on the three lectures to follow.

title: Postgres as a Coordinator
description:
Toronto Postgres
Trusting Postgres to store data is one thing; trusting it to coordinate work is another. This talk walks through the design we settled on — commit the durable fact inside the transaction, fire side effects after commit, and rebuild the job queue from committed rows so the chain is always the source of truth — and the real failure modes we hit getting there: an advisory-lock self-deadlock that Postgres's own detector couldn't see (half the wait cycle lived in the application), pg-boss semantics that didn't mean what we assumed, and MVCC read-then-write races. For each: the reproduction, the root cause, and the structural guard that keeps it from recurring. Because AI agents wrote and tested much of this, the talk also covers where that helped, where it quietly didn't, and the testing discipline we adopted as a result.
What you'll take away:

* A durable coordinator pattern: commit-in-transaction, side-effects-after-commit, queue reconstructable from committed rows
* Concrete concurrency failure modes on Postgres — advisory-lock scope, pg-boss singleton/priority semantics, MVCC visibility — and how to design them out
* Why the structural guard, not the one-off fix, is what makes correctness stick
* What building and testing with AI agents got right, and what needed guardrails

title: Looking Back, Moving Forward: Reconciliation in Canada
location: Palmerston, Theatre
description:
Dr. Cynthia Wesley-Esquimaux will share her observations on where reconciliation may be headed and explore opportunities for meaningful changes in our approaches to truth and reconciliation in Canada.
No registration required. All are welcome
Dr. Cynthia Wesley-Esquimaux served as Vice Provost Indigenous Initiatives at Lakehead University for three years and was appointed as the 1st Indigenous Chair for Truth and Reconciliation for Lakehead University in 2016 to the present.
Cynthia was inducted as a “Honourary Witness” by the Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada in 2014 and is Chair of the Governing Circle for the National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation at the University of Manitoba.
Cynthia is a faculty member at the Banff Centre for Arts and Creativity and continues to offer public education and training on Indigenous history and governance across Canada.
She is a member and resident of the Chippewas of Georgina Island First Nation and has dedicated her life to building bridges of understanding. She sees endless merit in bringing people from diverse cultures, ages, and backgrounds together to engage in practical dialogue and applied research initiatives.

title: Civic Meetup #561: Dark patterns 2.0: Manipulative design in the age of AI
location: Online: https://link.civictech.ca/zoom / Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario
description:
New technologies and organizations’ practices are regularly placing pressures and challenges on our privacy and transparency rights. This month, Civic Tech Toronto and the Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario are highlighting the work to defend, enforce, explain and update these rights. To see all September events, check our events listing on Guild. 

‎‎

Topic: Dark patterns 2.0: Manipulative design in the age of AI

"Dark patterns" are user interface design tactics that influence users to make choices that benefit an online service. Traditionally, dark patterns have relied on visual design elements and encouraged superficial user actions like clicking a button. However, dark patterns are now appearing in interactive dialogue between users and AI chatbots. This talk discusses why AI dark patterns may pose novel privacy risks and be especially difficult to resist – especially for young users.

‎‎

Speaker: Dominique Kelly \[joining remotely]

Dominique Kelly is a Postdoctoral Associate in the Faculty of Information and Media Studies at Western University. Her research interests include dark patterns, data privacy, and the social and cognitive effects of interacting with generative AI.

‎

Agenda:

7:00-7:20 Welcome and Introductions

7:20-7:50 Presentation and Q\&A/discussion

7:50-9:00 Breakout groups

Our weekly civic meetups bring together Torontonians (designers, coders, urban planners, government staff, mappers, policy-makers, students, communications strategists, community organizers, and more) who share an interest in making Toronto more responsive, prosperous, sustainable, and equitable through design, tech, and data.

title: Forest Bathing at the Garden
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Connect with nature and join us for a guided forest therapy walk!
Rekindle your relationship with nature on the fall equinox through a guided outdoor forest bathing walk with certified Forest Therapy guide Laura Bincik. At a slow pace and in community with other participants and the environment, you will be guided by a series of invitations throughout the experience to awaken your senses and intentionally connect with nature in the present moment.
 
We will gather briefly indoors to prepare for the walk and consider the origin of forest bathing, as well as some of the benefits of the practice. When we venture into the Toronto Botanical Garden and surrounding ravine, we will cover a loop of approx.1.5 km on paved pathways, lawns and bare ground, at times encountering uneven terrain, inclines, and declines. We will be strolling, standing, and sitting (if you wish to). Your comfort and safety are most important!
 
As this program occurs rain or shine, please dress for the weather and wear sturdy, closed-toed footwear. Long pants and shirt sleeves will help to protect against insect bites. You may wish to bring a water bottle, sunhat/glasses, walking poles, and/or a folding stool or sitting/kneeling pad.
 
As the walk ends, we will gather and partake in a seasonal tea and snacks, and taste honey harvested at Toronto Botanical Garden.
 
In the event of severe weather or environmental conditions, TBG staff will make alternative arrangements to the program.
 
Washrooms are available onsite.
 
The program is suited for adults 18+. All participants must sign a liability waiver at the start of the program.
 
Service animals welcome, but we ask that you leave your pets at home during this program.
 
Wednesday, September 23, 9:30 to 11:30 a.m.
Public $35, TBG Members $30 (plus applicable taxes and fees)
 
About Laura Bincik
Laura Bincik is a certified Forest Therapy guide with the Association of Nature and Forest Therapy. Following a career that straddled health care and education, Laura discovered that her lifelong sense of awe for the natural world could be enriched and shared with others to enhance wellbeing. Laura feels a connection to the land and the wonder of being in nature from countless hours spent exploring Toronto ravines in all seasons. An active member of Nature and Forest Therapy Canada, Laura follows the growing research on the mental and physical health benefits of Forest Bathing and is expanding her practice by connecting with local, national, and international leaders in the field.
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!
Additional Program Information



Please review our Refund Policy and Terms of Agreement.
For more information on accessibility at the garden please review our Accessibility Features webpage. If you have any accessibility requirements during your program please email programsupport@torontobotanicalgarden.ca.
To learn more about the Toronto Botanical Garden and our programs, please review our list of Frequently Asked Questions.

title: Robyn Rennie: A Discussion on Blindness Arts, Disability Culture and Creative Approaches
location: Brentwood, Community Room, Ground Floor
description:
Meet
Robyn Rennie
, an artist centering blindness arts, disability culture, and creative approaches to audio description and sensory access.
Rennie’s exhibition, SEEING BEYOND, previously presented at the Orillia Museum of Art and History, includes paintings, each accompanied by a life-size tactile replica and a custom-built audio device. Attendees who are blind or with low vision are invited to explore the tactile surface while listening to Rennie’s own authored description of the work.
With the goal of supporting broader uptake across galleries and museums, Rennie has made the device schematics open source and co-developed “Artcessible,” a QR-based smartphone app for accessing audio description, while continuing to critically examine the economic and material barriers embedded in mainstream tech solutions.
This event explores:
Blindness arts as a generative cultural framework rather than an accommodation model
Audio description as a creative, interpretive, and aesthetic practice
The design and fabrication of tactile replicas and dedicated audio devices
Open-source access technologies and questions of affordability and infrastructure
Free. Register for a reminder.
Doors open at 5:30 pm for attendees to explore paintings. At 6:00 pm, Rennie will discuss their practice, the exhibition and devices in use, and how more public institutions can integrate disability-led technological innovation into their programming.
This program is produced by
Ontario Culture Days
in collaboration with
Tangled Art + Disability
as Producing Partner and Toronto Public Library. This program is supported by the City of Toronto.
Ontario Culture Days is a province-wide festival made possible through the support of its foundational partners, the Province of Ontario and the Ontario Arts Council. We acknowledge the support of the Canada Council for the Arts.

title: Python Toronto September Meetup: September 23 at Fulfil
description:
Python Toronto
Python Toronto is back! Join us for our September meetup at **Fulfil**, hosted in the Industrious common area at **30 Adelaide Street East (near Yonge/Adelaide)** on Wednesday, September 23, 2026 at 6:00pm!

If you are interested in giving a talk, we'd love to have you! Please fill out this form – [Submit a Python Toronto talk](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfpNKB0Sbs893xp72M4TxmYGrTyLm4Nh1SSXnCqChP9mx6_9A/viewform?usp=header)! Talks are typically short, 5 to 10 minutes, and up to 20 minutes if you've really got something nice to present, and on any topic that would be interesting to a room of Python people. This can be a Python library that has helped you, a research paper you've enjoyed, or an interesting application of AI.

The Python meetup is a casual, community-oriented meetup hosted by companies that use Python in Toronto. Talks are short, informal, and sometimes ad-hoc.
Space is limited! Register now to hold your spot.

**When / Where**

* When: September 23, 2026, 5:30pm to 8:30pm. Talks will begin around 6:00pm.
* Where: Fulfil - Industrious common area, 30 Adelaide Street East, Toronto, ON (near Yonge/Adelaide)

Come early to enjoy snacks and drinks provided.

**Code of Conduct**
Python Toronto is dedicated to providing a welcoming, harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of gender, gender identity and expression, age, sexual orientation, disability, physical appearance, body size, race, ethnicity, religion (or lack thereof), or technology choices. We do not tolerate harassment of any form. Sexual language and imagery is not appropriate for this venue, including talks, workshops, parties, Twitter and other online media. Meetup participants violating these rules may be sanctioned or expelled from the meetup (without a refund where applicable) at the discretion of the meetup organizers.
