title: Planting Bulbs in the Fall for Spring Glory
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for an engaging demo on all things bulbs!
Planting bulbs in the fall will bring glorious rewards in your spring garden. Learn what to plant from tulips to garlic, how to plant them and yes, even a few pointers on squirrels!
 
Wednesday, September 23, 6:30 to 8 p.m.
Public $20, TBG Members $15 (plus applicable taxes and fees)
 
About Joanna Blanchard
Joanna Blanchard has been a member of the Toronto Master Gardeners for just over 15 years. She was introduced to horticulture and gardening almost from birth, since her father was a botany professor and her mother a plant pathologist! Throughout her childhood the talk at the dinner table was often about plants, and visiting gardens and garden centres were part of daily life. Despite her best teenaged efforts to repel the gardening bug she was unsuccessful! 
 
As soon as Joanna came to Canada from the UK, she got going with houseplants, flower boxes and books about plants. Moving into a house with a garden expanded the possibilities, and her gardening efforts have progressed from there. 
 
After several decades of gardening successes and many failures, she loves to share her passion for all things horticultural. 
 
Joanna is a past coordinator of the Toronto Master Gardeners and past president of the Leaside Garden Society. She is a member of the Greater Toronto Bulb Society, and has a particular love for the early-spring bulbs that brighten our lives after a long, cold winter.
 
About Toronto Master Gardeners
Toronto Master Gardeners (TMG) is a volunteer not-for-profit organization that shares current, science-based horticultural information with the gardening public through various channels, including in person, in print, through the media, and online. Committed volunteers support and inspire the community, and continually update the sound knowledge required to help them. Learn more and ask your questions Toronto Master Gardeners – Helping Gardeners.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!

title: Secrets of Rosehill Reservoir
location: Deer Park, Upstairs in room 204
description:
Rosehill Reservoir and David A. Balfour Park are the largest green spaces in midtown Toronto. Join photojournalist Ian Darragh for an illustrated talk celebrating this much-loved park.
You will learn about the many environmental benefits of urban parks; Toronto’s unique ravines; local history, and how Rosehill Reservoir is a key component of Toronto’s pioneering public drinking water system which saved thousands of children from outbreaks of typhoid and other waterborne diseases.
Ian Darragh is a former editor-in-chief of Canadian Geographic and writer for National Geographic. He contributed
two feature articles
about

title: A Chorus of Connection ft. Choir! Choir! Choir!
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
The evening will explore the theme of harmony and finding the collective beauty in individual voices.
Make the most of your
Connect IRL
experience by coming before or staying after the featured event. Grab a drink or snack at the bar. Try out one of the engagement activities available, including this event's
Con
versation
Station
:
Music
Caf
e
, where you can take a moment or two to connect with a stranger through the topic of music.
*****
Join us
in
the Appel Salon for a Chorus of Connection
with
Choir! Choir! Choir! founders, Daveed
Goldman
and
Nobu Adilman
,
in performance and conversation with Craig Pike and host Elamin Abdelmahmoud
.
For one evening, the Appel Salon becomes a choir. Daveed Goldman and Nobu Adilman will teach a song to a room full of people who have never sung together, and you'll hear a crowd turn into something that sounds and feels like a community. Between songs, Goldman and Adilman will be joined by That Choir Artistic Director Craig Pike to talk about why choirs matter, and what it tells us about the kinds of gatherings our city needs more of.
What is it about singing together that cuts through isolation so effectively? How does harmonizing with people we've never met create bonds that outlast the song? And what can an institution like the public library learn from a model built entirely on radical, no-barrier participation.
Come for an evening where strangers become a choir, and a choir becomes community.
About this event’s guests:
Choir! Choir! Choir!
Craig Pike
Elamin Abdelmahmoud
***
Warm-up Voices Workshop | 5:30 - 6:30 pm
This workshop will explore music in a new way while you connect with others in the room (no musical background or experience is necessary). Registration will open for this very soon.
The Music Caf
é!
| 5:30 – 6:30 pm & 8:00 – 9:00 pm
Pull up a chair at the Music Café, where the conversation starters are about the songs that made you cry, the album that got you through a breakup or the lyric you still can't get out of your head. Prompt cards on artists, genres, memories and moods will be available. This is a low-stakes way to bond with a stranger over shared taste (or gloriously different ones). Take a seat, swap a song story, and leave with a new favourite recommendation.
Connect IRL
is not your average series of events, workshops and activities, but a real chance to connect with other Torontonians in meaningful and sometimes unexpected ways. Through conversation stations meant to spark one-on-one conversations, or hands-on engagement activities and workshops before the featured event, participants can explore the value of connection and community.

title: Surviving Dementia Care: The Realities of Family Caregiving (Author Talk)
location: Don Mills, Auditorium
description:
Surviving Dementia Care
is a compassionate and insightful guide for anyone navigating the challenging journey of caring for a loved one with dementia. Drawing on research from information studies, literary studies, and interviews with family caregivers, this book reimagines dementia care – not as a set of skills to master, but as a deeply human experience to endure and understand.
​Author and Professor Emeritus D. Grant Campbell will address the experiences of families who are caring for a loved one who is living with dementia, including the various points of stress, as well as the various points of joy, and ways in which caregivers learn to survive the experience. Major topics include understanding the diagnosis, communicating with the loved one, choosing an assisted living facility, and using music and the arts as a means of connection.

title: Research Round: Extending the Utility of a Digital Microfluidic Based Omics (DISCO) Platform for Single Cell Proteomics
location: Zoom
description:
Savina Cammalleri is a Ph.D. student at the U of T’s Institute of Biomedical Engineering and is currently conducting her research at the Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences within the Molecular Neurobiology Group. 
Her work explores the extension of a digital microfluidic-based single cell omics (DISCO) platform for single-cell proteomics. By leveraging digital microfluidics to manipulate individual cells and samples, the platform aims to enable more efficient and scalable analysis of proteins at the single-cell level. 
This research has the potential to expand the capabilities of single-cell proteomics by providing a flexible approach for studying cellular heterogeneity and molecular processes. By further developing the DISCO platform, Savina’s work aims to contribute new tools for high-resolution biological analysis and ultimately advance our understanding of complex cellular systems.

title: Sept 24 - AI, ML and Computer Vision Meetup
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join our virtual meetup on September 24 to hear talks from experts on cutting-edge topics across AI, ML, and computer vision.

**Date, Time and Location**

Sep 24, 2026
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/ai-ml-and-computer-vision-meetup-september-24-2026)**

**How Do Mercedes-Benz AI Principles Drive our Innovation?**

At Mercedes-Benz, our AI Principles guide every step of innovation, emphasizing responsible use, safety and reliability, explainability, and the protection of privacy. These principles go beyond statements and actively shape how we design, test, and deploy AI systems in real-world automotive and enterprise settings. In this talk, I will present how these principles inspired our recent research on when reusing LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) is effective. By combining theoretical analysis with synthetic data as a proxy for enterprise scenarios, we uncovered the strengths and limitations of modular AI components under constrained data access. Our findings provide practical guidance on when reused LoRAs could deliver high-quality results.

*About the Speaker*

[Mei-Yen Chen](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mei-yen-chen-22937787) is a Senior Data Scientist at Mercedes-Benz Tech Innovation GmbH in Germany with 10 years of industry experience in AI and data solutions. She leads early-stage AI projects across business functions and collaborates with research institutions on machine learning and responsible AI.

**Region Tokens as the Visual Primitive: From Recognition to World Modeling**

Patch-based tokenization has become the default interface between vision encoders and downstream models, yet patches carry no semantic structure and scale poorly with resolution and temporal extent. This talk presents a research program centered on replacing patch tokens with region-level representations — semantically dense tokens grounded in visual entities rather than arbitrary grid crops.

I will describe RELOCATE, REN, and T-REN, a progression of methods that produce region tokens via pooling, train them with region-level objectives, and extend them to video with temporal coherence. I will then present ongoing work integrating region tokens into VLMs to directly expand visual context capacity, and preliminary results on future region trajectory prediction as a foundation for world modeling.

The broader thesis is that region-level tokens are a more natural unit of visual computation than patches, and their advantage compounds as task complexity, resolution, and temporal horizon increase.

*About the Speaker*

[Savya Khosla](https://www.linkedin.com/in/savyakhosla/) is a second-year Ph.D. student at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, advised by Prof. Derek Hoiem and Prof. Alex Schwing.

**Leveraging Text-To-Image Diffusion Models for Consistent Set-to-Set Generation**

Image collections are humans' primary way of capturing the world, yet advances in generative editing remain largely inapplicable to this modality. We address this gap by introducing Match-and-Fuse - a zero-shot, training-free method for consistent set-to-set generation from image collections that share a common visual element but differ in viewpoint, capture time, and surrounding content.
Our key idea is a unified graph-based framework that combines dense correspondences with an emergent prior in text-to-image diffusion models to generate coherent canvases. We achieve state-of-the-art consistency and visual quality, and unlock new creative capabilities for content generation.

*About the Speaker*

[Kate Feingold](https://www.linkedin.com/in/katefeingold/) is a PhD student in Computer Vision at the Weizmann Institute of Science. Her research sits at the intersection of generative models, 3D/4D perception, and multimodal learning, focusing on problems where vision meets other modalities or paradigms in creative tasks.

**Yield Estimation of a Coffee in a dense environment**

This presentation provides a detailed workflow related to coffee yield estimation in a dense environment. With photos of pre-harvest coffee plants from a couple of coffee estates, details related to pre-processing, annotation to detect regions of interest (ROI), object detection training and inferencing results with various Yolo models and finally segmentation with SAM2 and Yolo\*-seg with training and inference results to determine the count of raw, pre-mature, mature and over-mature coffee berries and finally the yield of the entire estate. All this is based on real world data captured on iPhone and android phones.

*About the Speaker*

[Raghu M. Rao](http://www.linkedin.com/in/raghumrao) is a consultant working on applications of computer vision AI models. He was previously with AMD and Xilinx. He has a Ph.D. in Wireless Communications from UCLA and is a Senior Member, IEEE. His current interests are in applications of AI for agriculture, health care and wireless communications.

title: Documentary Screening: Wilfred Buck
location: Palmerston, Theatre
description:
He’s from the “fresh-out-of-the-bush, partly civilized, colonized, displaced people,” and he’s here to take us to the stars. Lisa Jackson’s portrait of Cree Elder Wilfred Buck moves between earth and sky, past and present, bringing to life ancient teachings of Indigenous astronomy and cosmology to tell a story that spans generations. Adapted from Buck’s rollicking memoir
I Have Lived Four Lives
, the film weaves together stories from his life, including his harrowing young years of displacement and addiction. Seamlessly fusing present-day scenes with cinematic re-enactments and archival footage, this intimate yet expansive documentary takes us on an inspiring journey to the space beyond, and to the spaces between us all.
2024, 96 minutes.
This screening is presented in collaboration with the National Film Board of Canada, which is Canada’s only public producer and distributor of Canadian films and series.
Drop-in.

title: Shedding light on the dark side of the Universe
location: St. Lawrence
description:
The standard model of cosmology tells us that the Universe is mostly made up of ‘Dark Matter’, with normal matter contributing only about 15% of the total budget. However, direct detections have not yielded any results about the nature of this mysterious dark matter, leaving us with only indirect means of inferring its existence and distribution. I will try to answer tantalizing questions about its nature, and how it may have helped shape the Universe.
Presenter: Pratika Dayal
Special thanks to the Dunlap Institute for Astronomy & Astrophysics at the University of Toronto.

title: Canoe Camping in Killarney 2
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/killarney-camping-2)**

**Dive into the Killarney backcountry with this beautiful and beginner friendly canoe camping adventure.**

We're heading to Bell Lake, on the quieter east side of the park, for a weekend that mixes an easy paddle-in camping trip and an incredible hike to Silver Peak, the highest point in Killarney.

Friday, we'll paddle the short 2.5km crossing to our backcountry site, set up camp, and spend the afternoon settling in. The rest of the afternoon is yours to spend how you like. If you want to learn to pitch a tent, get a fire going properly, or handle a canoe, we'll show you. If you'd rather find a rock in the sun and do nothing, that works too.

Saturday, you can chill around camp or paddle over and hike Silver Peak, the highest point in the park. It's a roughly 11km round trip, starting on an easy rolling trail before a steep, hands on scramble up exposed quartzite for the final push. At the top, you're rewarded with a 360 degree view over Killarney's white ridges and out to Georgian Bay. Trust us, you won’t get many views in Ontario that are better than this!

Both nights, we'll eat around the fire and fall asleep under some of the clearest skies in Ontario. Killarney's stargazing is genuinely other-worldly. On a clear night you'll see the Milky Way and more stars than you knew existed. Sunday, we pack up and paddle back out.

By Sunday, you'll have spent two days swimming, paddling, and sleeping under the stars, surrounded by Killarney's unmistakable landscapes.

What's included

* Professional & certified guides
* ‍All camp meals, cooking equipment and mess kits
* ‍Tents
* Canoe rentals

Sleeping bags and sleep pads can be rented from WU for a small fee.

**Highlights**
**Silver Peak Summit:** The highest point in Killarney, with sweeping views over the range and out to Georgian Bay
**Stargazing:** With some of the darkest skies in Ontario, the Milky Way is in full view on a clear night
**Lake Swimming:** Cool off in clear water, or take the canoe out for a closer look at the shoreline

**Event cost: $455+HST (for explorer members) - $70 optional transport available.**
**Register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/killarney-camping-2)**

**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.

Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.

Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!

***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

title: Horror Classics on Film: Pulse
description:
Join author Allison Rumfitt and filmmaker David Prior as they discuss Kiyoshi Kurosawa's techno-thriller masterpiece with host Adam Nayman.
In this first instalment of Toronto Public Library's virtual series on Horror Classics on Film, writer and critic Alison Rumfitt, filmmaker David Prior, and host Adam Nayman discuss Pulse, Kiyoshi Kurosawa's sinister techno-thriller film.
Imagining a world where the internet becomes a breeding ground for malevolent spirits, the film's artistry lies in the spine-tingling power of suggestion rather than a barrage of blood and guts. This conversation will explore the lasting relevance and lingering imagery behind the film.
About this event's guests:
Alison Rumfitt
is a writer and cultural critic. Her two horror novels Tell Me I'm Worthless and Brainwyrms push the boundaries of both taste and form to the shock of readers everywhere. She has written for Little White Lies and Dazed, and interviewed new Doctor Ncuti Gatwa for Rolling Stone. She's considered herself a fan of Doctor Who ever since her father played her the theme song to scare her when she was about five years old.
David Prior
is an American filmmaker, best known for his work on the cult horror film The Empty Man, and television series such as Voir and Guillermo del Toro's Cabinet of Curiosities. He has also directed and produced making-of documentaries for films, most notably the works of David Fincher and Michael Bay.
Adam Nayman
is a critic, teacher, and author, whose books include critical surveys of the Coen Brothers, Paul Thomas Anderson, and most recently, in Mind Games, the filmmaker David Fincher. He is a regular contributor to The Ringer, a lecturer at the University of Toronto's Cinema Studies Institute, and he has written on film for The New Yorker and The New York Times.
Read more:
Tell Me I'm Worthless
Brainwyrms

title: Bringing Quine and Lewis Back Together
location: Jackman Humanities Building, Room 418, 170 St. George Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5R 2M8, Canada
description:
Speaker: Barry Loewer (Rutgers) 
This talk examines connections between Quine’s epistemology of science and Lewis’ metaphysics of science and their different conceptions of naturalness. I develop a metaphysical account of nomological modalities and fundamental properties Lewisian in spirit but dispensing with his possible worlds and his version of naturalness in favor of probabilities and a Quinean notion of naturalness. This account, called “the Package Deal Account of laws and chances” (PDA), is constructed out of Quine’s epistemology of science. The result is an account of the metaphysics of laws and other nomological modalities that combines features of Quines’ epistemology and Lewis’ physics and brings their views closer together.

[https://torontoadventures.ca/all-adventures/music-shows-on-the-river/](https://torontoadventures.ca/all-adventures/music-shows-on-the-river/)
Single Kayak (seats 1 person) : $49.95 +taxes
Tandem Kayak (seats 2 people) : $89.95 +taxes
Regular Canoe (seats 2 people) : $79.95 +taxes
Large Canoe (seats 3 people) : $99.95 +taxes
Stand Up Paddleboard (1 person) : $49.95 +taxes

**What's Included:**

* Boat(s)
* Paddle(s)
* PFD(s) “Lifejackets”
* A concert right on the river!
* Our experienced staff to help you every step of the way!

**What to Bring:**

* Dress for the weather!
* Sunscreen, Sunglasses & Hats, are all recommended for sunny days!
* We recommend securely fastened footwear (footwear is not required for SUPs).
* Blanket to keep you cozy during the show
* Snacks & Drinks (Non Alcoholic)
* Don’t forget your Cameras!

**[Google Link Directions](https://torontoadventures.ca/directions/#humberriverlocation)**
**[Cancellation Policy](https://torontoadventures.ca/faq/#cancellation)**[ ](https://torontoadventures.ca/faq/#cancellation)

We hope to see you out on the water!

title: Robert Harris: Agrippa
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
TPL presents bestselling novelist Robert Harris in conversation with Ian Brown at the Toronto Reference Library's Appel Salon.
What does it cost to build an empire, and what does it cost the men who build it for someone else? In his gripping new novel
Agrippa
, Robert Harris returns to ancient Rome to chronicle the tale of Agrippa, the commoner who will become the merciless agent of Emperor Augustus’s ambition. Now fifty, ailing, alone, and betrayed by his wife's infidelity, Agrippa retreats to his villa on the Bay of Naples to write his memoirs. But to stir up the past is dangerous, especially when that past includes the epic conflict with Mark Antony and Cleopatra, the great naval battle of Actium, and decades spent as the loyal shadow to a man history remembers as a god.
Join one of the world's most acclaimed historical novelists for an evening of ambition, empire, and the perilous friendship at the heart of Rome's transformation from republic to autocracy.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this event’s guests:

title: Frontenac Fall Colours Hike
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/fall-colours-frontenac)**

**A true member favourite returns! While the crowds flock to Algonquin to view fall colours, Frontenac is where it's really at.**

By late September, the first maples along this loop are already turning red and gold against bare granite, weeks ahead of peak colour further south. That granite is part of the Frontenac Arch, a two-billion-year-old ridge connecting the Canadian Shield to the Adirondacks, and it's what gives this loop its particular look in fall.

The Cedar Lake South Loop runs about 9km through a mix of open granite, rooted forest trails, and genuine wetland: expect boggy sections, small ponds, and stretches where the water clearly has the upper hand on the trail.

Frontenac sits at an ecological crossover point, where northern species like spruce and balsam fir grow next to southern hardwoods like sugar maple, red oak, and yellow birch. That mix means a wider range of fall colour than you'd get from a single-species forest: deep red, burnt orange, and gold, all held together by the seasonal consistency of the dark green conifers.

By the time we're back at the vehicles, you'll have spent the day walking through some of the best fall colours eastern Ontario has to offer!

**Self drivers please note** \- Frontenac is at least a 3hr drive and requires a $15 day pass \- you're strongly recommended to choose the transport option for this trip\. The day pass is included for anyone riding in the van\.
‍
**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to [info@wildernessunion.com](mailto:info@wildernessunion.com)

**Highlights**
**Stunning Fall Colours:** Red and gold hardwoods press right up against bare granite, the loop's sharpest colour contrast.
**Doe Lake Lookout:** A gap in the trees opens onto the full length of Doe Lake, framed by granite shoreline and turning hardwoods.
**Away from the Crowds:** Lesser known spot to enjoy the Fall colours.

**Event cost: $75+HST (for explorer members). Optional transportation available.**
**Register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/fall-colours-frontenac)**

**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.

Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.

Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!

***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

title: L'univers sombre et magnifique
location: North York Central Library, Room 1, 2e étage (2nd floor)
description:
Depuis des millénaires, les êtres humains contemplent le ciel nocturne et s'interrogent sur l'origine de l'univers. D'où vient-il ? De quoi est-ce fait? Où va-t-il? Dans cette présentation,
Renée Hložek
vous parlerai de cet univers — à la fois sombre et magnifique — et de la manière dont nous utilisons les télescopes pour en percer les secrets.
Renée Hložek
est cosmologiste sud-africaine et professeure agrégée au Dunlap Institute for Astronomy & Astrophysics de l’Université de Toronto. Ses recherches portent sur les origines et l’évolution de l’Univers, notamment le fond diffus cosmologique, l’énergie noire et la matière noire. Elle participe à d’importantes collaborations internationales, telles que l’Atacama Cosmology Telescope, le Simons Observatory et le Vera C. Rubin Observatory. Elle a reçu la médaille du roi Charles III pour la communication d’idées scientifiques, ainsi que la médaille Rutherford et la bourse Arthur B. McDonald du Conseil de recherches en sciences naturelles et en génie du Canada.

**Join us on our Full Moon Night Paddle event!** Use the following link to book your spot on our Full Moon Guided Night Tour: [https://torontoadventures.ca/all-adventures/full-moon-guided-tour/](https://torontoadventures.ca/all-adventures/full-moon-guided-tour/)

See Toronto’s Humber River like you’ve never seen it before!

Enter Toronto’s calm, meandering Humber River at King’s Mill Park North. We paddle down as the full moon guides our way to the mouth of Lake Ontario and towards a beautiful view of Toronto’s skyline! We will have staff on the water in their own safety boats during this night time paddle!

*Events are subject to weather and other factors out of our control. If we must cancel or delay an event we will those booked on the [torontoadventures.ca](http://torontoadventures.ca/) website know as soon as possible.*

**Pricing (per seat), Payable online through:** [https://torontoadventures.ca/all-adventures/full-moon-guided-tour/](https://torontoadventures.ca/all-adventures/full-moon-guided-tour/)
Single Kayak (seats 1 person) : $64.95 +taxes
Tandem Kayak (seats 2 people) : $99.95 +taxes
Regular Canoe (seats 2 people) : $89.95 +taxes
Large Canoe (seats 3 people) : $99.95 +taxes

description:

Your next great conversation could start over a drink, a game, or a simple “Hi.”

Join us at Stout Irish Pub in Cabbagetown for a relaxed evening built around actually getting to know people — not just standing around in a crowded bar hoping someone starts a conversation.

Fast Friends gives you a little structure to make meeting people easier: our host guides you through short conversations and rotations, then we open things up for games, drinks and further socialising.

🎲 And yes — Stout has 50+ board games.
So once you've met the group, you can grab a game with the people you clicked with, or simply stay for another drink and keep talking.

Meet your host Kruttika, grab a drink and get comfortable. If you're coming alone, that's completely normal — we'll help you get introduced.

You'll move through a series of short, guided conversations, meeting different people along the way. You don't need to figure out who to approach or how to start — we've designed the format to take care of that.

We'll introduce a simple interactive round to help you discover the unexpected things you have in common with people you've met.
Think less “networking exercise” and more:
“Wait… you like that too?”

🎲 From 8:30 PM — Board Games & Socialising
Stay and make an evening of it.
Choose from Stout's 50+ board games, grab another drink, find a few people to play with, or simply continue the conversations that started during Fast Friends.

And if you're staying later, Stout's current After Dark Special runs from 9–11 PM, with $7 beers and $7 highballs, among other specials.

Whether you've just moved to Toronto, have lived here for years, or simply feel like your social circle could use some new faces, you're welcome.
Ages 25–45
Solo attendees welcome
New faces always welcome
This is about friendship, conversation and building your social circle — not dating.

title: Toronto Cactus and Succulent Club Plant Sale
description:
The Toronto Cactus and Succulent Club (TCSC) is pleased to invite you to our annual autumn Display & Sale, a favourite event for plant enthusiasts. The event will be held in the Floral Hall.  



For those who were unable to attend the June Show & Sale, here is your chance to make amends.  



Join us to spend the day enjoying an impressive display of unique plants from around the world, expert guidance from experienced growers, and the opportunity to connect with fellow enthusiasts. 



A wide selection of cacti and succulents will be available for purchase, including many varieties not commonly found elsewhere. Whether you are an experienced collector or new to these fascinating plants, there is something for everyone. 



We hope to see you there! 



Sunday, September 27th, from 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

title: Barbecue and Hike through Tommy Thompson Park.
description:
These Boots Are Made for Hiking
Location: Meet at the entrance of Tommy Thompson Park -Leslie Street Spit
**It's time to have some fun!**
What better way to celebrate the end of Summer with a barbecue by the lake. Join us for burgers and drinks **under the tents** and on the water at Ashbridges Bay for burgers and drinks!
After a 8km hike at Tommy Thompson Park we will head to Ashbridges Bay for burgers- veggie and meat.
Feel free to bring alcoholic beverages, andboard games - We will have a beach ball.

Tommy Thompson Park is a man-made urban wilderness and wildlife sanctuary built on the Leslie Street Spit, stretching 5 kilometers to Lake Ontario.
Managed by the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority, this unique park offers a peaceful escape from the city with a mix of wetlands, meadows, and trails.
A unique place near downtown Toronto to experience nature, and *one of the best places for bird-watching in the city*, with more than 300 recorded species!

title: The Invincible - Stanisław Lem
description:
The Sci Fi Book Club
Hi everybody,

September's pick was just as popular as *Blindsight* on our survey. Our outer-space mystery series continues with our highest-voted classic in a while, Stanisław Lem's eponymous *The Invincible* is supposed to be a wild ride.

As a reminder, we skip our October book each year to highlight the [Brooklyn SciFi Film Festival](https://brooklynscififilmfest.com/). The BSFFF is back for its 7th installment, with films streaming online and screening in person throughout the week. I'll share more information about the different events and ways to participate in September. I hope you'll join us!

Book of the Month
*The Invincible* \- Stanisław Lem \(1964\)

*The Invincible* is considered one of Stanisław Lem's defining novels and another true classic of science fiction. We're back aboard a starship this month, following a crew sent to investigate the disappearance of an expedition on a distant planet. It's a mystery wrapped in world-building, atmospheric exploration, and the kind of ideas that made Lem such an influential voice in the genre.

Book Club has really enjoyed the Lem stories we've read so far, can't wait to dive into one of the novels that put him on the map. Ursula K. Le Guin said about *The Invincible*: "Anybody who likes a mystery will find it here — and its solution."

To join a Book Club meeting, all you will need is YOURSELF. If you haven’t had a chance to finish the book, we still would love for you to join us in the discussion.

Not able to join us in person for events? [The Sci Fi Book Club is on Discord](https://discord.gg/B9NMnC2F). Join us and keep the conversation going.

title: Matriarchal Messages for the Masses
description:
A community-centred pop-up project initiated by Amy Wong that celebrates the wisdom passed down through mothers, aunties, elders, caregivers, and chosen family.

MMM! Matriarchal Messages for the Masses MMM! (Matriarchal Messages for the Masses) is a community-centred pop-up project initiated by Amy Wong that celebrates the wisdom passed down through mothers, aunties, elders, caregivers, and chosen family. Through an open call and poster making workshop, you are invited to share matriarchal messages, everyday teachings, reminders, and words of care. Drawing especially from QT2S+/BIPOC knowledge traditions, selected submissions will be transformed into a series of collaboratively produced screen-printed T-shirts and totes. Part wearable tribute, part living archive, MMM! brings intergenerational knowledge into public space and honours the voices that shape our cultures and communities. Sept 28-29 MMM! (Matriarchal Messages for the Masses) Project Launch in the Lobby at 100 McCaul. November 2-6: MMM! Poster Workshop, Lobby 100 McCaul (led by Amy Wong and Tannis Nielsen, FOA) January 2027 dates TBA: Screen printing workshops (led by Amy Wong and Shannon Gerard, FOA) Feb 2027 dates TBA: Pop-up shop with proceeds to be donated to Sistering and the Barbara Schlifer Commemorative Clinic

title: Computers for Beginners
location: York Woods, Enhanced Learning Center
description:
Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse
A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this first session you will:
Observe and practice how to operate a mouse effectively
Understand various mouse pointers and cursors
Review basic keyboard functions
Use the mouse for basic Windows functions
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a computer mouse at a basic level and will be able to go online for additional practice.
Prerequisites: No computer experience required.
Format: Hands-on with demonstrations
Computers for Beginners 2: Use the Keyboard
A class on basic keyboard functions for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this second session you will:
Familiarize yourself through practice with the most essential keyboard functions (alphabet, number and symbol keys)
Practice proper keyboarding posture
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a keyboard at a beginner level and know how to go online for additional practice.
Prerequisites: Computer for Beginners 1 or basic mouse skills
Format: Hands-on with demonstrations
Computers for Beginners 3: Use Windows
A class on essential basic Windows skills for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this third session you will:
Become familiar with the Windows (10) operating system
Practice using common Windows features: File Explorer, Desktop, Taskbar, Windows, Applications
Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to create and organize files in the Windows environment.
Prerequisites: Computer for Beginners 1 & 2 or basic mouse and keyboarding skills
Format: Hands-on with demonstrations
Computers for Beginners 4: Use the Internet
An introductory class on the Internet for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fourth session you will:
Understand how to read a web site address
Practice using web addresses
Search for information using a search engine
Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches.
Prerequisites: Computer for Beginners 1 & 2 or basic mouse and keyboarding skills
Format: Hands-on with demonstrations
Computers for Beginners 5: Use Google Search and Maps
A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fifth session you will:
Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites
Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel.
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use more advanced search engine features and use Google Maps at a basic level.
Prerequisites: Computers for Beginners 1 & 2 or basic mouse, keyboarding and internet skills
Format: Hands-on with demonstrations
Computers for Beginners 6: Use Gmail
Learn to use Gmail, Google’s free web-based email service.
In this sixth session you will:
Practice basic email functions: send, read, reply, forward, delete email, and attach files
Review how spam and junk mail work
Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to use email.
Instructions on how to set up and manage your own free Gmail account are included in the handout.
Prerequisites: Basic keyboarding and mouse skills required.
Format: Hands-on with demonstrations

title: CNC Milling for Artists - Sept 28  [Mondays - 6 Week Comprehensive]
location: TTLMakerspace, 192 Spadina Ave., Toronto, ON
description:
CNC for Artists 

 
 

 
 In this course at TTLMakerspace, you will learn the technical aspects of using modern digital fabrication techniques with a CNC mill for artistic expression. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Starting with desktop versions of CNC machines, you’ll work your way through lessons up to the industrial Omni 1350 6’ x 8’ CNC milling machine. 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Schedule : 
 
 
 Six three-hour weekly classes, Mondays 6pm to 9pm. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Outcomes : 
 
 
 At the end of this course you will have achieved the following goals: 
 
 
- 
 Understanding of how to design for the strengths of a CNC mill 

- 
 Familiarity with the properties of a variety of hardwood materials 

- 
 Experience with constructive structural geometry 

- 
 Using a vector design tool 

- 
 Creating decorative inlays with veneer 

- 
 3-dimensional surfaces for decorative wall-art 

- 
 3D surface milling 

- 
 Machine maintenance and Safety 

 
 
 Following this course, you’ll be certified to use desktop mills, and book time with the industrial mill at TTLMakerspace (with your membership). You will also be able to join the growing community of TTL Makers sharing CNC knowledge on our Discord community. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Useful for: inlays, wall-art, sculptural designs, lighting 
 
 

 
 
 Want to get notified next time classes are posted? 

 Join our mailing list!

title: Fat Fables: Resisting Fatphobia and Finding Fat Joy
location: Parkdale
description:
Join artists, Jules Vodarek Hunter and Morgan Davis, co-creators of
Fat Fables
, for an evening of learning, performance and making connections.
Fat Fables
is a performance and creation program for Fat Two-Spirit, Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Trans, Queer, Intersex, Asexual (2SLGBTQIA+) folks. The facilitators will share its positive impact in celebrating and uplifting different bodies, discuss the origins of fatphobia and how it shapes the current state of affairs on all bodies today.
Photo Credit: Jae Yang
A brief excerpt from the book, Belly of the Beast: the Politics of Anti-fatness as Anti-blackness by Da'Shaun Harrison, will be read to spark an open conversation. With size-inclusive seating and cozy welcoming vibes, the facilitators will lead a creative writing session, where attendees can write, share, and participate as much or as little as they want.
The goal of Fat Fables is to create community for fat queer and trans folks, to tell stories, and to dream of a fat future where we all thrive. Fat people deserve to be visible, to be seen and to be artists on stage.
The program aims to help attendees feel empowered, supported, and to leave with a full heart.
Registration required.
Free. Doors open for registrants at 5:45 pm. At 6:00 pm, spots become first-come, first-served until capacity is reached. The program will run from 6 pm to 8 pm.
This program is produced by
Ontario Culture Days
in collaboration with
SummerWorks
as Producing Partner and Toronto Public Library. This program is supported by the City of Toronto.
Ontario Culture Days is a province-wide festival made possible through the support of its foundational partners, the Province of Ontario and the Ontario Arts Council. We acknowledge the support of the Canada Council for the Arts and the Government of Canada.

location: North York Central Library, Room 101
description:

(1998).
Synopsis (Criterion Pictures): Smoke Signals tells the story of the relationship between a father and his son. The story unfolds as Victor Joseph and another young man from the Indian reservation, Thomas Builds-the-Fire, set off to collect Arnold Joseph's pick-up truck and ashes from Arizona after Arnold has died. The two men remember Victor's father along the way, but their recollections are very different from each other. Victor learns many things about his father during his journey and, in the end, begins to understand, forgive, and grieve his loss.
No registration required.

title: Surviving Dementia Care: The Realities of Family Caregiving
location: Gerrard/Ashdale, 2nd Floor Program Room
description:
Are you a caregiver for someone with dementia? This talk addresses the specific experiences of people who are caring for a loved one, including the points of stress, the points of joy, and ways in which caregivers learn to survive the experience.
Learn about understanding the diagnosis, communicating with the loved one, managing guilt and grief, choosing an assisted living facility, using music and the arts as a means of connection and how the loving bond within the family can be maintained for as long as possible.
Presented by D. Grant Campbell, author of
Surviving Dementia Care
(University of Toronto Press, 2026).
D. Grant Campbell is a Professor Emeritus of Library and Information Science in the Faculty of Information and Media Studies, at the University of Western Ontario in London, Ontario. He holds a PhD in English Literature from Queen’s University and a Master of Information Studies from the University of Toronto. A violinist for over 50 years, he has played in numerous community orchestras, and has also conducted music sessions in various dementia settings in Toronto and London.

title: Data Analytics Essentials Learning Circle
location: Palmerston, Meeting Room
description:
Interested in learning about data analytics? Let's take a free online course together in a welcoming space!
A
learning circle
is a study group, guided by library staff, for people who want to take a free online course together in a supportive and welcoming environment.
Organizations all over the world recognize the value of analytics. Together, we'll learn about the essential tools used in this field.
In this 12-week learning circle, we will work through the Data Analytics Essentials course from Cisco Networking Academy. We will explore the fundamental tools of a data analyst, including how to:
transform, organize and visualize data with spreadsheet tools like Excel
query data from a relational database using SQL
improve data presentations using business intelligence tools like Tableau
We will meet weekly,
in-person,
every Tuesday afternoon, September 15 - December 8, 2-3:30 PM (12 sessions).
Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend sessions on a weekly basis.
Learners who complete the course will be able to:
earn a digital badge
download a certificate of completion

location: York Woods
description:

Learning circles are study groups guided by staff for people who want to take a free online course together in a welcoming space. Learners meet weekly and work together through the course materials. Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions.
Learners who successfully complete both courses will earn a digital badge and certificate of completion.
Python Essentials 1
is the first in a 2-course series that teaches computer programming skills including how to design, develop, and improve computer programs using the Python programming language. The course covers essential programming topics such as data types, variables, control flow, functions, and exceptions.
Python Essentials 2
is the second in a 2-course series that will prepare you for the PCAP – Certified Associate in Python Programming certification exam at Pearson VUE. This intermediate-level course covers advanced aspects of Python programming, including modules, packages, exceptions, file processing and object-oriented programming (OOP).
For more information about the Python learning circle, please contact

title: ROTMAN Talk:  Prof. Daron Acemoglu- "What Happened to Liberal Democracy?" ($25)
description:
TORONTO ARTS & CULTURE
### **Book Synopsis:**

**From Daron Acemoglu, 2024 Nobel laureate in economics and coauthor of *Why Nations Fail,* an ambitious and expansive inquiry into the biggest story in global politics over the last hundred years: the rise and fall of liberal democracy.**

**"A very important work and a must-read."** —Thomas Piketty, #1 *New York Times* bestselling author of *Capital in the Twenty-First Century*

**Tickets are $25 only (or with book $44). LINK below.**

**"Daron Acemoglu is one of the most brilliant and insightful thinkers I’ve ever known. His particular genius is being able to look at impossibly complex problems and see right to the heart of what matters. This book is a tour de force that left me feeling more optimistic about the future than I have in a long time."**

—Steven Levitt, #1 *New York Times* bestselling author of *Freakonomics*

The dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991 raised hopes that we were one step closer to the triumph of liberalism. Soon, many predicted, we would all be living in functional liberal democracies. Sustained economic growth would benefit all segments of society and war would be a relic of the past. A generation later, one can only ask: What happened?

**Nobel laureate Daron Acemoglu** argues in this powerful book that liberal democracy flourished when it pursued its core promises of shared prosperity, democratic governance, and the free pursuit of knowledge. But liberalism, a philosophy built to challenge power, never fully adjusted to becoming the establishment. Nor was it able to deal with the economic and social disruptions that digital technologies wrought. Worse, in the postindustrial economy, liberalism turned its back on its core promises. As a segment of college-educated elites became politically dominant and separated from the rest of society, they sowed the seeds of widespread inequality while intensifying efforts to reshape mass culture and values.

**Ticket link** (mostly sold-out)--

https://www.rotman.utoronto.ca/news-events-and-ideas/public-events/events-listings/2026/september-2026/sept-29-daron-acemoglu/

title: In Depth Sewing Intro - Sept 29 [Tuesdays - 6 week program]
location: TTLMakerspace, 192 Spadina Ave., Toronto, ON
description:
LEARN TO SEW 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Suitable for beginners. This class goes over the basics of operating a sewing machine, cutting and sewing garments, and basic pattern alterations. 
 
 
 The main project for this class is an apron custom fit to YOU. A typical first project is a tote bag,but we’ve chosen to have our students make an apron as it covers the same skills while also teaching basic tailoring and fitting. The goal of this class is to provide students with the basic skills associated with sewing, understanding patterns, and textiles, while promoting confidence and shifting the mindset of your everyday clothing as things that suit your needs and body, rather than things to simply wear. 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 This class will also explore clothing repairs and minor alterations like hemming, altering
necklines, adding pockets, etc. Students are encouraged to bring in items they wish to alter or repair. 
 
 
 Materials and equipment for all projects are provided with the course. 
 
 

 
 Schedule 
6 weeks, Tuesdays 6pm to 9pm 
 
 

 
 
 Outcomes 
 At the end of the course you will have achieved the following goals: 
 
 
- Proficiency with operating a sewing machine safely 

- Understanding of fabric types, their uses, how to prep them for sewing, and how to cut fabric 

- Comfort with taking measurements of the body and how to apply them to a pattern 

- Knowledge of basic pattern alterations and how to adjust existing garments to fit you better 

- Understanding of how to transfer patterns to fabric so that space is used as efficiently as possible 

- Understanding of pinning and ironing techniques 

- Familiarity with basic sewing techniques including seams, hemming, hand stitching,
applying pockets, fasteners including buttons, zippers, snaps, and ties, as well as
different stitch uses for different techniques and materials

- Basic repairs like fixing holes, torn seams, holes in pockets, adding patches

- Basic alterations like adjusting hems, changing necklines, switching out buttons or other fasteners

title: TechTalk (In-Person) - September 2026
description:

After a brief pause, we're back with another in-person event.

Here’s the September edition of our Tech Talk event at Super.com on September 29, 2026

Join us for some drinks, snacks, and Tech Talks.

Make sure to mark your calendars, come out, and join us for this event!

**🕑 Agenda & Schedule ✨**

* 18:00 - Doors open
* 18:20 - Intro and announcements

* 18:30 - **httpstate - Synchronizing state across all of your apps** by **[Alex Morales](https://httpstate.com)**
*Abstract*: Moving data between frontend, backend, apps, and databases usually requires complex wiring. httpstate is a lightweight library that handles end-to-end state management in just a few lines of code—eliminating boilerplate so you can transfer data without the setup overhead.

* 19:00 - **Strudel - live-coding music in your browser with Javascript** by **[Fabio Neves](https://fabioneves.ca)**
*Abstract*: Code isn't just for apps—it makes real-time music. While tools like TidalCycles and Sonic Pi require external setups, Strudel is a self-contained JS live-coding tool running straight in your browser via the Web Audio API. Join us as we explore live-coding history and code an EDM track live 🎛️🎚️

title: ABCD Reads "Country People" by Daniel Mason
description:
A Book Club, Downtown (ABCD)
ABCD Reads "**[Country People](https://tpl.bibliocommons.com/v2/record/S234C4758420)**" by Daniel Mason.

[[RESULTS](https://opavote.com/results/5996722009669632) of the poll for this event]

**:: ABOUT THE BOOK ::**
"Daniel Mason’s latest novel sees him return to the verdant New England landscape that so captivated readers of 2023’s acclaimed North Woods. This time, though, he hops the border from Massachusetts into Vermont – and effects a deeper shift in the process. Where North Woods was a foray into history, telling the tale of a house and its inhabitants over three centuries, in Country People Mason turns his attention to literature and mines the rich seams of text, from myths to Milton to Shakespeare to Tolstoy and all points in between, that make up his novel’s foundations. This is, at its core, a story about stories; a tale about the tales we tell each other, and our children, and ourselves." (from [The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/jul/07/country-people-by-daniel-mason-review-a-joyful-follow-up-to-north-woods))

"Miles Krzelewski is a devoted husband, a doting father beloved for his outlandish bedtime stories, and the proud owner of a truffle-hunting dog in a land with no truffles. He is also a bit lost, twelve years late with his PhD on Russian folktales, and increasingly haunted by a sense that he's become a disappointment to his family. So when his wife Kate accepts a visiting professorship at a prestigious college in the far away forests of Vermont, he decides that this will be his year to finally move forward with his life. [...] Joyous, absurd, and life-affirming, Country People is a luminous exploration of marriage and parenthood, the nature of belief and the power of stories, and the ways in which we find connection in an increasingly fragmented world." (from [Goodreads](https://www.goodreads.com/en/book/show/242518677-country-people))

**:: ABOUT THE EVENT ::**
You are welcome to arrive 30 minutes before the event and stay 30 minutes or longer afterward to connect with other attendees outside the book talk.

Please ensure you have read the book before attending (though finishing any book is not a barrier to participating, as long as you don't mind spoilers).

First-time attendees can join for free. If the event is full, we maintain an unofficial waitlist. Please send [Michael](https://www.meetup.com/members/55295192/) a direct message for more information, in either case.

We request a $3 contribution from regular attendees to help cover our monthly meetup costs.

**:: ABOUT OUR NEXT BOOK ::**
At the end of each event, we will ask for nominees for our next book. If you have a good one in mind, please ensure it is between 200-400 pages long, available from the Toronto Public Library, and counts as contemporary literary fiction (though these are not hard and fast rules). When enough nominees are collected, Michael will send the members a direct message with a link where you can vote.

title: Crossing the Wine-Dark Sea: Emily Wilson on Translating Antiquity
location: Toronto Reference Library, Appel Salon, Second Floor
description:
Renowned classicist and translator Emily Wilson explores the art and challenges of bringing ancient literature to modern readers.
In Crossing the Wine-Dark Sea, Emily Wilson — whose acclaimed renditions of Homer's Odyssey and Iliad have captured a generation's imagination — takes readers on a sharp and often entertaining tour through antiquity. Drawing on twenty years of scholarship and teaching, Wilson illuminates the difficult choices translators must make, the pleasures of finding new solutions to old problems, and the inevitable frustrations of never fully capturing what lives in the original text.
Across chapters ranging from the politics of Helen of Troy to the obscenities of Aristophanes, from Roman imitation of Greek models to contemporary debates over "foreignizing" and "domesticizing" styles, Wilson examines how modern norms of gender, sexuality, violence, humor, and power complicate our readings of ancient works—and how translation always risks denaturing what is unique and strange about the ancient world.
Brilliant, erudite, and accessible to readers with no classical background, Crossing the Wine-Dark Sea is at once an introduction to the wonders of Greek and Roman literature, a manifesto for the value of translation in a rapidly changing world, and an invitation to encounter ancient cultures anew.
Emily Wilson speaks with Ella Street about Crossing the Wine-Dark Sea and the lifelong work of carrying ancient voices into the present.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

title: National Day for Truth and Reconciliation Commemoration
description:
Date: Tuesday, September 29, 2026
Time: 7:00 pm – 9:00 pm
Location: Bata Shoe Museum, 327 Bloor St. W.
Tickets: Pay What You Wish (Free, $10, $20, $30)
Age Restriction: Due to the nature of the event, 16+ 
Honouring the experiences of Residential School survivors, join us for an intimate and insightful conversation with Ojibwe Kwe author, educator, and Residential School survivor, Karen Chaboyer, to commemorate Orange Shirt Day and National Day for Truth and Reconciliation. Tea and bannock will be provided by Candace’s Catering.  
Agenda
6:30 pm – Doors open
7:00 pm – Conversation begins
8:00 pm – Conversation ends, Open dialogue and visiting
9:00 pm – Museum closes 
RSVP  
ABOUT KAREN CHABOYER: 
 
Karen Chaboyer is an Ojibwe kwe, a great-grandmother, a grandmother, and mother. She is also an author, a public speaker, and an educator. Karen is from Rainy River First Nation, a community in Northwestern Ontario, Treaty 3 Territory. Karen is a survivor of St. Margaret’s Indian Residential School, also known as the Fort Frances Indian Residential School where she attended for 9 years. Karen was born into a family of 11 siblings: 9 brothers and 2 sisters. She is the third youngest in her family. She is also a second generation survivor of Residential School. Karen has been presenting since 2006. Her audiences are mostly elementary/high schools, colleges, universities and organizations. Karen shares the effects Residential School had on her and how she lost her identity, her roots, her culture and language. Karen’s goal is to educate people on the impact Residential Schools had on her and Indigenous individuals, families and communities to this day. 
 
 
  

Please review our Terms and Conditions in advance and check in with Visitor Services upon arrival. Questions? Email us info@batashoemuseum.ca anytime.

title: Queer Death Salon: Grief Gardening
location: Online, online
description: In times of grief, many people find that a connection to land, earth, and the tending of life can help carry us through. It is well established that a connection to nature, no matter how small, helps improve our experiences of depression, anxiety, and sense of wellbeing. Pulling from their their personal experiences, Eli will lead participants in a discussion about; the history of Grief Gardening through various cultural perspectives gardening as a tool for emotional processing and providing a sense of control and purpose creating sites for remembrance tending to a relationship with nature to encourage a sense of hope and renewal He will also support participants with ideas about how to get started or expand on our grief gardens. Eli (they/he) is a gardener and former landscaper, wetlands restorationist and wildlife biologist currently living on Ohlone land in Oakland. Mutual aid, covid realism, disability justice, queerness and art as well as gardening all help them with the little and big sources of grief that life brings us. ‍

title: Sept 30 - Building Composable Vision Workflows in FiftyOne
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
This workshop explores the [FiftyOne](https://docs.voxel51.com/index.html) plugin framework to build custom computer vision applications. You’ll learn to extend the FiftyOne App with Python based panels and server side operators, as well as integrate external tools for labeling, vector search, and model inference into your dataset views.

**Date, Time and Location**

Sep 30, 2026
9 AM - 10 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/building-composable-vision-workflows-in-fiftyone-september-30-2026)**

You’ll also automate repetitive tasks by writing custom workflows executing within the FiftyOne environment. Attendees will learn to transform FiftyOne from a visualization tool into a central hub for your vision stack.

What you'll learn:

* **Build Python plugins.** Define plugin manifests and directory structures to register custom functionality within the FiftyOne ecosystem.
* **Develop server side operators.** Write functions to execute model inference, data cleaning, or metadata updates from the App interface.
* **Build interactive panels.** Create custom UI dashboards using to visualize model metrics or specialized dataset distributions.
* **Manage operator execution contexts.** Pass data between the App front end and your backend to build dynamic user workflows.
* **Implement delegated execution.** Configure background workers to handle long running data processing tasks without blocking the user interface.
* **Build labeling integrations.** Streamline the flow of data between FiftyOne and annotation platforms through custom triggers and ingestion scripts.
* **Extend vector database support.** Program custom connectors for external vector stores to enable semantic search across large sample datasets.
* **Package and share plugins.** Distribute your extensions internally and externally

title: Decadence and Seventy Book Launch
location: Ben McNally Books
description:
[at Ben McNally Books]
Join us at Ben McNally Books, in partnership with Biblioasis and Random House Canada, for a double book launch, featuring both Richard Kelly Kemmick and Ian Brown.
About the Books:
Decadence
"The genre of memoir is bullshit (as I humbly posit). No one actually lives like they are moving along some grand Freytag’s triangle. Rather, we live within isolated instances, specific struggles and victories, which, when compiled, form a narrative."—Richard Kelly Kemick.
In
Decadence
, Richard Kelly Kemick’s “accidental memoir of a sort,” the author ranges widely through his myriad preoccupations and obsessions—volleyball, municipal landfills, dogs, high school plays, Christmas villages, love—out of which the shape of a unique sensibility is revealed. Reminiscent of the three Davids—Rakoff, Sedaris, and Wallace—these essays accrete into a portrait of a man trying to make sense of a world in which there are no goddamn rules; and yet one in which every action has sometimes profound consequences.
A book of intelligence and care and kindness and humour and yearning and the occasional epiphany, Decadence gathers up from the odds and ends of living what makes a modern life—quiet and desperate as it may at times be—worth celebrating.
Order a copy of
Decadence
here
Seventy
Ian Brown, award-winning author of The Boy in the Moon and the memoir Sixty, now recounts his daily reckoning with the milestone age of seventy. Fearlessly candid, often funny and relentlessly real, Brown asks the terrifying questions we all have about growing old, even when he doesn’t want to know the answers.
An acclaimed journalist and chronicler of contemporary life, seventy-year-old Ian Brown is not going gently into his eighth decade. The outlook is more perilous than it was at age sixty, but Brown is determined (however hopelessly) not to let time get the better of him.
During the course of his seventy-first year, Brown writes incessantly, travelling on assignment for the Globe and Mail across the United States in the months leading to the shocking 2024 election; holidays with family and friends, always aware he might not see them again; skis and rows and exercises like a madman while turning a wary eye on the live-forever movement; takes up pickleball and talks books; and in general tries (and frequently fails) to show some human courage in the face of the march of his dwindling years.
Along the way he encounters the lists that have suddenly become essential to daily life (what to take when leaving the house, what to pack for a trip, what to pick up at the drugstore); the indignities of medical tests and the shock of financing a retirement; the terrors and pleasures of growing older with one’s spouse of four decades; the now-suspenseful drama of sex; the thrilling spectacle of watching adult children inhabit new roles of familial responsibility; and the shocking new lessons of life as an older person (accept compliments with grace, remember to smile, stand up straighter).
As the percentage of the Canadian population over eighty-five will triple in the next twenty-five years, Brown contemplates his mortality and that of his contemporaries for readers of all ages. Growing old—anything after seventy—is a grave challenge, but also enormously liberating: if there is something you want to say or do, now is your chance to say it or do it. “I have to keep taking chances,” Brown reckons. “I don’t want to give in too soon.”

Seventy

description:
Throughout the month of October, works by artist Sine Lam will be on display at the Forest Hill branch.
Sine Lam is an emerging artist currently based in Ontario. She studied Fine Art at St. Lawrence College. Her artistic practice blends symbolism, realism, and surrealism, drawing inspiration from human emotion, urban solitude, connection, memories, nature, and time.
Her series,
Passage of Time
, reflects her experiences of city life and explores themes of contrast and contradiction— visual beauty paired with melancholy, and relaxation alongside loneliness, much like life itself, where joy and sorrow coexist. Her work often carries hidden messages through symbolic elements.
Sine's work has been featured in various group exhibitions, including at the Marianne van Silfhout Gallery.

program. Toronto Public Library provides space for local artists to exhibit their work at locations across the city. These exhibits aim to reflect the diverse cultural interests of the city and its neighbourhoods.

branch page before you visit.

title: Financial Workshops for Seniors

description:

Thursday Oct 1: What Do Seniors Get?
Learn about benefits for older adults living in Ontario, including Canada Pension Plan (CPP), Old Age Security (OAS), Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS), and Guaranteed Annual Income Supplement (GAINS).
Thursday Oct 15: Understanding the Personal Income Tax System.
What is a taxable income and how can tax credits, deductions, entitlements and exemptions help to reduce taxable income.
Thursday Oct 29: Protecting Your Retirement Income.
Learn how to reduce claw backs to GIS and GAINS payments if receiving additional income from employment, a private pension, or a Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP).
Thursday Nov 12: Coming to Canada and Leaving Canada.
Learn about eligible benefits for those that resided in Canada for fewer than 40 years between the ages of 18 and 65, or for those planning on emigrating from Canada after retiring.
Thursday Nov 26: Tax Credits and Benefits for Seniors and People with Disabilities.
Learn about other tax credits and benefits for seniors, people with disabilities, and caregivers, including the disability tax credit, the Canada caregiver credit, and the home accessibility tax credit.
Registration not required. Drop-in welcome.

title: AI Everywhere, All At Once
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor Auditorium
description:
AI is suddenly everywhere, in ads, on your phone, your news feed, all your software, even your search bar. Who decides what gets made with AI? What does it cost? And what does it feel like? What happens when these tools start to feel less like tools and more like collaborators?
In this kickoff event for our Innovator in Residence (Applied AI Development) program, join Ryan Kelln for an illustrated talk with live demos. Let's think together deeply about the impact, costs and opportunities presented when trillions of dollars are spent researching and developing digital intelligence. We'll talk candidly about the people who make it, why they make it, and how it shifts power. Then we'll look at what your library can offer that the AI companies can't, and how to get the most out of the 12 week residency program ahead.
Registration is required and will start September 9, 2026 at 9:00 AM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.

title: Zahra Ahooei: Film Screening & Conversation
location: OCAD University Auditorium,100 McCaul St, Toronto, ON M5T 2W7, Canada
description:
Join Iranian filmmaker Zahra Ahooei, for a screening and conversation about her award-winning short films and her current documentary project, HouseLight.

FREE (by Ticket only): ZAHRA AHOOEI OCAD FILM SCREENING TICKETS https://www.eventbrite.ca/e/zahra-ahooei-film-screening-conversation-october-1-2026-tickets-1999296660130?aff=oddtdtcreator

October 1, 2026
6:30-8:00pm
OCAD University, 100 McCaul Street
Auditorium (Room 190)

Zahra Ahooei is an Iranian filmmaker, writer, and media artist currently based in Canada. She has directed several short narrative films, including Reflex (2024), Prestige (2020), Sign Out (2017), and Extra Time (2015), which have been screened internationally and recognized with various awards. Her background also includes years of experience in journalism, television writing, and content creation for both broadcast and digital platforms.

Zahra’s upcoming project, HouseLight, is a feature-length documentary that employs a non-fiction storytelling approach. Rooted in her personal experiences, the film explores themes of loss, memory, and immigration through a distinctly female perspective. In 2024, Zahra developed this project during her participation in the Newcomer Filmmentor program at the Liaison of Independent Filmmakers of Toronto (LIFT).

She is currently an IIE Artist Protection Fund Fellow in residence at OCAD University, which acts as the primary host and creative hub for the development and production of her ongoing film project. As part of this fellowship network, OBORO, an artist-run centre in Montreal dedicated to the presentation and production of visual, media, and digital arts will also host Zahra during the later stages of the project in collaboration with APF and OCAD University.

In November 2025, while still in development, HouseLight was selected to participate in Doc Lab Montreal’s feature film program, part of Forum RIDM, the industry platform of the Montreal International Documentary Festival (RIDM), one of North America’s leading documentary events fostering creative exchange, professional development, and international co-productions.

title: Jill Lepore: The Artificial State
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
TPL and Toronto Metropolitan University present Pulitzer-Prize winning historian Jill Lepore in conversation with Sanjay Ruparelia at the Toronto Reference Library's Appel Salon.
As Professor of American History at Harvard University and Professor of Law at Harvard Law School, Jill Lepore brings her rare gift for narrative history to one of the most urgent questions of our time: has democracy already been quietly replaced by rule of a different kind, one governed not by citizens, but by machines owned by corporations?
In her new book
The Rise and Fall of the Artificial State
, Lepore traces our increasing dependence on and strangulation by data. Framing the book as a successor to Hannah Arendt's
The Origins of Totalitarianism
, Lepore shares a new history for our twenty-first century.
What does it mean when the era of the liberal nation-state seems to be giving way to the rule of artificial intelligence? Lepore insists history is driven not by machines but by individuals, societies, cultures, and ideas, and that the architects of the Artificial State drew their governing philosophy not from science, but from science fiction.
Can what has been built be undone? And what would it take to reimagine a genuinely democratic relationship between technology and self-governance, one where humans, not machines, remain accountable to one another?
Join one of America's most celebrated historians, fresh from her bestselling
We the People: A History of the U.S. Constitution
, for an essential conversation about power, technology, and the fight to reclaim democratic life from the architects of an artificial future.
Question and answer session and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this Event's Guests:
Jill Lepore
Sanjay Ruparelia
Read More:
Rise and Fall of the Artificial State
We the People
***
This event is part of our
On Civil Society
series, where we host local and international authors, activists and academics in conversation about the most critical topics of our time. Generously supported by the McConnell Foundation and also by Chris M. Reid.
***
About the series:
On the Frontlines of Democracy
is a public lecture series to analyze the trajectory of democracy in the twenty-first century.
In every region, the prospects of democracy face serious challenges, old and new. Can we protect constitutional rights and renew collective self-rule in an era of popular mistrust, severe partisanship and resurgent nationalism? Can they reduce inequalities of power, wealth and status, defend deep diversity and confront climate change in the new digital age? Can we develop innovative strategies to revitalize civic engagement, empower public institutions and resist autocratic threats? And what can we offer, learn and do to promote the prospects of democracy in our increasingly post-western global order?

title: Global Philosophy Research Interest Group Talk (Martin Adam, University of Victoria)
location: Jackman Humanities Building 100
description:
The Global Philosophy Research Interest Group is delighted to welcome as guest speaker Martin Adam, an associate professor in the Department of Pacific and Asian Studies at the University of Victoria. His work is centered on Indian Buddhism and Buddhist Ethics, with more general interests in other south Asian religious traditions and western Philosophy. He received my PhD from McGill University in 2003, having spent extended stays at institutions in India, Nepal, and Switzerland. 
Talk Title
Buddhist Phenomenology and the Question of AI Agency 
Talk Abstract
Agency is only one among the many attributes of human consciousness whose replication is being actively pursued in the race to develop artificial general intelligence. Work towards its achievement is handicapped by a lack of agreement as to its definition. The present article examines the idea of agency, inquiring in particular about that element of human agency in virtue of which we are sometimes able to say that we act freely. Part of the experience of being a human agent consists in the fact that we sometimes feel free in acting and sometimes feel unfree. Here, our discussion will be trained on the psychological basis of this aspect of our experience of free agency, irrespective of the philosophical question of whether we ever actually are “truly” free in a metaphysical sense. The analysis proceeds with an eye towards assessing the possibility of attributing agency to an artificially created intelligence. Following an ordinary language account of how we tend to speak and think about free agency, I examine what the tradition of Theravāda Buddhist Abhidhamma has to contribute on this topic—finding a number of remarkable parallels. The article concludes with a consideration of whether from an Abhidhammic perspective it might ever make sense to attribute free agency to a created machine intelligence.

title: Language, Epistemology, Metaphysics, and Mind Research Interest Group (Adam Pautz, Brown)
location: Jackman Humanities Building, Room 418, 170 St. George Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5R 2M8, Canada
description:
The Language, Epistemology, Metaphysics, and Mind Research Interest Group is delighted to welcome as guest speaker Adam Pautz, a professor in the Department of Philosophy at Brown University. His research is about consciousness and its place in nature, the idea that all facts are grounded in physical facts, and the issue of whether things are the way they appear. He tries to make progress on some of the traditional “big questions” about mind and world by using recent science as well a priori methods. 
Pautz’s current research project is a “consciousness-first” program in the philosophy of mind. The idea is that conscious acquaintance is not something that can be reductively explained in other terms (e. g. representation plus cognitive or rational access); rather it must be taken as a starting point from which to explain other things (cognition, rationality, value). The resulting view has some similarities to Bertrand Russell’s early view about the foundational role of acquaintance. 
More to follow.

title: Clay Tile Workshop
location: Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Experiment with clay and craft your own unique tile in this hands-on workshop designed for both beginners and art enthusiasts.

Guided by our Museum Educators, participants will explore shaping, designing, and decorating techniques inspired by ceramic works in the Aga Khan Museum’s Collections. title: Essence of the Garden: Plein Air Art Exhibition and Sale
description:
Celebrating Art, Nature, and Community — Essence of the Garden is the 2nd annual plein air art exhibition and sale featuring over 100 original artworks created outdoors at Toronto Botanical Garden and Edwards Gardens. This curated, site-specific show invites visitors to experience the Garden through the eyes of the artists who paint here—capturing moments of light, movement, and the essence of the natural world. 



Saturday, October 3 through 18, 2026Open Daily, 10:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.Free Admission  



This exhibition coincides with Toronto’s Ravine Days, an annual city-wide celebration of Toronto’s ravine system. 



Presenting Sponsor Foresters Financial 







 What You’ll See




Over 100 plein air paintings celebrating the Garden created by 46 talented local artists



Artworks displayed in public spaces across the Visitor Centre and are available for sale.



Visit the Garden Shop for unique, artist-made gifts and mini works



Engage with the artist(s) who will be hosting workshops and will be onsite throughout the exhibition painting ‘plein air’








Meet the Artists




Full list of artists coming soon.








Take Home a Piece of the Garden



Artwork will be available for purchase throughout the run of the show—buy your favourite painting and take home a piece of the Garden. Additional items from participating artists will be available at the Garden Shop and/or pop-up boutique, including miniature art, prints, cards, and magnets. Sales support both the artists and Toronto Botanical Garden’s community programming.
