title: Dystopia Nonfiction Book Club: A Good War
location: Toronto Reference Library, Lower Level, Room B1
description:
Join us each month to discuss issues in politics and society, and explore how powerful forces are exploiting our world and dystopian imaginings are becoming present-day realities.
October’s book is
A Good War: Mobilizing Canada for the Climate Emergency
by public policy advisor Seth Klein. Copies of the book are available in print, eBook & eAudiobook format. Book club attendees are encouraged to read the book in advance of the meeting.
"In A Good War, Seth Klein explores how we can align our politics and economy with what the science says we must do to address the climate crisis. But Klein brings an original and uniquely hopeful take to this challenge. The book is structured around lessons from the Second World War – the last time Canada faced an existential threat. Others have said we need a “wartime approach” to climate change, but this is the first book to delve into what that could actually look like. Canada’s wartime experience, Klein contends, provides an inspirational reminder that
we have done this before
. We have mobilized in common cause across class, race and gender, and entirely retooled our economy in the space of a few short years."
Drop in. No registration required.

title: David Treuer: The Savage Mind
location: Toronto Reference Library, Appel Salon, Second Floor
description:
New York Times bestselling author David Treuer shares his groundbreaking, intimate reckoning with the history of North America.
The Savage Mind is a seamless blend of memoir, history and reportage, in which Treuer leverages his unique dual perspective as the son of a Holocaust survivor and the first American Indigenous woman judge in the United States to offer an examination of the distinct nature of North American violence.
In contrast to the frontier thesis of American history, Treuer contends that frontier violence cannot be defined as an external force, but that it has actually entered the culture and taken root in our very selves.
By reckoning with these histories, the book confronts our complicity in either normalizing violence, or blaming it on outside sources, instead of seeing its recurring patterns and contending with its significance.
David Treuer speaks with journalist Brandi Morin about The Savage Mind and shares why he chooses to embrace an ultimately hopefully view of the continent.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this event’s guests:
David Treuer
Brandi Morin
Read more:

The Heartbeat of Wounded Knee
Our Voice of Fire

title: ABCD Reads "Salvation of a Saint" by Keigo Higashino
description:
A Book Club, Downtown (ABCD)
ABCD Reads "**[Salvation of a Saint](https://tpl.bibliocommons.com/v2/record/S234C2888913)**" by Keigo Higashino.

[RESULTS of the poll for this event]

**:: ABOUT THE BOOK ::**
"The Devotion of Suspect X was a hit with critics and readers alike. The first major English language publication from the most popular bestselling writer in Japan, it was acclaimed as "stunning," "brilliant," and "ingenious."
Now physics professor Manabu Yukawa—Detective Galileo—returns in a new case of impossible murder, where instincts clash with facts and theory with reality.
Yoshitaka, who was about to leave his marriage and his wife, is poisoned by arsenic-laced coffee and dies. His wife, Ayane, is the logical suspect—except that she was hundreds of miles away when he was murdered. The lead detective, Tokyo Police Detective Kusanagi, is immediately smitten with her and refuses to believe that she could have had anything to do with the crime. His assistant, Kaoru Utsumi, however, is convinced Ayane is guilty. While Utsumi's instincts tell her one thing, the facts of the case are another matter. So she does what her boss has done for years when stymied—she calls upon Professor Manabu Yukawa.
But even the brilliant mind of Dr. Yukawa has trouble with this one, and he must somehow find a way to solve an impossible murder and capture a very real, very deadly murderer.
Salvation of a Saint is Keigo Higashino at his mind-bending best, pitting emotion against fact in a beautifully plotted crime novel filled with twists and reverses that will astonish and surprise even the most attentive and jaded of readers." (from [Macmillan Publishers](https://us.macmillan.com/books/9781250036278/salvationofasaint/))

"When a man is discovered dead by poisoning in his empty home his beautiful wife, Ayane, immediately falls under suspicion. All clues point to Ayane being the logical suspect, but how could she have committed the crime when she was hundreds of miles away?
As Tokyo police detective Kusanagi tries to unpick a seemingly unrelated sequence of events he finds himself falling for Ayane. When his judgement becomes dangerously clouded his assistant must call on an old friend for help; it will take a genius to unravel the most spectacular web of deceit they have ever faced…
SALVATION OF A SAINT is a magnificently complex and page-turning thriller starring international crime fiction’s most enigmatic sleuth.This is essential reading for all fans of exceptional crime fiction." (from [Hachette UK](https://www.hachette.co.uk/titles/keigo-higashino/salvation-of-a-saint/9780349138817/))

**:: ABOUT THE EVENT ::**
You are welcome to arrive 30 minutes before the event and stay 30 minutes or longer afterward to connect with other attendees outside the book talk.

Please ensure you have read the book before attending (though finishing any book is not a barrier to participating, as long as you don't mind spoilers).

First-time attendees can join for free. If the event is full, we maintain an unofficial waitlist. Please send [Michael](https://www.meetup.com/members/55295192/) a direct message for more information, in either case.

We request a $3 contribution from regular attendees to help cover our monthly meetup costs.

**:: ABOUT OUR NEXT BOOK ::**
At the end of each event, we will ask for nominees for our next book. If you have a good one in mind, please ensure it is between 200-400 pages long, available from the Toronto Public Library, and counts as contemporary literary fiction (though these are not hard and fast rules). When enough nominees are collected, Michael will send the members a direct message with a link where you can vote.

title: Jamaluddin Aram: The Blood of Things
location: North York Central Library, Concourse Event Space, North York Central Library (5120 Yonge St), Lower Level
description:
TPL presents Afghan-Canadian writer Jamaluddin Aram in conversation with Dmitri Nasrallah at the North York Central Library's Concourse Event Space.
What does it mean to carry a homeland inside you after it has been lost, not once, but again and again? In his essay collection
The Blood of Things
, Aram turns his attention fully to Afghanistan, its beauty, its suffering, and its complexity. Spanning from the recent fall of Kabul to the early days of Islam, from the myth of the Order of Assassins to the persecution of the country's ethnic Hazara community, Aram weaves personal stories with sweeping historical and political inquiry.
Drawing on his own journey from Afghanistan to Toronto, and his work as associate producer of the Oscar-nominated film
Buzkashi Boys
, Aram brings a novelist's eye for character and an essayist's rigor to bear on questions of identity, belonging, and what remains possible even amid profound loss.
Join Jamaluddin Aram for an intimate evening of readings and conversation on exile, memory, and the enduring pull of home.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this event’s guests:
Jamaluddin Aram
Dimitri Nasrallah

title: Résumé and Cover Letter for Industry
description:
About the facilitator 
 
Jessica Wurster, Career Exploration & Education, Graduate Career Educator  
Jessica (she/they) has been supporting students in their career journeys for over 15 years at universities in Quebec and Ontario. As Graduate Career Educator, Jess draws on their doctoral training in Communication Studies and professional experience to develop and deliver programming and resources targeted to professional and graduate students and recent alumni. She’s also a quilter, a frequenter of farmer’s markets in the east end and beyond, and a collector of cookbooks.    
Looking to tune up your résumé and cover letter for industry roles? Join us for a session with Career Exploration & Education to learn strategies, tips, and AI-assisted approaches to build and refresh your industry job application materials.  
We will discuss:  

Creating application materials targeted to industry roles  
How to analyze industry job descriptions so you can successfully tailor your résumé  
Strategies to create a more effective and captivating résumé including writing strong accomplishment statements and organizing résumé sections effectively 
How to use AI tools effectively and ethically to support résumé and cover letter development, including prompt-engineering techniques that help generate stronger content, identify skills alignment, and customize materials for specific roles 
Best practices for reviewing, refining, and personalizing AI-generated content to ensure authenticity and accuracy 

Bonus Activity: Participate in a résumé review for personalized feedback! You will need to bring a digital copy of your working résumé (it does not need to be finalized) and be ready to share it with your peers. You’ll also can practice AI prompting strategies to strengthen and tailor your application materials  
Register in Advance.

title: Working With Your Go To Emotional State
location: North York Central Library, Room 101
description:
Most of us have a
"go-to emotion."
It is the emotion that shows up automatically when we feel hurt or overwhelmed. That emotion can be
anger, anxiety, depression, guilt, shame, or even emotional numbness.
In this interactive presentation, we will explore how your go-to emotion developed, what purpose it serves, and offer techniques on how to respond from a more measured space.
Join Ann Schnurr, a Registered Psychotherapist with more than 25 years of experience, as she supports adults to understand their go-to emotion for greater emotional resilience, healthier relationships, and a deeper connection with self.
Registration is encouraged

Drop-ins welcome until capacity is reached.  For more information contact the Business Science & Technology desk at 416-395-5613

title: The Friendship Test: Engagement Activity
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
The Friendship Test
Bring your best friend, your partner, or your whole crew and put your friendship to the test, Newlywed Game–style. Answer questions about each other's habits, histories and hot takes to see who really knows who, and who's got some catching up to do. It's playful proof that even our closest bonds have more to discover, echoing Berkowitz's case that friendship takes real, ongoing work.
This interactive pre-show is followed by
Friendships and other Complexities ft. Roger Berkowitz
, which starts at 7pm in the Appel Salon.
You can register for that event
here
, but please note if you wish to attend the pre-event activities you need to register separately
on this page
.
***
This evening’s
theme explores
the challenge of
staying in dialogue and connection across our
difference
s
through Hannah Arendt’s friendships
.
Make the most of your
Connect IRL
experience by coming before or staying after the
featured event
. Grab a drink or snack at the bar. Sign up for the workshop or try out one of the engagement activities available, including this event's Conversation Station: The Kitchen Table, where you can take a moment or two to connect with a stranger to reflect on the rewards and challenges of friendship.
The Kitchen Table |
5:30 – 6:30 pm & 8:00 – 9:00 pm
Grab a seat and dig into the questions we rarely ask out loud: How has your definition of friendship changed? Can you stay close to someone you disagree with? What makes a friendship last? Inspired by Berkowitz's argument that friendship — not agreement — is the glue of a healthy society, this café is a space to reflect on your own circle with the strangers sitting next to you.
Connect IRL
is not your average series of events, workshops and activities, but a real chance to connect with other Torontonians in meaningful and sometimes unexpected ways. Through conversation stations meant to spark one-on-one conversations, or hands-on engagement activities and workshops before the featured event, participants can explore the value of connection and community.

title: Friendships and other Complexities ft. Roger Berkowitz
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
This evening’s theme explores the challenge of staying in dialogue and connection across our differences through Hannah Arendt’s friendships.
Make the most of your
Connect IRL
experience by coming before or staying after the featured event. Grab a drink or snack at the bar. Sign up for
The Friendship Test Workshop
(see registration below) or try out one of the engagement activities available, including tonight’s
Conversation Station: The Kitchen Table
, where you can take a moment or two to connect with a stranger to reflect on the rewards and challenges of friendship.
*****
Join us at the Toronto Reference Library's Appel Salon
for
Friendships and other Complexities
with political theorist Roger Berkowitz in conversation with Sanjay Ruparelia.
This one is about the harder kind of connection: staying in relationships with people you disagree with. We'll consider friendship not as a private comfort but as political work; the daily, unglamorous business of talking with people whose views unsettle us and whose reasoning we may never fully understand. Expect to be asked what you're willing to hold open, and to talk it through with people who won't necessarily see it your way.
What can Hannah Arendt's friendships — including with people whose politics she found troubling — teach us about sustaining democracy today? If our current political crisis is, at its root, a crisis of friendship, what has eroded our capacity to stay in dialogue across difference? And in an age of mass loneliness and ideological certainty, what would it mean to treat friendship, rather than consensus or moral purity, as the foundation of democratic life?
Berkowitz is founder and academic director of the Hannah Arendt Center for Politics and Humanities at Bard College. In A World We Share: Hannah Arendt and the Power of Friendship in a Broken World, he rethinks politics through Arendt's own life — a Jewish woman who escaped Nazi Germany, lived as an exile in Paris and then New York, and became a bold critic of popular ideas after World War II. People who knew her said she had a special talent for making friends. Berkowitz argues that a politics built solely on being right becomes cruel, coercive and ultimately anti-political.
Come ready to disagree agreeably.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this event’s guests:
Roger Berkowitz
Sanjay Ruparelia
Read more:
World We Share : Hannah Arendt and the Power of Friendship in A Broken World
***
Sign up for The Friendship Test Workshop
|
5:30 - 6:30 pm
The Kitchen Table |
5:30–6:30 pm & 8:00 – 9:00 pm
Grab a seat and dig into the questions we rarely ask out loud: How has your definition of friendship changed? Can you stay close to someone you disagree with? What makes a friendship last? Inspired by Berkowitz's argument that friendship — not agreement — is the glue of a healthy society, this café is a space to reflect on your own circle with the strangers sitting next to you.
Connect IRL
is not your average series of events, workshops and activities, but a real chance to connect with other Torontonians in meaningful and sometimes unexpected ways. Through conversation stations meant to spark one-on-one conversations, or hands-on engagement activities and workshops before the featured event, participants can explore the value of connection and community.

learning circle

transform, organize and visualize data with spreadsheet tools like Excel
query data from a relational database using SQL
improve data presentations using business intelligence tools like Tableau

title: Archaeoastronomy: Stonehenge and All That
location: Yorkville
description:
Join us at the Yorkville Library for an Archaeoastronomy Lecture. Archaeoastronomy
is the interdisciplinary study of how people in the past have understood the phenomena in the sky, how they used these phenomena, and what role the sky played in their cultures.  Today, astronomy is considered to mean the scientific study of the universe, but it  continues to connect, in so many  other intriguing ways, with every aspect of cultures, including myth, religion, and the arts.

title: Autumn Watercolour Workshop
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Celebrate the beauty of autumn with this beginner-friendly watercolour workshop!
Explore the transparency and fluidity of watercolour while capturing the beauty of fall foliage. Bring your own favourite leaves or choose from samples provided by the facilitator, and learn techniques for colour application, blending and harmonizing. Beginners welcome. All materials are included.

About Linda Borris
Linda is a Toronto-based artist, specializing in watercolour painting techniques. She focuses on her interests in botanical studies and constantly strives to discover interesting ways to portray her work. Linda’s painting compositions depict her particular attention to detail. Her art generally consists of bright, bold colours and forms. Mostly working with florals, Linda occasionally completes a fun landscape. Her paintings’ subject matter are usually taken from her own photography images. Linda loves to share her enjoyment in the lively and vibrant world of botanical essences. Her art can be seen in both group exhibits and separate venues.
 
She is a member of the Beach Guild of Fine Art and former member of Botanical Artists of Canada.
 
Also visit Linda’s work on Instagram: @watercolourslinda

title: Botanical Printed Notebook and Prints
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for a fun-filled afternoon of creating a customized notebook and prints!
Using the process of linocut, you’ll create a custom printed Japanese notebook and 4 fine art prints. From designing your image, through to carving and printing, our instructor will demonstrate linocut techniques and provide individual guidance. By the end of the workshop, you’ll leave with 1 unique botanical-themed notebook, 4 original prints and new printmaking skills. Beginners welcome.
 
You can create anything, so please bring photos, sketches, and designs for reference and inspiration. Your image needs to measure 4×6 inches. If you’re stuck for ideas, pressed leaves will be available.
 
Making art can be messy, please wear old clothes or an apron. Materials included.
 
Each student will receive:
 


1 Japanese notebook
1 block of soft cut lino
4 sheets of toned art paper
black printmaking ink


Saturday, October 24, 1 to 4 p.m.
Public $80, TBG Members $70 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Alan Li
Artist and conservationist Alan Li uses pencils, ink and paint to document the wonders of the natural world. Alan’s mission is to build connections to nature through arts-based education. Since 2015, he has been partnering with non-profit environmental organizations to teach nature-focused art programs and workshops.
 
Alan was responsible for the successful launch of the Toronto Nature Sketch program in 2018, teaching all of the art lessons during that inaugural year. Nature Sketch is an initiative of Canadian artist Robert Bateman and the Bateman Foundation.
 
In 2019, Alan was a speaker at the annual Ravine Symposium at Toronto Botanical Garden. In his presentation, he shared stories behind ravine inspired artwork created by himself and a small brigade of volunteer artists. Funds raised through the sale of the artwork were donated to ravine conservation initiatives at the garden.
 
Alan currently teaches Field Sketching, Nature Drawing and Linocut Printmaking at Toronto Botanical Garden and the High Park Nature Centre.

title: The Friends of the Arthur Conan Doyle Collection: 2026 Cameron Hollyer Memorial Lecture
location: Toronto Reference Library, Beeton Hall, Ground floor
description:
The Sultan and the Detective: Sherlock Holmes’ Curious Adventures in the Ottoman Empire
Historical fact: the last great Ottoman sultan, Abdülhamid II, fell asleep each night to the adventures of Sherlock Holmes, read aloud to him by a palace attendant. This unlikely obsession is the starting point for Andrew Finkel's novel
The Adventure of the Second Wife.
In this talk, Finkel explores how the world of Arthur Conan Doyle intersected with the late Ottoman Empire, and what this reveals about storytelling, translation, and the unexpected ways stories travel across languages, cultures, and empires to take on meanings the author never intended.
Andrew Finkel is a journalist and author who has reported from Turkey for major international outlets including
The Times, The Economist, TIME, CNN,
and
The New York Times
. He co-founded Platform24 (P24), an Istanbul-based NGO that supports independent journalism and freedom of expression, and is the author of
Turkey: What Everyone Needs to Know
.

title: Water Marbling Bookmarks Workshop
location: Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Immerse yourself in the mesmerizing world of water marbling — an ancient technique of floating pigments on water and transferring them onto paper to create intricate, fluid designs.

Practiced for centuries across the Islamic world, particularly in regions such as Türkiye, Iran, and the Indian subcontinent, water marbling has been used to adorn calligraphy, manuscripts, and decorative papers. In this introductory workshop, you will explore its rich history and cultural significance while mastering traditional tools and methods to produce a variety of classic patterns. Guided step-by-step, you will create between five and eight unique marbled bookmarks to take home — each a one-of-a-kind reflection of colour, movement, and your own creative expression.

Featuring vintage gear and a powerhouse rhythm section, Future Now is a manifestation of Blurton’s 40+ years in the Canadian music scene (Change Of Heart, C’mon, Public Animal).


The seasonally appropriate Ace of Wands brings gothic-glam aesthetics and dreamy fuzz, alongside rural Quebec quintet Tonnerre’s bluesy invocation of nature and what lies beyond. Starting the night is tween brothers Lego Money: a beacon of hope for Gen Alpha everywhere.


Inspired by this next wave of young musicians, Wavelength is delighted to announce the implementation of Pay What You Can youth pricing! Audience members 25 and under can set their own ticket price at Wavelength shows: 25 tickets will be available online and 25 tickets will be available at the door, arrive by 7:30 to claim your spot.


Get your pointer and your pinky finger ready for this multi-generational line-up of rockers!


Poster by Jadyn Klassen

title: Paradise Opening Night Reception
location: Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre
description:
In the multimedia exhibit, Paradise , which includes sculpture, print, and video, Japanese Canadian artists and childhood friends Emma Nishimura and Mitchell Akiyama grapple with their family histories of internment. Please join us at our opening reception for a chance to take in this meaningful show and to meet the artists! Light refreshments will be served.

title: Computers for Beginners
location: York Woods, Enhanced Learning Center
description:
Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse
A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this first session you will:
Observe and practice how to operate a mouse effectively
Understand various mouse pointers and cursors
Review basic keyboard functions
Use the mouse for basic Windows functions
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a computer mouse at a basic level and will be able to go online for additional practice.
Prerequisites: No computer experience required.
Format: Hands-on with demonstrations
Computers for Beginners 2: Use the Keyboard
A class on basic keyboard functions for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this second session you will:
Familiarize yourself through practice with the most essential keyboard functions (alphabet, number and symbol keys)
Practice proper keyboarding posture
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a keyboard at a beginner level and know how to go online for additional practice.
Prerequisites: Computer for Beginners 1 or basic mouse skills
Format: Hands-on with demonstrations
Computers for Beginners 3: Use Windows
A class on essential basic Windows skills for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this third session you will:
Become familiar with the Windows (10) operating system
Practice using common Windows features: File Explorer, Desktop, Taskbar, Windows, Applications
Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to create and organize files in the Windows environment.
Prerequisites: Computer for Beginners 1 & 2 or basic mouse and keyboarding skills
Format: Hands-on with demonstrations
Computers for Beginners 4: Use the Internet
An introductory class on the Internet for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fourth session you will:
Understand how to read a web site address
Practice using web addresses
Search for information using a search engine
Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches.
Prerequisites: Computer for Beginners 1 & 2 or basic mouse and keyboarding skills
Format: Hands-on with demonstrations
Computers for Beginners 5: Use Google Search and Maps
A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fifth session you will:
Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites
Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel.
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use more advanced search engine features and use Google Maps at a basic level.
Prerequisites: Computers for Beginners 1 & 2 or basic mouse, keyboarding and internet skills
Format: Hands-on with demonstrations
Computers for Beginners 6: Use Gmail
Learn to use Gmail, Google’s free web-based email service.
In this sixth session you will:
Practice basic email functions: send, read, reply, forward, delete email, and attach files
Review how spam and junk mail work
Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to use email.
Instructions on how to set up and manage your own free Gmail account are included in the handout.
Prerequisites: Basic keyboarding and mouse skills required.
Format: Hands-on with demonstrations

The Overlords appeared suddenly over every city—intellectually, technologically, and militarily superior to humankind. Benevolent, they made few demands: unify earth, eliminate poverty, and end war. With little rebellion, humankind agreed, and a golden age began.

As civilization approaches the crossroads, will the Overlords spell the end for humankind . . . or the beginning?

title: Book Club
location: Long Branch, Program Room
description:
Come join the readers at Long Branch each month. We share opinions and thoughts of the books selected. For the Month of October take a look at "Children of the Moon" by Anthony DeSa.
From critically-acclaimed author Anthony De Sa, a raw and compelling story of love, war and the differences that both divide and unite us. In the wispy grasslands of Tanzania in the 1950s, a Maasai woman gives birth to a miracle. The other villagers see the baby as a curse. The baby--a daughter, named Kibo--has skin as white as bone, and from her first moments on earth, she is forced to claim her life in spite of the violence she incites. As she grows, Kibo sheds her identity to become Liloe, and then Po, continuously trying to adjust herself so that she can fit into the world around her. Further south, in Portuguese-controlled Mozambique, a young boy, Ezequiel, has been adopted by two missionaries. Zeca, too, struggles with a lack of acceptance. Not recognized by his Portuguese father's community, or by his Makonde mother's tribe, Zeca lives his life on the borders of both worlds. And when civil war erupts in Mozambique, Zeca must choose what--and who--he is willing to leave behind
No Registration Required. Drop in.
All Welcome

title: The Lede: A Live Editorial Meeting Experience
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
TPL and the Canadian Journalism Foundation present a special Media Literacy week event!
Three journalists. One front page. Only one story leads.
The Lede pulls back the curtain on a process most people never see: how editors weigh impact, timeliness, public interest and audience relevance under pressure, in real time.
Three journalists from The Globe and Mail, Canada's national newspaper, deputy head of investigations Robyn Doolittle, politics and economy editor Ryan MacDonald and senior visuals editor Solana Cain, will each pitch the story they believe deserves the lead position in tomorrow's news. Editor-in-chief David Walmsley will question their assumptions, challenge their reasoning and make the final call, live, in front of the audience.
The audience does not just watch. Before Walmsley announces his decision, they vote on which story should lead, then see how their judgment compares with his.
Join us for a chance to understand not just what the news is, but how it gets made, and to walk away a sharper, more critical reader of it.
About this event’s guests:
David Walmsley
is
The Globe and Mail
’s editor-in-chief and the current president of the World Editors Forum. He is the co-creator of World News Day, a global day of education involving more than 1,000 publishers across 100 countries explaining the role of journalism and how it can make the world a better place. Under his editorship, The Globe has won the annual Canadian Michener Award for meritorious public service journalism five times and has dominated the annual National Newspaper Awards.
Robyn Doolittle
is the deputy head of investigations at
The Globe and Mail
. Doolittle came to
The Globe
in 2014 to join the investigative unit. After a decade on the i-Team, she spent time in the Report on Business covering corporate law. She has investigated political and business corruption, a series of shootings and arsons targeting Canadian waste giant GFL, the Hockey Canada scandal, gender inequities in the workforce and Canada’s broken freedom of information system as part of the Secret Canada project. Her two books, “Had It Coming – What’s Fair In The Age of #MeToo?,” and “Crazy Town: The Rob Ford Story,” were both national bestsellers.
Ryan MacDonald
is the editor of politics and economy at
The Globe and Mail
, leading a talented team of reporters covering the intersection of business and economic policy, including energy, finance, trade and fiscal matters. Since joining
The Globe
in 2007, MacDonald has held multiple editorial positions and was notably part of the team that won the 2022 CJF Climate Solutions Reporting Award for its narrative-shifting stories on how to re-engineer Canada’s economy to adapt to and capitalize on climate change. Prior to joining
The Globe
, MacDonald served as the national editor at the
Ottawa Citizen
.
Solana Cain
is a senior visuals editor at
The Globe and Mail
, Canada’s national newspaper. She joined
The Globe
through the 2019 summer program, quickly distinguishing herself as a perceptive and composed photo editor. In 2020, Cain helped establish Room Up Front, a mentorship initiative supporting BIPOC photojournalists. The program received a special citation at the 2023 National Newspaper Awards for its significant contribution to Canadian journalism. A dedicated mentor and educator, she actively advises emerging photographers and lectures at Toronto Metropolitan University, Sheridan College, and Loyalist College.

title: Get Things Done with AI: Build Your Own Productivity System
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
What if your to-do list could check in on you, notice what's been stuck for weeks, and offer to help instead of just sitting there?
In this class, you'll explore a personal productivity system built around an AI agent and a weekly-review practice. See how the agent loads goals, counts what actually got done, flags the items that keep slipping, and drafts next week's plan. It can support without cheerleading, asking "Why has this been stuck for three weeks? Here are your options." You'll try it yourself with a practice set of goals, and leave with the plain-text templates and a clearer map of how an AI might support you, ready to build your own system at home.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.

title: Marlon James: The Disappearers
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
TPL presents Booker Prize-winning author Marlon James in conversation with Kamal Al-Solaylee at the Toronto Reference Library's Appel Salon.
In his triumphant return to the Jamaica of his Booker Prize-winning
A Brief History of Seven Killings
, Marlon James delivers
The Disappearers
, an epic, unflinching novel about survival in the aftermath of violence. Written with the language-rich, urgent style that has made James one of the most acclaimed novelists working today, this is a story of men forced to make impossible compromises to survive a society that demands their erasure.
At once a detective story and a searing sociocultural history,
The Disappearers
plunges into the tragic, ongoing consequences of violent homophobia, rendering its characters' inner lives with the vivid imagery, sharp dialogue, and unrelenting energy that have defined James's celebrated body of work.
Join one of the most acclaimed novelists of his generation, in conversation with Kamal Al-Solaylee, for an evening exploring rage, resilience, and the price of queer solidarity in a world built to deny it.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

title: Financial Workshops for Seniors
location: Queen/Saulter
description:
Presented by John Stapleton from Open Policy Ontario, learn more about government programs, benefits and eligibility criteria for seniors. These sessions are designed for seniors with low income and those who advise them.
Thursday Oct 1: What Do Seniors Get?
Learn about benefits for older adults living in Ontario, including Canada Pension Plan (CPP), Old Age Security (OAS), Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS), and Guaranteed Annual Income Supplement (GAINS).
Thursday Oct 15: Understanding the Personal Income Tax System.
What is a taxable income and how can tax credits, deductions, entitlements and exemptions help to reduce taxable income.
Thursday Oct 29: Protecting Your Retirement Income.
Learn how to reduce claw backs to GIS and GAINS payments if receiving additional income from employment, a private pension, or a Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP).
Thursday Nov 12: Coming to Canada and Leaving Canada.
Learn about eligible benefits for those that resided in Canada for fewer than 40 years between the ages of 18 and 65, or for those planning on emigrating from Canada after retiring.
Thursday Nov 26: Tax Credits and Benefits for Seniors and People with Disabilities.
Learn about other tax credits and benefits for seniors, people with disabilities, and caregivers, including the disability tax credit, the Canada caregiver credit, and the home accessibility tax credit.
Registration not required. Drop-in welcome.

title: The Grim History of the Death Penalty in Canada
location: Pape/Danforth, Second floor program room
description:
Death by hanging was a grim reality within the Canadian criminal justice system until its abolition in 1976. But what did capital punishment look like in Canada? In this session, author Lorna Poplak will present the history of the death penalty in Canada, with a focus on the inconsistent application of the death sentence, the treatment of women, wrongful conviction, the difficult journey toward abolition, and the last two hangings at Toronto’s notorious Don Jail.

title: Jesse Wente: Tough Lies
location: North York Central Library, Concourse Event Space
description:
Award-winning author Jesse Wente shares his highly-anticipated new book exploring how we can heal from colonialism.
In Tough Lies, Wente explores his own healing path and how it informs what he sees as necessary for reconciliation between Nations, asking us to consider several pressing questions.
What does healing from colonialism look like for First Nations? What about non-Indigenous people? What are the barriers to this healing, and what can we do to move past them?
Through a lens of healing and anti-colonial thought, Wente examines his reaction to incidents that have hit close to home, chronicling his personal journey and what it has taught him about the present and future of reconciliation in Canada.
Jesse Wente speaks with professor Kim Anderson about Tough Lies and the path for healing between Nations.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this event’s guests:

Kim Anderson

title: Magnifica Humanitas: Choosing Humanity in the AI Revolution
location: Ontario
description:
— A Symposium on Putting Pope Leo’s “AI Encyclical” into Practice 







October 30-31, 2026 (Fri/Sat), 10:30am – 5:00pm 



Father Madden Hall (in Carr Hall, 100 St. Joseph St) 



Free admission / Lunch included: Register now 



How do we maintain our humanity and agency in a world that increasingly revolves around AI? 



From workplaces to social media feeds, from breakthroughs in healthcare research to that question you Googled last night, AI seems to be permeating every aspect of our lives. But as the ways we think, work, live, and act are being rapidly transformed, how do we protect and nurture those parts of our humanity that matter most—our dignity, our agency, our creativity and moral commitments? 



Join us as we discern our stakes in the current AI revolution through the lens of Magnifica Humanitas, Pope Leo’s “AI encyclical.” Through two days of panels, discussions, and workshops, we will explore how the Pope uses Catholic social teaching to engage with the structural realities of AI, and consider our own practical responses to his call to prioritise human dignity over unrestricted AI development. 



By asking practical questions about AI in light of Magnifica Humanitas, this symposium will help us engage critically and faithfully with changing technologies in our own lives, work, and service to the world. Whether you are new to the conversation and wanting to learn more or are already confronting pressing issues around AI, we welcome you to join us in this timely dialogue on navigating the emerging AI frontier. 



__________ 



Magnifica Humanitas Online Reading Group 



Monday evenings (7-8pm) from Sep. 14-Oct. 19 



Free Registration Here 



Are you interested in Pope Leo’s “AI encyclical,” but daunted by the thought of reading it alone? Have you been tempted to ask ChatGPT for a summary? Join us instead for this virtual reading group and explore the encyclical in conversation with others. Over 6 weekly sessions, Dr. Ren Ito will facilitate discussions of each chapter of Magnifica Humanitas. Participants will build an understanding of the encyclical’s key arguments, and will learn to engage with current issues of new technology through the lens of Catholic social teaching. 



Participants will also have the opportunity to present reflections on and takeaways from the encyclical during a session of our October 30-31 Magnifica Humanitas symposium.

title: 🇨🇦Japanese and English Language Exchange  (Page for everyone)
description:
Toronto Japanese English Exchange (TJEX.ca)
～English description below～

イベント参加費として、日本人の方(日本で生まれ育ち、現在英語を勉強している方)は2、日本人以外の方(日本語を勉強している方)は5頂いております。

皆さんから頂いたお金は、こちらのサイトの維持費や将来のランゲージエクスチェンジ施設利用料やソーシャルイベント等のために使われます。ご理解の程、よろしくお願いいたします。

予約受付開始：土曜日5:00PM

予約取消締切：土曜日14:00PM(当日)

予約受付締切：土曜日15:00PM(当日)

スケジュール

5.15 PM - 5:30PM - チェックイン、グループ分け

5:30 PM - 6:15PM - 日本語の時間［または英語の時間］

6:15PM - 7:00 PM - 英語の時間［または日本語の時間］

【イベント内容】

Language Exchangeへようこそ！このグループでは、皆さんのレベルに応じて、3〜4名のグループにわかれ、同じ席になった人たちで各45分間、それぞれ英語と日本語でフリートークを行なっていただきます。決まったディスカッショントピックなどはございませんので、気軽に質問をしながらそれぞれのセッションを楽しんでいただければと思います。

開催場所：Atrium フードコート

TJEXのサインボードを持ったオーガナイザーにお声がけください。(もしサインがなかったり、わからなければメッセージをお願いします！)

予約規約（⚠️重要）

・当日の不参加、もしくは15分以上の遅刻、また予約取消締切後の変更は原則不参加(No-Show)とみなします。不参加(No-show)が3回になりますと会員登録が抹消され、退会となりますのでご注意ください。

・イベントに遅れそうな場合は必ずオーガナイザーまでメッセージをお願いします。イベント開始時間にいるメンバーでグループを組み直すこともあるので、連絡なしで到着された場合はイベントに参加できない可能性もあります。原則、30分以上遅れての参加はご遠慮いただいております。あらかじめご了承ください。

キャンセル待ち

・満席の場合、”キャンセル待ち”リスト(waiting-list)にご登録いただくことが可能です。“参加予定”リスト（going-list)中に空席が発生した場合は、”キャンセル待ち”への登録が早かった方を優先に、オーガナイザーが”参加予定”へ移動しますので、当日の参加状況の変更がないかご自身でご確認ください。

※ご注意※

・空席ができた際は、自動的に”キャンセル待ち”より”参加予定”へ変更されます。この時にMeetupよりお知らせがあるかはわかりません。

・システムにより自動的に”参加予定”とされ、それに気づかずに参加しなかった場合でも、不参加とみなされますのでご了承ください。

Instagramアカウント @tjex.ca

最新情報やミートアップの様子を掲載しています。

ぜひこちらもフォローお願いします！

***Although our group is a non-profit organization, we collect $ 5 per English Speaker for every event. All the proceeds are used to run this website and for social events***

*Canadian English speakers must be Native or Fluent in English in order to participate*

RSVP:
RSVP open: 5:00 PM

RSVP cancel deadline: Saturday, 2:00 PM (day of the event)

RSVP close: Saturday, 3:00 PM (day of the event)

Day of Event:
5:15 PM - 5:30 PM - Check-in and Group placement

5:30 PM - 6:15 PM - Japanese conversation

6:15 PM - 7:00 PM - English conversation

Event Description:
This is an in-person language exchange! Members are placed into groups of three or four based on their language level. Each 45 minute session consists of friendly casual conversation, and/or informal study.

Optional Dinner :
After the Language event, we usually go for Dinner. Dinner is optional, you may or may not join the Dinner, it depends on you.
However, Dinner is only for Participants that joined on the day of the event.

Event Location:
Atrium Food Court

The food court is directly connected to the Dundas subway station. Leave the subway station and walk west along Dundas Street.

At the intersection of Bay Street and Dundas Street, you will find an entrance. Proceed down the escalator.

The food court is on the basement floor. Please talk to the organizer with the signboard showing TJEX. (If you can’t find them, please send a message to the organizer.)

⚠️RSVP & Late Policy:
If you are unable to join on the day of the event, please change your status from 'going-list' to 'not going-list'. Failure to Not show up will result in 1 No -Show. Also, in case of arriving 15 mins late to the event will result in 1 No-Show.

Members are removed from the group after 3 No-Shows.

Waiting List:
Members can join the waiting-list even if an event is full. When a spot becomes available, we will move you to the going-list.

Going List:
Only Members on the going-list can participate on the day of the event.

@tjex.ca

Feel free to follow us!

title: Jennifer Botterill & Cassie Campbell-Pascall: Game Changers
location: Toronto Reference Library, Appel Salon, Second Floor
description:
Trailblazing hockey players Jennifer Botterill and Cassie Campbell-Pascall share their new memoirs.
Botterill broke barriers as the youngest player on Team Canada at the first Olympics for women’s ice hockey, while Campbell-Pascall set records as the longest-serving captain in Canadian hockey history—and the first of any gender to lead the country to two Olympic gold medals.
Since their Hall of Fame playing careers, both have remained at the very top their game as sought-after broadcasters and advocates for athletes. Now, in their memoirs Why Not You and Just a Girl, these two titans of hockey invite us into their worlds like never before.
Jennifer Botterill and Cassie Campbell-Pascall speak with sportscaster Ailish Forfar about their new memoirs, taking a look back on their decorated hockey careers and toward a brighter future for all who play the game.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

title: Bring Your Problem: Can AI Help?
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
Do you have a recurring problem you think AI might help with? A thing you keep doing by hand that feels like it should be easier? Bring it. If you don't have one, come help your neighbours with theirs.
In this interactive class, you'll learn a simple seven-step way to think about problems: what's annoying you, what you've tried, what AI could actually do, and where it would fail. We'll gather real problems from the room, sort them into groups, and map out what's worth solving with AI, and what's better solved without it. We'll also talk honestly about what an AI fix costs: your money, your time, and sometimes your private information. The problems AI could help with most are often the most personal, and the most personal ones are worth the most care.
Registration is required and will start October 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.

Meet the Resident:
Sarah Zanchetta (she/they) is a queer textile artist and educator whose practice dives into the loss of connection and knowledge of poisonous plants in North America. Zanchetta uses textiles, texts, and hosts community workshops to create intimate works and spaces where we can unfold our curiosities, care and anxieties about what grows beside our feet. She holds a Master of Visual Studies from the University of Toronto (2023) and a BFA from OCAD University (2018).

title: Culture and Technology Book Club : Killed by a Traffic Engineer
location: North York Central Library, in the elearning lab (2nd floor)
description:
The Culture and Technology Book club brings readers together every two months to discuss new and classic texts that raise important questions about the way technology transforms our cultural and political lives.
This meeting we'll discuss:
Killed by A Traffic Engineer
(also available as an audiobook)
Civil Engineering professor Wes Marshal takes a hard look at how traffic engineering standards in North America have shaped our streets for the worse. He examines some of the dubious and unscientific assumptions central to traffic engineering such as their fixation on speed. Marshal asks what it might look like to build transportation infrastructure with a more holistic understanding of people's needs.
Register for this program to receive the discussion questions a week in advance of the meeting.

title: 🇨🇦Japanese and English Language Exchange  (Page for everyone)
description:
Toronto Japanese English Exchange (TJEX.ca)
～English description below～

イベント参加費として、日本人の方(日本で生まれ育ち、現在英語を勉強している方)は2、日本人以外の方(日本語を勉強している方)は5頂いております。

皆さんから頂いたお金は、こちらのサイトの維持費や将来のランゲージエクスチェンジ施設利用料やソーシャルイベント等のために使われます。ご理解の程、よろしくお願いいたします。

予約受付開始：土曜日5:00PM

予約取消締切：土曜日14:00PM(当日)

予約受付締切：土曜日15:00PM(当日)

スケジュール

5.15 PM - 5:30PM - チェックイン、グループ分け

5:30 PM - 6:15PM - 日本語の時間［または英語の時間］

6:15PM - 7:00 PM - 英語の時間［または日本語の時間］

【イベント内容】

Language Exchangeへようこそ！このグループでは、皆さんのレベルに応じて、3〜4名のグループにわかれ、同じ席になった人たちで各45分間、それぞれ英語と日本語でフリートークを行なっていただきます。決まったディスカッショントピックなどはございませんので、気軽に質問をしながらそれぞれのセッションを楽しんでいただければと思います。

開催場所：Atrium フードコート

TJEXのサインボードを持ったオーガナイザーにお声がけください。(もしサインがなかったり、わからなければメッセージをお願いします！)

予約規約（⚠️重要）

・当日の不参加、もしくは15分以上の遅刻、また予約取消締切後の変更は原則不参加(No-Show)とみなします。不参加(No-show)が3回になりますと会員登録が抹消され、退会となりますのでご注意ください。

・イベントに遅れそうな場合は必ずオーガナイザーまでメッセージをお願いします。イベント開始時間にいるメンバーでグループを組み直すこともあるので、連絡なしで到着された場合はイベントに参加できない可能性もあります。原則、30分以上遅れての参加はご遠慮いただいております。あらかじめご了承ください。

キャンセル待ち

・満席の場合、”キャンセル待ち”リスト(waiting-list)にご登録いただくことが可能です。“参加予定”リスト（going-list)中に空席が発生した場合は、”キャンセル待ち”への登録が早かった方を優先に、オーガナイザーが”参加予定”へ移動しますので、当日の参加状況の変更がないかご自身でご確認ください。

※ご注意※

・空席ができた際は、自動的に”キャンセル待ち”より”参加予定”へ変更されます。この時にMeetupよりお知らせがあるかはわかりません。

・システムにより自動的に”参加予定”とされ、それに気づかずに参加しなかった場合でも、不参加とみなされますのでご了承ください。

Instagramアカウント @tjex.ca

最新情報やミートアップの様子を掲載しています。

ぜひこちらもフォローお願いします！

***Although our group is a non-profit organization, we collect $ 5 per English Speaker for every event. All the proceeds are used to run this website and for social events***

*Canadian English speakers must be Native or Fluent in English in order to participate*

RSVP:
RSVP open: 5:00 PM

RSVP cancel deadline: Saturday, 2:00 PM (day of the event)

RSVP close: Saturday, 3:00 PM (day of the event)

Day of Event:
5:15 PM - 5:30 PM - Check-in and Group placement

5:30 PM - 6:15 PM - Japanese conversation

6:15 PM - 7:00 PM - English conversation

Event Description:
This is an in-person language exchange! Members are placed into groups of three or four based on their language level. Each 45 minute session consists of friendly casual conversation, and/or informal study.

Optional Dinner :
After the Language event, we usually go for Dinner. Dinner is optional, you may or may not join the Dinner, it depends on you.
However, Dinner is only for Participants that joined on the day of the event.

Event Location:
Atrium Food Court

The food court is directly connected to the Dundas subway station. Leave the subway station and walk west along Dundas Street.

At the intersection of Bay Street and Dundas Street, you will find an entrance. Proceed down the escalator.

The food court is on the basement floor. Please talk to the organizer with the signboard showing TJEX. (If you can’t find them, please send a message to the organizer.)

⚠️RSVP & Late Policy:
If you are unable to join on the day of the event, please change your status from 'going-list' to 'not going-list'. Failure to Not show up will result in 1 No -Show. Also, in case of arriving 15 mins late to the event will result in 1 No-Show.

Members are removed from the group after 3 No-Shows.

Waiting List:
Members can join the waiting-list even if an event is full. When a spot becomes available, we will move you to the going-list.

Going List:
Only Members on the going-list can participate on the day of the event.

Group Instagram -
@tjex.ca

Feel free to follow us!

title: Immersion Festival
location: Betty Oliphant Theatre, 404 Jarvis St, Toronto, ON
description: Join us for a celebration of Canadian cultural life for audiences and a sought-after performance and networking opportunity for renowned and aspiring artists, with three distinct stage performances, twelve workshops, a dance education roundtable, and community gatherings. Performances and workshops are open to all! Enjoy The Vanguard Presentation includes commissioned works by Katlyn Addison and Tanya Charles, Travis Knights and Divine Brown, and Nubian Néné. The National Presentation features Ebnflōh Dance Company, Lua Shayenne Dance Company, and N.A.P.P.Y. Dance, while the Next Gen showcase highlights emerging Black youth artists. Our workshops for youth, beginners, and professionals are led by Kwasi Obeng-Adjei, Reequal Smith, Natasha Powell, and Isaac Gasangwa, exploring diverse Black and diasporic movement practices. Three gathering events bring together presenters, artists, and academics to connect, exchange ideas, and celebrate Black dance across Canada.

title: Changing the Narrative: Toronto’s Indigenous – Settler History
location: Toronto Reference Library, 1st Floor, Beeton Hall
description:
Learn more about Toronto's multifaceted Indigenous history, which has often been ignored or minimized due to the telling of the region's history only from settler perspectives. Join us for a panel discussion about a public history project that worked with five local First Nations to create a more accurate and inclusive story of the region's past, and is transforming the way settlement of 19th century Ontario is represented at The Village at Black Creek (formerly Black Creek Pioneer Village).
Changing the Narrative: Reconnecting Settler and Indigenous Histories at Black Creek Pioneer Village was a collaborative project of York University historians, The Village at Black Creek, Jumblies Theatre, and the Mississaugas of the Credit, Chippewas of Rama, Six Nations of the Grand River, Chippewas of Georgina Island, and Mississaugas of Scugog Island First Nations.
This panel discussion will share research highlights, reflect on the process of collaboration, and explore how the project is expanding and enriching storytelling at one of the region’s prime living history museums.
The project’s findings have also been published in
Where Histories Meet: Indigenous and Settler Encounters in the Toronto Area
, by Victoria Freeman. The book explores this history from multiple perspectives in an accessible and richly illustrated format and includes excerpts from interviews with twenty Indigenous elders and knowledge keepers. It has been nominated for a
2026 City of Toronto Book Award
.
Panel members include:
Victoria      Freeman
, historical researcher and author of
Where Histories Meet:      Indigenous and Settler Encounters in the Toronto Area
.
Jennifer      Bonnell
, professor in the Department of History at York University and the      lead of the Changing the Narrative Project.
Allison      White
, curator at The Village at Black Creek (Toronto and Region      Conservation Authority).
Darin      Wybenga
, heritage interpreter for the Mississaugas of the Credit First      Nation, and member of the Research Committee for the Changing the      Narrative project.
Lauri      Hoeg
, Anishinaabe artist and cultural advisor from the Chippewas of      Georgina Island First Nation, and member of the Research Committee for the      Changing the Narrative project.
The panel discussion will last approximately 60 minutes, followed by a Q&A with audience members. No registration required.

title: Hank Idsinga: The High Road
location: North York Central Library, Concourse Event Space, North York Central Library (5120 Yonge St), Lower Level
description:
TPL presents retired homicide detective and author Hank Idsinga in conversation with Wendy Gillis at the North York Central Library's Concourse Event Space.
In his bestselling memoir
The High Road: Confessions of a Homicide Cop
, Idsinga takes readers behind the crime scene tape and into the mean streets of Toronto's most notorious murders. Teaming up with partners including future police chief Mark Saunders, Idsinga built a reputation for excellent recall and sharp instinct, finding motive and method faster than most. As the public face of that investigation, Idsinga remained strong and compassionate before the cameras, even as the police force faced fierce criticism over its handling of the case.
How do homicide detectives carry the weight of the cases they never solve? What does real accountability within policing actually look like, and why does it matter? And what can three decades on the front lines of Toronto's worst crimes teach us about justice, institutional trust, and the human cost of violence?
Join veteran crime reporter Wendy Gillis in conversation with Hank Idsinga for a gripping, candid evening inside the world of Canada's most storied homicide unit.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

title: ABCD Reads Body Language by Meg Howrey
description:
A Book Club, Downtown (ABCD)
ABCD Reads ***[Body Language](https://tpl.bibliocommons.com/v2/record/S234C4801989)*** by Meg Howrey.
([RESULTS](https://opavote.com/results/6325601387675648) of the poll for this event.)

**:: ABOUT THE BOOK ::**
"Sloane, a former actress now working as a therapist, is determined to find a meaningful way through menopause, away from marketing schemes, possibly with the aid of psychedelics. Her sister Laurel is managing her own growing rage and restlessness while engaging in work at an environmental non-profit and raising teenagers. Nanette, the youngest, has answered a long-delayed religious calling and is living as a Novice in a convent. All three lives will be further disrupted when Sloane receives a call summoning her to their mother’s house, Laurel discovers possible evidence of her husband’s infidelity, and Nanette finds herself in the middle of a media frenzy after a spontaneous act of public prayer.
Soon, all three are reunited under their mother’s roof, and no one can seem to agree about anything beyond the Barbara has dementia, as did her mother and sister before her. Will it be an opportunity for the closed door of their very private mother’s inner life to crack open? A lesson in care; a shared responsibility that will be the making of this family, divided by large age gaps, parental divorce, and temperament? Or will a stunning revelation upend not only their mother’s remaining time, but divide the sisters permanently?
With razor-sharp prose and undeniable humor, acclaimed author Meg Howrey brings an American family in the midst of a painful crisis to unforgettable life, interrogating memory and emotional inheritance, the right of a woman’s autonomy, and the indelible bonds even the most disparate of sisters can share." (from [Goodreads](https://www.goodreads.com/en/book/show/244709885-body-language))

"Howrey is a reliably beautiful stylist, and her slyly funny prose and blade-sharp insights into human behavior really should put her in the same conversation as writers like Ann Patchett and Barbara Kingsolver. Though this novel hits some familiar beats, Howrey manages to haul in plenty of shimmering pearls on the perils and joys of womanhood—whatever that means.
A comfort meal of a novel: poignant and prismatic." (from [Kirkus](https://www.kirkusreviews.com/book-reviews/meg-howrey/body-language-4/))

**:: ABOUT THE EVENT ::**
You are welcome to arrive 30 minutes before the event and stay 30 minutes or longer afterward to connect with other attendees outside the book talk.

Please ensure you have read the book before attending (though finishing any book is not a barrier to participating, as long as you don't mind spoilers).

First-time attendees can join for free. If the event is full, we maintain an unofficial waitlist. Please send [Michael](https://www.meetup.com/members/55295192/) a direct message for more information, in either case.

We request a $3 contribution from regular attendees to help cover our monthly meetup costs.

**:: ABOUT OUR NEXT BOOK ::**
At the end of each event, we will ask for nominees for our next book. If you have a good one in mind, please ensure it is between 200-400 pages long, available from the Toronto Public Library, and counts as contemporary literary fiction (though these are not hard and fast rules). When enough nominees are collected, Michael will send the members a direct message with a link where you can vote.

title: Financial Workshops for Seniors
location: Queen/Saulter
description:
Presented by John Stapleton from Open Policy Ontario, learn more about government programs, benefits and eligibility criteria for seniors. These sessions are designed for seniors with low income and those who advise them.
Thursday Oct 1: What Do Seniors Get?
Learn about benefits for older adults living in Ontario, including Canada Pension Plan (CPP), Old Age Security (OAS), Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS), and Guaranteed Annual Income Supplement (GAINS).
Thursday Oct 15: Understanding the Personal Income Tax System.
What is a taxable income and how can tax credits, deductions, entitlements and exemptions help to reduce taxable income.
Thursday Oct 29: Protecting Your Retirement Income.
Learn how to reduce claw backs to GIS and GAINS payments if receiving additional income from employment, a private pension, or a Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP).
Thursday Nov 12: Coming to Canada and Leaving Canada.
Learn about eligible benefits for those that resided in Canada for fewer than 40 years between the ages of 18 and 65, or for those planning on emigrating from Canada after retiring.
Thursday Nov 26: Tax Credits and Benefits for Seniors and People with Disabilities.
Learn about other tax credits and benefits for seniors, people with disabilities, and caregivers, including the disability tax credit, the Canada caregiver credit, and the home accessibility tax credit.
Registration not required. Drop-in welcome.

title: Imagining a Turtle Named Franklin by Brenda Clark
location: Lillian H. Smith, Lower Level- Auditorium
description:
Photo credit: Lee Higginson.
Join the Osborne Collection of Early Children's Books for our 19th Annual Sybille Pantazzi Memorial Lecture: Imagining a Turtle Named Franklin by Brenda Clark.
Award winning picture book illustrator, Brenda Clark is the original illustrator of the beloved Franklin the Turtle book series, by author Paulette Bourgeois. In this lecture, she will share how she became an artist and how Franklin was created. Brenda’s illustrations have played a key role in Franklin’s worldwide popularity, leading to the inspiration of the animated TV series, merchandise, spin-off books, a children’s garden on Toronto Island and a Canadian postage stamp. She will walk us through the process of designing and painting the art and explain how it takes some amazing teamwork to meet the challenges of Franklin’s success.
For the past 40 years, Brenda Clark has delighted children as the illustrator of the hugely successful Franklin the Turtle children’s book series. Over 70 million Franklin books have been sold in more than 30 languages worldwide, making it the single most successful picture book series in the history of Canadian publishing. In 2011, the archives of Brenda Clark were donated to the Osborne Collection of Early Children’s Books, and recognized by the Canadian Cultural Property Export Review Board as cultural property for its “Outstanding Significance and National Importance”. In 2014, Brenda was named a Member of the Order of Canada. She lives in Port Hope, Ontario.
Book signings will take place before the lecture from 5:00-6:00 pm on the 4th floor in the Osborne Collection.

title: Ghost Stories of Toronto: Séances & The World Wars
description:
Séances were all the rage a century ago. Having begun to fall out of fashion in the early 1900s, they experienced a resurgence after the deadly years of the First World War and the Spanish Flu as people held out hope they could still communicate with their lost loved ones. In the third lecture of this series by author Adam Bunch, we'll explore the history of séances during those turbulent times, from those who truly believed in their power, to the fraudsters who preyed on a grieving city, to the prime minister who took advice from the spirits of the dead.
About this event's guest:
Adam Bunch
Read More:
The Toronto Book of Love
The Toronto Book of the Dead
About this series:
You can learn a lot about Toronto through its ghost stories. Whether you believe in the supernatural or not, the tales we tell about spirits and spectres illuminate the true history of the city. They're often tied to dramatic stories of death and disaster, to fascinating historic sites, and to pivotal moments that helped shape our communities. In this series of talks by author Adam Bunch, we'll explore Toronto's past through tales of ghosts, séances and hauntings. Whether it's phantom horses from the War of 1812, the strange prime minister who believed in the occult, or the ghost who was arrested by the Toronto Police Morality Squad, these supernatural stories have a lot to teach us about the history of the place we call home.

Meet the Resident:
Sarah Zanchetta (she/they) is a queer textile artist and educator whose practice dives into the loss of connection and knowledge of poisonous plants in North America. Zanchetta uses textiles, texts, and hosts community workshops to create intimate works and spaces where we can unfold our curiosities, care and anxieties about what grows beside our feet. She holds a Master of Visual Studies from the University of Toronto (2023) and a BFA from OCAD University (2018).

title: Toronto's Ravines: Nature and History at Your Doorstep
location: Richview, Room A, 2nd Floor
description:
Toronto's ravine landscapes are not just a sanctuary for wildlife; they also protect the city against flooding and allow us to enjoy nature at our doorsteps. This presentation by the Toronto Field Naturalists shares how the ravines are changing over time; how they are responding to numerous pressures and how you can explore and help protect them.
Presenter Bio:
Ellen Schwartzel is a former president of the Toronto Field Naturalists, and she enjoys leading walks through Toronto's ravines.  Ellen's career in environmental policy included 23 years with the Environmental Commissioner of Ontario. She was Ontario's Deputy Environmental Commissioner for four years, until retiring in 2018.  Ellen’s academic training was in Botany, and she received her BSc and MSc at the University of Toronto.
This program is part of TPL's
Our Fragile Planet
program series, supported by Friends of Toronto Public Library, South Chapter.​

title: Dystopia Nonfiction Book Club: AI Snake Oil
location: Toronto Reference Library, Lower Level, Room B1
description:
Join us each month to discuss issues in politics and society, and explore how powerful forces are exploiting our world and dystopian imaginings are becoming present-day realities.
November’s book is
AI Snake Oil: What Artificial Intelligence Can Do, What It Can't, and How to Tell the Difference
by computer scientists Arvind Narayanan & Sayash Kapoor. Copies of the book are available in print,
eBook
&
eAudiobook
format. Book club attendees are encouraged to read the book in advance of the meeting.
"Confused about AI and worried about what it means for your future and the future of the world? You're not alone. AI is everywhere—and few things are surrounded by so much hype, misinformation, and misunderstanding. In AI Snake Oil, computer scientists Arvind Narayanan and Sayash Kapoor cut through the confusion to give you an essential understanding of how AI works, why it often doesn't, where it might be useful or harmful, and when you should suspect that companies are using AI hype to sell AI snake oil—products that don't work, and probably never will. While acknowledging the potential of some AI, such as ChatGPT, AI Snake Oil uncovers rampant misleading claims about the capabilities of AI and describes the serious harms AI is already causing in how it's being built, marketed, and used in areas such as education, medicine, hiring, banking, insurance, and criminal justice. The book explains the crucial differences between types of AI, why organizations are falling for AI snake oil, why AI can't fix social media, why AI isn't an existential risk, and why we should be far more worried about what people will do with AI than about anything AI will do on its own. The book also warns of the dangers of a world where AI continues to be controlled by largely unaccountable big tech companies. By revealing AI's limits and real risks, AI Snake Oil will help you make better decisions about whether and how to use AI at work and home."
In addition, we will be discussing Chapter 1 of
Atlas of AI: Power, Politics, and the Planetary Costs of Artificial Intelligence
by artificial intelligence and media researcher Kate Crawford.
Drop in. No registration required.

This Month: Birds in Winter
Winter is a harsh season, yet many birds stay in Toronto and survive. Why don’t they all fly south? How do they stay warm and find food and shelter? Which birds stay and which ones migrate? Learn about migrant birds and their incredible journeys, visiting birds who come to the city from their boreal and Arctic homes, and our resident birds who spend the long, cold winter months here.

description:

In this hands-on class, you'll explore a job-hunting dashboard built with AI: how it tracks applications, sets automatic alerts for postings that match you, and practices interviews with you through role-play. title: 2026 Duende International Flamenco Festival: Masterclasses
location: Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
This special series of masterclasses offers dancers a rare opportunity to learn with three extraordinary flamenco artists, Óscar de los Reyes, Carmen Talegona, and El Yiyo.

Each workshop offers participants a deeper understanding of the art form’s power, precision, musicality, and emotional truth. The three artists brings a distinct voice, lineage, and approach, guiding dancers toward greater technical clarity, expressive range, and connection to rhythm, structure, and cante. Together, these masterclasses create a rich encounter with flamenco as a living, evolving art form — one that honours tradition while continuing to move boldly into the future.

Open to intermediate, advanced, and professional-level dancers, the workshops offer an inspiring environment for growth, exchange, and artistic discovery.

title: Duende International Flamenco Festival: Flamenco and the World
location: Aga Khan Museum, Massey Hall, Nanji Family Foundation Auditorium
description:
Celebrate flamenco’s global transformation through cross-cultural exchange at the Aga Khan Museum’s 12th annual Duende International Flamenco Festival: Flamenco and the World.

From November 18 to 22, experience the vibrant evolution of flamenco — from its regional roots in Andalusia to a dynamic global art form shaped by cross-cultural exchange. This year’s lineup spans both traditional flamenco from Andalusia and innovative collaborations at the crossroads of qawwali and Persian muqam, tracing the art form’s evolution from its regional roots to a global practice.

title: Rachel Cusk: Life of M
location: Toronto Reference Library, Appel Salon, Second Floor
description:
Critically acclaimed author Rachel Cusk shares her irresistible new novel.
Life of M introduces us to movie star M, one of the most recognizable faces of our time, whose image has been ubiquitous since she was a child.
With such fame, her life has the appearance of freedom: people are instantly obliging, spaces are altered to accommodate her, time can be rearranged. M may live in the same places as real people. She may meet her friends or collect her children from school or walk her dogs as they do. But it seems the rules of reality have melted away.
Now, a writer has decided to pay close attention to M’s life in the hope of understanding who she really is. It is hard not to feel ugly next to M, hard not to feel insignificant. But what truths―about the very experience of living―might this proximity allow the writer to briefly capture?
Rachel Cusk speaks with Sheila Heti about Life of M, an astonishing new novel about fame, power, beauty, and truth
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

title: Farruquito: A Flamenco Dynasty
location: Nanji Family Foundation Auditorium, Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Part of the Aga Khan Museum’s 12th annual Duende International Flamenco Festival: Flamenco and the World, join us for a film screening that celebrates the legacy of Farruquito, one of the greatest flamenco dancers of this century.

Farruquito is celebrated as the finest flamenco dancer of his generation. He belongs to a legendary dynasty of bailaores (dancers). At only 20, he was already at the height of his success, captivating audiences around the globe from New York to Tokyo – with his extraordinary talent, yet the shadows of his family’s tumultuous history loomed large.

The film follows Farruquito’s journey through triumph and tragedy, focusing on a pivotal moment that changes everything — a tragic accident that leads to the death of a pedestrian and lands him in prison. This harrowing experience forces him to confront the demons of his past and the heavy burden of his family’s legacy.

title: The Ishizue Award Dinner 2026
location: Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre
description:
The JCCC Board of Directors is pleased to announce that the 8th Ishizue Award and accompanying dinner will be held on Thursday November 19 2026. The Ishizue Award acknowledges and expresses our appreciation and respect to members or friends who have made exceptional contributions to the Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre. The name Ishizue, meaning cornerstone or foundation, pays tribute to the 75 families who, at significant personal financial risk, guaranteed the original mortgage on the JCCC at 123 Wynford Drive in the early 1960’s. These families provided the foundation upon which the JCCC was built, and their support for the JCCC will forever be recognized as the cornerstone for who we are as a community. The recipients of this annual award are a very distinguished group of people who have each made significant life contributions to the Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre. They are: Ken Fukushima Harry Kawabe Akiko Maruoka David Ohashi (Post humous) Connie Sugiyama David Tsubouchi We cordially invite you to honour these distinguished award recipients at an intimate and elegant dinner on Thursday November 19th at 6:30pm at the Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre. Black tie optional. Tickets are $180 each (plus HST) . Maximum of 10 guests per table. To purchase tickets please order through the button below or in person at the JCCC, starting September 21, 2026, and ending November 9, 2026. Please contact Sharon Marubashi for any further information by email or phone (647-291-4751). Purchase Ticket (on Sale Sep 21) On behalf of all of the directors of the Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre, we look forward to spending a special evening of recognition and celebration together.

title: Qawwali Flamenco
location: Massey Hall, Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
From Pakistan to Andalusia, musical traditions have crossed paths, met, nourished one another, and blended so thoroughly that between the volcanic power and virtuosity of qawwali singing and the hypnotic lyricism of flamenco, distances fade and similarities naturally emerge.

Qawwali Flamenco marks the long-awaited return of the celebrated collaboration between Pakistani qawwali master Faiz Ali Faiz and flamenco guitar virtuoso Juan Gómez “Chicuelo.”

Following their acclaimed first collaboration a decade ago, Faiz and Gómez reunite to deepen a remarkable artistic dialogue. The first chapter of their Qawwali Flamenco journey explored the relationship between human beings and their beloved; this new creation turns toward the connection between humanity and the divine.

description:
Due to renovations the Bookclub will take place in Scadding Court Community Center in Room 4 (same building), participants will be responsible in sourcing copies of the monthly titles themselves as the branch will not be open to the public during this time. We apologize for the inconvenience!
Become a page-turner by joining the Between the Lines Book Club! Here, we embark on a new chapter with every read, diving into a world of endless possibilities. From gripping thrillers to heartwarming coming-of-age tales, or a sprinkle of fantasy adventures, there's something for everyone. Whether you're a die-hard fan of one genre or love mixing things up, you'll find a place here to discuss, share, and connect with fellow readers. Ready to explore different worlds and discover your next favorite book? Join us and let's turn the page together!
Friday September 18
: The Covenant of Water by Abraham Verghese
The Covenant of Water
by Abraham Verghese is a sweeping, richly detailed novel set in Kerala, India, that follows a family across generations as they live with a mysterious condition in which some family members have a fear of water. Beginning in the early 1900s, the story unfolds through the lives of several generations, connecting their personal struggles, relationships, and secrets in unexpected ways. Blending family history, love, loss, medicine, faith, and cultural traditions, the novel explores how the past shapes generations to come. Verghese brings the landscape and people of Kerala vividly to life, while weaving together themes of resilience, sacrifice, healing, and the complicated bonds of family. It is an immersive and emotional story that invites readers to become deeply invested in the lives of its characters and the mysteries that connect them.

title: Orhan Pamuk's The Museum of Innocence: Novel and Museum
location: Toronto Reference Library, Appel Salon, Second Floor
description:
Nobel Prize-winner Orhan Pamuk speaks about the creation of Istanbul's Museum of Innocence.
Renowned Turkish novelist and Nobel Prize-winner Orhan Pamuk joins celebrated museum and cultural planning leader, Gail Lord, for an extraordinary conversation about one of the most singular acts of imagination in contemporary literature and museology: the creation of Istanbul's Museum of Innocence.
Conceived in tandem with his acclaimed novel of the same name, Pamuk's museum houses the fictional world of his characters Kemal and Füsun in a real, physical space — a small house in Istanbul filled with everyday objects, each one tied to a moment in the novel. The result is a haunting blur between fiction and reality, where a love story lives on not only on the page, but in glass display cases, drawers, and rooms visitors can walk through.
How does one curate a museum for people who never existed? What does it mean to give physical form to memory, longing, and melancholy — the very textures of a novel? And what challenges arise when an author becomes a museum-maker, translating narrative into space, object, and atmosphere?
Orhan Pamuk sits down with Gail Lord, co-founder of Lord Cultural Resources and one of the world's leading museum planners, to discuss the twin creation of the novel and the museum, the ethereal act of turning fiction into physical experience, and what he hoped visitors would feel wandering through the rooms of a story. The conversation will also turn to Pamuk's evolving philosophy of museums — the ideas first laid out in his "Modest Manifesto for Museums" — exploring his belief in small, intimate institutions that honor individual and everyday stories over the grand, monumental narratives so often privileged by national museums.
The discussion will also look ahead to Pamuk's second museum project, currently in development, in which he continues to explore the relationship between storytelling, memory, and collected objects. Building on the foundations laid by the Museum of Innocence, this new endeavor promises to further test the boundaries between literature and lived space, offering fresh insight into how narrative can be translated into an immersive, tangible experience.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this event’s guests:
