title: Blackbird: In the Footsteps of Ziryab
location: Nanji Family Foundation Auditorium, Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Blackbird: In the Footsteps of Ziryab makes its world premiere as a bold new multidisciplinary performance celebrating the enduring connections between cultures through oral and artistic traditions. Led by Artistic Director Amir Amiri, the Amir Amiri Ensemble, featuring Óscar de los Reyes and Esperanza Soria, the performance brings together Canadian and Spanish Andalusian artists in a powerful artistic dialogue. Connected through centuries of migration, poetry, rhythm, and memory, the performance explores a shared cultural legacy while embracing new creative expression. The essentials of flamenco are all present: voice, complex rhythm, and dance.

This presentation ultimately asks how music travels through history, how cultures reshape one another, and how artists continue to carry ancient knowledge into contemporary life. The project seeks to illuminate the enduring connections between Persian and Andalusian artistic worlds, while creating a contemporary performance grounded in research, artistic integrity, and shared humanity.

title: Flamenco: Made in Canada presents Duende Al Nur
location: Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Duende al Nur , meaning “Duende toward the light,” is an immersive flamenco work where light, shadow and fire transform the dancing body.

Performed on a luminous plexiglass platform, the piece explores light as a sacred, living force rising from beneath the dancer. From darkness, the body is awakened by illumination. Breath becomes pulse, pulse becomes rhythm, and rhythm becomes flamenco. Through footwork, castanets, zills, breath and silence, Carmen Romero moves through a ritual journey of awakening and renewal. Rooted in the emotional power of duende and the Arabic resonance of nur, the work becomes a passage through memory, prayer, rhythm and transformation.

The work draws from flamenco’s emotional intensity, rhythmic complexity and theatrical power while opening the performance space to Arabic resonance, sacred illumination and immersive sound. Rather than presenting cultural influence literally, Duende al Nur approaches these elements as echoes, atmospheres and poetic points of connection.

title: Los Magníficos
location: Nanji Family Foundation Auditorium, Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
“Los Magníficos” is a once-in-a-lifetime encounter with the greatness of contemporary flamenco. Five outstanding artists come together in a unique performance where singing, dance, guitar, and piano reach their highest expression.

Sandra Carrasco, one of the most important voices of the moment, takes us to the very heart of flamenco. David de Arahal captivates audiences with his mastery of the guitar, while Andrés Barrios transforms the piano into pure emotion. Dancer “El Yiyo” embodies the power and intensity of flamenco, joined by Carmen “La Talegona,” whose artistry and magnetic stage presence bring elegance, strength, and depth to this extraordinary encounter.

Prepare for an intense and magnetic journey, where energy and sensitivity intertwine in an explosion of talent. “ Los Magníficos” is not just a performance; it’s a unique opportunity to witness the union of some of the finest artists of our time in a moment destined to remain forever in the memory of flamenco art.

What if your to-do list could check in on you, notice what's been stuck for weeks, and offer to help instead of just sitting there?
In this class, you'll explore a personal productivity system built around an AI agent and a weekly-review practice. See how the agent loads goals, counts what actually got done, flags the items that keep slipping, and drafts next week's plan. It can support without cheerleading, asking "Why has this been stuck for three weeks? Here are your options." You'll try it yourself with a practice set of goals, and leave with the plain-text templates and a clearer map of how an AI might support you, ready to build your own system at home.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.

title: Jeff Chang: Bruce Lee and the Making of Asian America
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
TPL presents award-winning author Jeff Chang in conversation with [HOST TBC] at the Toronto Reference Library's Appel Salon, celebrating what would have been Bruce Lee's birthday.
More than half a century after his death, Bruce Lee remains as towering a figure as ever, the man who popularized martial arts in the West, became a bridge between Eastern and Western culture, and was poised to conquer Hollywood when he died suddenly at age thirty-two. But in the decades since, his legend has eclipsed the man. Forgotten is the immigrant, the fighter, the seeker, the teacher, the father grappling with exile and belonging in a country that questioned his right to simply exist.
In his epic new cultural biography
Water Mirror Echo: Bruce Lee and the Making of Asian America
, acclaimed author Jeff Chang recovers the man behind the icon. Drawing on in-depth interviews with Lee's closest intimates, thousands of newly available personal documents, and dozens of rare photographs from the family archive, Chang traces Lee's remarkable journey: a charismatic child star turned delinquent teen fighter in Hong Kong, exiled alone to America, who transformed personal struggle into a philosophy of movement and being. Chang reveals how Lee's rise didn't just create a Hollywood legend, it helped birth something even more enduring: the very concept of Asian America.
Join Jeff Chang for a special evening honoring Bruce Lee's birthday, offering a stirringly human portrait of the icon, the immigrant, and the movement he unknowingly ignited.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

title: Wednesday Afternoon @ the Movies: One False Move
location: Weston, Program Room. Lower Level.
description:
Join us on Wednesday afternoon at the library for a screening of One False Move movie.
A small-town police chief conceals an explosive secret. A pair of ruthless drug dealers leave a bloody trail in their wake as they make their way from Los Angeles to Arkansas. And an enigmatic woman is caught in the middle. The way these desperate lives converge becomes a masterclass in slow-burn tension thanks to the nuanced direction of Carl Franklin, whose haunting debut feature travels a crooked road across America’s most fraught divisions—urban and rural, Black and white—while imbuing noir conventions with a wrenching emotional depth.
Rated R. 1hr 45mins.
English Subtitles for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing (SDH) when available.

title: Vibe Coding: Make Your Own Interactive Story with AI
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
What if you could write a story where the reader chooses what happens, like a branching adventure, a mystery, or a game, and have AI build it with you?
In this class, you'll learn "vibe-coding": using an AI coding assistant to build your own interactive story or simple game. You'll design the branches, describe the rules in plain language, test for the tricky edge cases (what if the player picks the weird option?), and end up with a single file you can share with anyone. Just a story you want to tell. This is the playful sibling of the practical vibe-coding workshop.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.
Registration is required and will start October 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.

title: Financial Workshops for Seniors
location: Queen/Saulter
description:
Presented by John Stapleton from Open Policy Ontario, learn more about government programs, benefits and eligibility criteria for seniors. These sessions are designed for seniors with low income and those who advise them.
Thursday Oct 1: What Do Seniors Get?
Learn about benefits for older adults living in Ontario, including Canada Pension Plan (CPP), Old Age Security (OAS), Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS), and Guaranteed Annual Income Supplement (GAINS).
Thursday Oct 15: Understanding the Personal Income Tax System.
What is a taxable income and how can tax credits, deductions, entitlements and exemptions help to reduce taxable income.
Thursday Oct 29: Protecting Your Retirement Income.
Learn how to reduce claw backs to GIS and GAINS payments if receiving additional income from employment, a private pension, or a Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP).
Thursday Nov 12: Coming to Canada and Leaving Canada.
Learn about eligible benefits for those that resided in Canada for fewer than 40 years between the ages of 18 and 65, or for those planning on emigrating from Canada after retiring.
Thursday Nov 26: Tax Credits and Benefits for Seniors and People with Disabilities.
Learn about other tax credits and benefits for seniors, people with disabilities, and caregivers, including the disability tax credit, the Canada caregiver credit, and the home accessibility tax credit.
Registration not required. Drop-in welcome.

title: How Pleasant to Know Mr. Lear
location: Mount Pleasant, Basement program room
description:
Dennis Duffy, Professor Emeritus, Department of English, University of Toronto, discusses the genius of Edward Lear as a painter and poet, the great joiner of oil painting and printed nonsense.
Lear was a singular eccentric in his bespoke but loosely-fitting suits and his runcible hat, he created work placing him among the finest of graphic cartoonists and satirists. This presentation explores that jagged world that he made up for himself, in order to preserve his own complex selfhood.

title: Artists in the Library: Origami Lotus Flowers
location: Thorncliffe, Program Room
description:
This is a six-part workshop series that creates a space for exploring belonging and not belonging through conversation and hands-on art-making. Guided by reflective questions, participants engage in practices such as origami with washi, drawing, dyeing, and writing, using the lotus as a shared symbol of transformation and resilience across cultures. The workshops foster an inclusive, supportive environment, particularly for those who feel marginalized or disconnected. The series culminates in a collaborative public floral installation in the library, sharing participants’ work with the wider community.
Led by artists "Being~inbetween"
The workshops are open to youth, ages 13-17, and require no prior artistic experience.

title: Data Analytics Essentials Learning Circle
location: Palmerston, Meeting Room
description:
Interested in learning about data analytics? Let's take a free online course together in a welcoming space!
A
learning circle
is a study group, guided by library staff, for people who want to take a free online course together in a supportive and welcoming environment.
Organizations all over the world recognize the value of analytics. Together, we'll learn about the essential tools used in this field.
In this 12-week learning circle, we will work through the Data Analytics Essentials course from Cisco Networking Academy. We will explore the fundamental tools of a data analyst, including how to:
transform, organize and visualize data with spreadsheet tools like Excel
query data from a relational database using SQL
improve data presentations using business intelligence tools like Tableau
We will meet weekly,
in-person,

earn a digital badge

title: Python Essentials 1 and 2 Learning Circle
location: York Woods
description:
Learn Python and build your programming skills in a supportive group. This learning circle will meet on Tuesday afternoons from September 22 to December 8, 2-3:30pm. Learning circles are study groups guided by staff for people who want to take a free online course together in a welcoming space. Learners meet weekly and work together through the course materials. Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions.
Learners who successfully complete both courses will earn a digital badge and certificate of completion.
Python Essentials 1
is the first in a 2-course series that teaches computer programming skills including how to design, develop, and improve computer programs using the Python programming language. The course covers essential programming topics such as data types, variables, control flow, functions, and exceptions.
Python Essentials 2
is the second in a 2-course series that will prepare you for the PCAP – Certified Associate in Python Programming certification exam at Pearson VUE. This intermediate-level course covers advanced aspects of Python programming, including modules, packages, exceptions, file processing and object-oriented programming (OOP).

title: Run Your One-Person Business with AI
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
When you're the whole company, the admin never ends: emails, scheduling, proposals, follow-ups. What if you could design a system to handle the busywork?
In this class, you'll learn to design an administrative system for a one-person business with AI as your assistant: intake pipelines, email drafting, client communication, and scheduling. Learn to map work into four piles: what's rules-based, what AI drafts, what needs your judgment, and what should never be automated. You'll build reusable templates and leave with a clearer plan for how AI could help your business.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.

title: The Delicious and Surprising History of The Dining Room
location: Hillcrest - Closed, Auditorium
description:
John Ota presents​ and discusses his book,
The Dining Room : Exploring the Design of Twelve Iconic Rooms in Search of the Perfect Dining Experience.​
​(Random House, 2026).
Explore the stories behind twelve iconic dining rooms in homes around the world—from a Japanese samurai house to Claude Monet's brilliant yellow dining room to Frida Kahlo's Casa Azul to Jackie Kennedy’s White House—and travel through time in pursuit of the ultimate design.​
The Dining Room is an englightening and joyous celebration of history, culture and the art of dning. Presenter John Ota's charming observations of the surprising impact of dining rooms on our lives and the cherised moments we share within them will delight armchair travellers, history fanatics and interior design enthusiasts alike.

title: Data Analytics Essentials Online Learning Circle
description:
Interested in learning about data analytics? Let's take a free online course together in a welcoming space!
A
learning circle
is a study group, guided by library staff, for people who want to take a free online course together in a supportive and welcoming environment.
Organizations all over the world recognize the value of analytics. Together, we'll learn about the essential tools used in this field.
In this 12-week learning circle, we will work through the Data Analytics Essentials course from Cisco Networking Academy. We will explore the fundamental tools of a data analyst, including how to:
transform, organize and visualize data with spreadsheet tools like Excel
query data from a relational database using SQL
improve data presentations using business intelligence tools like Tableau
We will meet online every Thursday evening,
September 24 - December 10, 6-7:30 PM
(12 sessions).
Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend sessions on a weekly basis.
Learners who complete the course will be able to:
earn a digital badge
download a certificate of completion

title: Art of Darkness: Edgar Allan Poe's Life & Work
location: Toronto Reference Library, Appel Salon, Second Floor
description:
Professor Emily Ogden shares her intimate inquiry into the shadowy life and compelling work of the definitive author of the macabre.
Since Edgar Allan Poe’s mysterious death in 1849, his stories and poems have captivated millions of readers around the world. Nearly two centuries later, why do we continue to descend into the darkness of his imagination—and of the genres, from horror to crime, that he pioneered?
In Darkness Becomes Bright, Ogden plumbs the darkness within Poe and enters it alongside him. She interweaves stories from his mysterious and tragic life with those of his most famous readers and translators, showing us how Poe’s vision echoes across the generations, allowing us to make peace with our own flawed humanity.
Emily Ogden speaks with author and critic Naben Ruthnum about the brief life and immortal art of Edgar Allan Poe.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this event’s guests:
Emily Ogden
Naben Ruthnum

title: Vietnam & Cambodia with Angkor Wat! Ancient Kingdoms of Southeast Asia!!
description:
20s 30s Toronto Social & Activities
A Meetup trip in December . . . what can be a better gift for the holidays?! Join our travelers group on a captivating 14-day journey through the heart of Southeast Asia as we explore the vibrant cultures and breathtaking landscapes of Vietnam & Cambodia (Dec 04-18, 2026)

As with all our tailor-made Meetup trips, our expert guides will lead us off the beaten path to uncover the authentic charm of each destination, while comfortable accommodations and delicious local cuisine ensure a truly immersive travel experience. Embark on an unforgettable journey through the vibrant cities and breathtaking landscapes of Vietnam, finishing with the wonders of Cambodia.

We begin in Hanoi, where history and culture come alive, then sail the emerald waters of Halong Bay. Step back in time among the imperial treasures of Hue, wander the lantern-lit streets of charming Hoi An, and feel the dynamic energy of Ho Chi Minh City. We conclude your adventure at the awe-inspiring temples of Siem Reap, home to the legendary Angkor Wat.

TRIP HIGHLIGHTS:

* **Hanoi**; explore Ho Chi Minh sites, Temple of Literature, Old Quarter cyclo ride & water puppet show
* Visit rural **craft villages**: conical hat & incense making, home-hosted lunch, village walk

* **Hue**: Perfume River boat ride, Thien Mu Pagoda, Khai Dinh’s Tomb & Imperial Citadel
* Scenic **Hai Van Pass train** to Danang; explore Dragon Bridge, Cham Museum, Marble Mountain
* **Hoi An Ancient Town** (UNESCO), visit tailor shops, pottery village & organic farm with cooking class
* **Ho Chi Minh City & Cu Chi Tunnels**; War Remnants Museum, Reunification Palace & Ben Thanh Market
* **Mekong Delta cruise**: coconut workshops, sampan ride, orchards & lunch in riverside village
* **Siem Reap**: dinner with Apsara dance, Angkor temples (Ta Prohm, Bayon, Angkor Wat)

title: AI for Us: Shaping AI in Toronto
location: North York Central Library, Room 2/3
description:
Toronto is one of the biggest AI cities in the world. But what do the people here actually think about it and how do we want to shape its development and use?
A panel of experts, who know AI from very different angles, united for an open conversation about what AI is doing to this city, and what we want it to do instead. We'll talk about:
The human beings behind the machines: what drives the people who build AI, and what worries them.
Work, money, and meaning: what happens to jobs, creativity, and value when AI lands here.
Who gets to shape it and who's left out (both are our neighbours).
The stories we tell: how art, media, news, and everyday talk shape what we expect, fear, and hope for.
No pitches, no boosterism. Just an honest conversation about the ideas and stories shaping AI in this city, and what we want it to become.
Featuring:
Jerrold McGrath
, Cultural Programmer and Theorist, In the Meantime
Joseph Wilson
, Anthropologist & Author of Humans of AI: Understanding the Humans Behind the Machines
Owais Lightwala

Meet the Resident:
Sarah Zanchetta (she/they) is a queer textile artist and educator whose practice dives into the loss of connection and knowledge of poisonous plants in North America. Zanchetta uses textiles, texts, and hosts community workshops to create intimate works and spaces where we can unfold our curiosities, care and anxieties about what grows beside our feet. She holds a Master of Visual Studies from the University of Toronto (2023) and a BFA from OCAD University (2018).

title: Shedding light on the dark side of the Universe
location: Malvern, Community Room
description:
The standard model of cosmology tells us that the Universe is mostly made up of ‘Dark Matter’, with normal matter contributing only about 15% of the total budget. However, direct detections have not yielded any results about the nature of this mysterious dark matter, leaving us with only indirect means of inferring its existence and distribution. I will try to answer tantalizing questions about its nature, and how it may have helped shape the Universe.
This talk will be given by Dr. Pratika Dayal from the Dunlap Institute for Astronomy & Astrophysics at the University of Toronto.
No registration is required, but registering will make sure you receive a reminder.

title: Our Annual Giving Back! Sandwich Making for Charity
description:
These Boots Are Made for Hiking
**Meetup Location**: **Toronto Sailing and Canoe Club**
**1391 Lakeshore Blvd, M6K 3C1**

Hold the date!
Join us for champagne and our sandwich making event for two downtown shelters. Food for shelters are at a long time low, and rely on donations including ours at this time of year. Last year we made 750 sandwiches!
**Show your holiday spirit and lets see if we can beat our record!**
Here's how it works:
You bring a loaf of bread or two ( you can also bring pitas to stuff and wraps) and filling for the sandwiches. We have different stations for sandwich makers, wrappers, labelers and packers.
**It's chaotic, and a lot of [fun...and](http://fun...and/) there is champagne involved.**
Here are just a few suggestions for sandwiches -
peanut butter and jam
egg salad - cook and peel your eggs before you arrive
tuna or salmon salad
ham and cheese
cheese
chick pea
Cucumber, salad, and cream cheese
Salmon, rice and cucumber
See you soon! xoxox

title: Thailand Sea Side Discovery: Bangkok, Phuket and Krabi Island
description:
20s 30s Toronto Social & Activities
Join us for an unforgettable 10-day Meetup adventure through Thailand, blending culture, temples, islands, beaches, and relaxed free time. This trip is a true Meetup - designed for those who want to travel the world and explore exotic destinations like Thailand, but don’t want to do it alone. We are traveling as a group, while still enjoying flexibility and optional experiences.
This journey blends the energy of Bangkok, the tropical beauty of Phuket, and the laid-back charm of Krabi, creating the perfect balance of culture, nature, and downtime. We will explore iconic temples, cruise through stunning islands, relax on white-sand beaches, and enjoy free time to wander, shop, or simply slow down and soak it all in.

**Trip Highlights**
• Bangkok City & Temple Tour
• Optional Ayutthaya Day Trip
• Flight to Phuket included
• Phi Phi Islands Tour
• Big Buddha Visit
• Scenic drive from Phuket to Krabi
• 4 Island Hopping Tour with Picnic

**Who is this trip for**
✔ Solo travelers who don’t want to travel alone
✔ People who want structure without feeling rushed
✔ Travelers who enjoy a mix of sightseeing and free time
✔ Anyone who wants to experience Thailand with a fun, supportive group

This adventure is ideal for solo travelers, friends, couples and even families, who want the comfort of a group while keeping the experience fun and social.

The best way to see what it's like is to check the gallery with past pix from our previous trip: https://photos.app.goo.gl/qXfrs5zQp5rULNvb9

For a detailed Day By Day itinerary [Click Here](https://forms.gle/cQdqYw74gAYqphXX8) to fill out the form and receive information.

**Land Tour cost $2997 per person, double occupancy (we match roommates for those willing to share and save).**
**If you want your own room: Solo occupancy $3867**

**The only way to secure your spot for this meetup is a $325 deposit that is refundable up to 90 days before departure.**
**[Click here for secure deposit link](https://www.paypal.com/instantcommerce/checkout/4K9UHVSFEL8UA)**

When you make a deposit be sure to fill out this [ATTENDEE’S FORM](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScjUyrsruOGiQWnWgqn-hiNuIpheVNCkYkavtNyYNsAnn0tZA/viewform).
As mentioned, . . . the cost is $2997. This is for the "Land" portion only. **International airfare is not included.** This gives you the flexibility to have a flight with timing that works best for you. Or to use points/miles.
Ekaterina can also help arrange your airfare.
To contact her for more info, [CLICK HERE](https://www.meetup.com/messages/?new_convo=true&member_id=14363992) [to send her a message.](https://secure.meetup.com/messages/?new_convo=true&member_id=14363992)

**What is included in the cost:**
✔ Meet & greet upon arrival at the airport
✔ 3 Nights in Bangkok
✔ 3 Nights in Phuket
✔ 3 Nights in Krabi
✔ Accommodation with daily breakfast as mention
✔ Airfare from Bangkok to Phuket
✔Transfer services in private air-conditioned vehicle
✔English speaking guide throughout program
✔Entrance fees, other boat fees where applicable
✔ Meals as listed in the program
✔Bottled water on coach during transfer
✔ Airport arrival and departure transfers in Bangkok
✔ Airport arrival transfer in Phuket (one time together for the group)
✔ Airport departure transfers in Krabi
✔ Road transfer from Phuket to Krabi

**What is not included:**

* International Airfare
* Meals not mentioned in the itinerary
* Visa
* Early check-in and late check-out
* Tips, drinks, personal expenses and others
* Travel insurance

Want more info?
[Click Here to fill out our info request form](https://forms.gle/cQdqYw74gAYqphXX8)
OR
RSVP to the event with your email to receive additional info.
OR
[CLICK HERE to send me a message](https://secure.meetup.com/messages/?new_convo=true&member_id=14363992)
Whatever is easiest for you!

We do a Q & A Zoom once a month.

title: Everest Base Camp Yoga Trek: Discover the Land, People & Spirit of Nepal
description:
20s 30s Toronto Social & Activities
**This is definitely a bucket list type of trip. It embodies adventure and the romance of traveling to far off places. It is also tempered with safety and do-ability.**
The actual dates are Apr 10-26, 2027 and the trip is 17 days/16 nights.

We have done this adventure three times already, in 2021, 2023 and 2025, and everybody had a blast! [CLICK HERE to see attendee photos of the EBC trek](https://photos.app.goo.gl/jtHi3tTjVhYGjtc19)

WE HAVE MADE CHANGES BASED UPON EXPERIENCE.

1. **We are ADDING** Yoga and Meditation, and a local expert TO BE WITH US to guide in Buddhist practice and local culture.
2. **We are ADDING** two days while going up to better acclimatize.
3. **We are ADDING** a HELLICOPTER FLIGHT from our highest camp back to start point AND REMOVING two days going down by taking the flight.

To clarify. We are NOT going up to the top of Everest (29,000’)
We are going to Everest Base Camp at 17,600’
Our starting elevation will be in Lukla at 9,400’

You need to be of average or better fitness. If you can manage walking 3-6 hours a day, up and down a hill while carrying a light daypack, you will be OK! If you are very fit and work out and train, you will be at the front.

Professional guides to lead, and Yaks to carry our gear are included. And a Yak Herder too!!

All that is left for us to carry is our water, snacks and camera.

*But I don't have the needed gear?!*
Sleeping bag and parka, rated to -10C are provided and walking poles too!

*Does this include food?*
All meals on the trek potion are included.

*What is lodging like?*
We are sleeping in a series of "Tea Houses" along the route. You will have a bed in a shared room with roommate (from the group). Sorry, a solo room will not be available on this trip. We will pair up everybody.

*How dangerous is this? What if I get sick or hurt?*
This is NOT the summiting Everest with people dying from bad choices. We will be walking on an established, well used trail the entire time, and NOT on snow or ice. Stats from past years show that 30,000 people a year do the EBC Trek. With all that said, . . . **our trip INCLUDES emergency insurance.** We are also Certified Wilderness First Responders.
**Plain and simple, safety is our primary goal. We will have an experienced guide and porters, and we will be along the entire way.**

*How much does this cost?*
**Everest Base Camp Trip US$3750 - 17 Days, land only (airfare not included)**
For this trip we don’t offer single occupancy and we match you with a roommate if you don't have one.

*RSVP to this event shows your interest, but does not hold your space.*
*The only way to secure your spot for this trip is a US$250 deposit for the land portion:* ***[CLICK HERE FOR SECURE DEPOSIT LINK](https://www.paypal.com/instantcommerce/checkout/A3DBBZGZVRNL4)***
*Deposit is refundable up to 90 days before the departure (less PayPal fees).*

For more information fill out this form: [https://forms.gle/cQdqYw74gAYqphXX8](https://forms.gle/cQdqYw74gAYqphXX8)

Land Cost includes:

* Airport pick up and drop off 4 times
* 3 nights at Kathmandu hotel
* 13 nights Tea House accommodation during the trek.
* Kathmandu / Lukla Flights
* All entries, required permits and taxes
* Guide, Assistant guides and Porters
* Food and drinks during the trek
* Helicopter ride back from Gorakshep to Lukla
* Sim Card
* Sleeping bag, down jacket, hiking poles
* Welcome and Farewell dinner
* Sightseeing Tour in Kathmandu

This is the adventure of a lifetime!

It is done in a safe manner and includes lots with no surprises.
**To receive detailed itinerary, inclusions etc [CLICK HERE and fill out our google form.](https://forms.gle/cQdqYw74gAYqphXX8)**[ ](https://forms.gle/cQdqYw74gAYqphXX8)

AND/OR if you ***have questions?***
***[Message direct to Anna](https://secure.meetup.com/messages/?new_convo=true&member_id=131297062) (flights, itinerary, payments)***
***[Message Direct to Marc](https://secure.meetup.com/messages/?new_convo=true&member_id=273063881) (hiking information)***
AND/OR
***We do a Zoom Q & A (every other) Wed 6:00-7:30 PM***
***[CLICK HERE FOR THE Zoom Event](https://www.meetup.com/moretoexplore/events/296044209/)***
***[CLICK HERE for Google Form to get Reminder for the zoom](https://forms.gle/6Zs4GMhsN7ZD8ugW6)***

*NOTE: The "land portion" of this trip starts in Kathmandu on Apr 25 and ends on Mar 11. This event is longer than Meetup date range.*

As a meetup group we have gone to EBC, Kilimanjaro, Machu Picchu, Galapagos and other bucket list place. Come alone and leave with new lifelong friends.

title: Unforgettable Croatia! The Pearls of the Dalmatian Coast - Split, Dubrovnik..
description:
20s 30s Toronto Social & Activities
Join our Meetup group on this exciting tour of beautiful Croatia - a country blessed with both, transparent sapphire waters and glamourous old towns. A blissful vacation to a country full of beauty and history with an awesome group of active and fun people! Create lifelong friendships on our tours! *Come alone, leave with friends!*

From north to south, we will start with Croatia's charming capital, Zagreb. Visit the amazing Plitvice Lakes National Park, with its cascading waterfalls. Explore the former Roman citadel of Split with Diocletian's famous palace. Marvel at the UNESCO World Heritage city of Dubrovnik, boasting the largest and best preserved city walls in Europe. Check out the filming locations of Game of Thrones. Relax on Croatia's stunning Dalmatian coast, overlooking the crystal blue Adriatic Sea. Spend a couple of days on the sun drenched islands of Hvar and Korčula. Be our own boat crew for a day, while sailing to the famous Blue cave and 5 more islands.

For a detailed Day By Day itinerary:
**[Click Here](https://forms.gle/cQdqYw74gAYqphXX8)**[ to fill out our info request form](https://forms.gle/cQdqYw74gAYqphXX8)
